Stores — nested state, one signal per property

A store is read like a plain object and written only through its setter — by path, with produce, or with reconcile for fresh server data.

import { createEffect, createRoot } from "solid-js";
import { createStore, produce, reconcile } from "solid-js/store";

type Line = { sku: string; name: string; qty: number };
type Cart = { lines: Line[]; coupon: string | null };

const cart = createRoot(() => {
  const [state, setState] = createStore<Cart>({
    lines: [{ sku: "kb-01", name: "Keyboard", qty: 1 }],
    coupon: null,
  });
  // each effect re-runs only for the properties it read
  createEffect(() => console.log("first line qty:", state.lines[0]?.qty));
  createEffect(() => console.log("coupon:", state.coupon ?? "none"));
  createEffect(() => console.log("items:", state.lines.reduce((n, l) => n + l.qty, 0)));
  return { state, setState };
});

cart.setState("lines", 0, "qty", (q) => q + 1);            // path setter: one property
cart.setState("coupon", "SPRING10");
cart.setState(produce((draft) => { draft.lines.push({ sku: "ms-02", name: "Mouse", qty: 1 }); }));
const keyboard = cart.state.lines[0];
// fresh data from the server: reconcile diffs by key and keeps unchanged items' proxies
const fromServer = [{ sku: "kb-01", name: "Keyboard", qty: 2 }, { sku: "ms-02", name: "Mouse", qty: 3 }];
cart.setState("lines", reconcile(fromServer, { key: "sku" }));
console.log("same keyboard proxy:", cart.state.lines[0] === keyboard);
Result
first line qty: 1
coupon: none
items: 1
first line qty: 2
items: 2
coupon: SPRING10
items: 3
items: 5
same keyboard proxy: true

Resources — async data driven by a signal

createResource(source, fetcher) refetches whenever source() changes and exposes the state; <Suspense> and <ErrorBoundary> read it in JSX.

import { createEffect, createResource, createRoot, createSignal } from "solid-js";

type Product = { sku: string; name: string };
const catalog: Record<string, Product> = {
  "kb-01": { sku: "kb-01", name: "Keyboard" },
  "ms-02": { sku: "ms-02", name: "Mouse" },
};

// In the app: fetch(`/api/products/${sku}`); here an in-memory stand-in with one await of latency.
async function fetchProduct(sku: string): Promise<Product> {
  await Promise.resolve();
  const product = catalog[sku];
  if (!product) throw new Error(`no product ${sku}`);
  return product;
}

const page = createRoot(() => {
  const [sku, setSku] = createSignal("kb-01");
  const [product, { mutate }] = createResource(sku, fetchProduct);
  createEffect(() => {
    // check `error` first: reading an errored resource throws (to the nearest ErrorBoundary)
    if (product.error) console.log(`${product.state}: ${(product.error as Error).message}`);
    else console.log(`${product.state}: ${product()?.name ?? "…"}`);
  });
  return { setSku, mutate };
});

const settle = () => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 0));
await settle();
page.setSku("ms-02");                       // "refreshing" keeps showing the previous product
await settle();
page.mutate({ sku: "ms-02", name: "Mouse (renamed)" });   // set the value locally, e.g. an optimistic edit
page.setSku("xx-99");
await settle();
Result
pending: …
ready: Keyboard
refreshing: Keyboard
ready: Mouse
ready: Mouse (renamed)
refreshing: Mouse (renamed)
errored: no product xx-99

React → Solid

The JSX looks the same; the execution model does not.

ReactSolidThe trap
const [n, setN] = useState(0)const [n, setN] = createSignal(0)n is a function: {n()}, not {n}
useMemo(fn, deps)createMemo(fn)no dependency array — reads are tracked
useEffect(fn, deps)createEffect(fn), or on(deps, fn); onMount for onceno dependency array; only what the last run read is tracked
return cleanup from an effectonCleanup(cleanup)a value returned from createEffect's function is passed to its next run, not called
useRef for a DOM nodelet el!: HTMLInputElement + ref={el}assigned when the element is created; use it in onMount
useRef for a mutable valuea plain let in the component bodythe body runs once, so locals persist
useCallback, React.memonothingcomponents never re-run, so identities are already stable
useReducer / ImmercreateStore + producenever assign to the store directly; go through the setter
{items.map((i) => <Row key={i.id} />)}<For each={items}>{(i) => <Row item={i} />}</For>.map works but rebuilds every row on each change
{cond && <Panel />}, ternaries<Show when={cond()} fallback={…}>, <Switch>/<Match>&& and ternaries work in JSX; <Show> adds fallback, keyed and the narrowed-value callback
<Child {...props} />, destructured propsprops.x, splitProps, mergePropsdestructuring freezes the values
<Suspense> + use(promise)<Suspense> + createResourceread resource() inside the boundary
key={id} to reset a subtree<Show when={id()} keyed>without keyed the children stay and only the value updates
className, onChange on a text inputclass, onInputSolid's onChange is the native change event — it fires on blur

Traps React developers hit

Each one compiles, renders once correctly, and then silently stops updating.

  • Destructuring props (function Price({ cents })) or copying them to locals (const c = props.cents): read once, never updated. Use props.cents where it is needed.
  • Reading a signal in the component body (const label = count() > 0 ? …) instead of in JSX or a function: the body runs once. Make it const label = () => ….
  • Reading a signal after an await or inside setTimeout in an effect: it is not tracked — tracking only sees synchronous reads.
  • Returning a cleanup function from createEffect as in React: it is not called. Register teardown with onCleanup.
  • Prefer derivation — a function or createMemo — over an effect that writes another signal; effects are for the world outside Solid.
  • Keep computations under an owner (a component, or createRoot); one created after an await has none and is never disposed.
  • Group several writes in batch so dependents run once, with consistent values. Solid 1.x does not batch event handlers for you; only effects, onMount and store setters are batched automatically.
  • Solid has no virtual DOM: JSX compiles to real DOM creation plus one effect per dynamic expression, which is why the compiler (vite-plugin-solid) is required.

Styling — Design Tokens & Chakra UI

Decide a value once, name it by role, switch it per colour mode — as CSS custom properties, then with Chakra UI 3's system, style props and recipes.

Where a styling decision lives

One row per decision: the theme owns scale, roles and mode, and a component only picks reusable styles, one-offs and responsive values.

Tokens defined once, emitted as CSS variables

When several stacks (CSS, a charting library, email templates) must agree on the palette — one typed source, generated CSS.

const scale = {
  space: { 1: "0.25rem", 2: "0.5rem", 4: "1rem", 6: "1.5rem" },
  radius: { control: "6px", card: "12px" },
  text: { sm: "0.875rem", md: "1rem", lg: "1.125rem" },
} as const;

// Roles say what a colour is FOR; every scheme must give every role a value.
type Role = "surface" | "text" | "muted" | "accent" | "danger";
const schemes: Record<"light" | "dark", Record<Role, string>> = {
  light: { surface: "#ffffff", text: "#111827", muted: "#4b5563", accent: "#1d4ed8", danger: "#b91c1c" },
  dark: { surface: "#111827", text: "#f3f4f6", muted: "#9ca3af", accent: "#60a5fa", danger: "#f87171" },
};

const declare = (prefix: string, values: Record<string, string>) =>
  Object.entries(values).map(([name, value]) => `  --${prefix}-${name}: ${value};`);

function tokensCss(): string {
  return [
    ":root {",
    ...Object.entries(scale).flatMap(([group, values]) => declare(group, values)),
    ...declare("color", schemes.light),
    "}",
    ':root[data-theme="dark"] {',
    ...declare("color", schemes.dark),   // only roles change per scheme; the scale never does
    "}",
  ].join("\n");
}

console.log(tokensCss());

Typed references and per-instance variables

A typo in a token name should fail the build, and a per-item value (progress, a brand colour from the API) belongs in a custom property, not a generated class.

import type { CSSProperties } from "react";
import { renderToStaticMarkup } from "react-dom/server";

// Let `style` carry custom properties without a cast.
declare module "react" {
  interface CSSProperties {
    [property: `--${string}`]: string | number | undefined;
  }
}

type Role = "surface" | "text" | "muted" | "accent";
type Space = 1 | 2 | 4 | 6;
const color = (role: Role) => `var(--color-${role})`;
const space = (step: Space) => `var(--space-${step})`;

// The stylesheet draws the bar from the variable:
//   .fulfilment { background: linear-gradient(to right, var(--color-accent) var(--progress), transparent 0) }
function FulfilmentBar({ packed, total }: { packed: number; total: number }) {
  const style: CSSProperties = {
    "--progress": `${Math.round((packed / total) * 100)}%`,
    padding: space(2),
    color: color("muted"),     // color("primary") does not compile: not a Role
  };
  return <div className="fulfilment" style={style}>{packed} of {total} items packed</div>;
}

console.log(renderToStaticMarkup(<FulfilmentBar packed={3} total={4} />));
Result
<div class="fulfilment" style="--progress:75%;padding:var(--space-2);color:var(--color-muted)">3 of 4 items packed</div>

Resolve and apply the colour scheme

The user's choice beats the OS; apply it before first paint so nothing flashes, keep following the OS while the choice is "system", and set it on one element so every consumer follows.

import { JSDOM } from "jsdom";

type Preference = "light" | "dark" | "system";
type Scheme = "light" | "dark";
type OsDark = Pick<MediaQueryList, "matches" | "addEventListener">;

function readPreference(storage: Storage): Preference {
  try {
    const saved = storage.getItem("theme");
    return saved === "light" || saved === "dark" ? saved : "system";
  } catch {
    return "system";             // storage blocked: getItem throws SecurityError
  }
}

// Our tokens read data-theme; Chakra's _dark and Tailwind's class-based dark: read the
// class; form controls and scrollbars read color-scheme.
function applyScheme(root: HTMLElement, scheme: Scheme) {
  root.dataset.theme = scheme;
  root.classList.toggle("dark", scheme === "dark");
  root.classList.toggle("light", scheme === "light");
  root.style.setProperty("color-scheme", scheme);
}

function startScheme(root: HTMLElement, storage: Storage, osDark: OsDark) {
  const apply = () => {
    const preference = readPreference(storage);
    applyScheme(root, preference === "system" ? (osDark.matches ? "dark" : "light") : preference);
  };
  apply();
  osDark.addEventListener("change", apply);     // the OS switched while the page is open
}

const { window } = new JSDOM("<!doctype html><html></html>", { url: "https://shop.example/" });
const root = window.document.documentElement;
const osDark = Object.assign(new window.EventTarget(), { matches: false });   // a stand-in matchMedia
startScheme(root, window.localStorage, osDark);
console.log("saved none, OS light ->", root.className);
osDark.matches = true;
osDark.dispatchEvent(new window.Event("change"));
console.log("OS turns dark       ->", root.className, root.style.getPropertyValue("color-scheme"));
Result
saved none, OS light -> light
OS turns dark       -> dark dark
Setup
  1. Node.js 22.18 or later (it runs .mts files directly by stripping the types)
  2. npm i jsdom @types/jsdom (stands in for the page here)
  3. Save as main.mts and run node main.mts
  4. In the page: inline these functions in <head> as plain JavaScript (types removed), and call startScheme(document.documentElement, localStorage, matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)"))

Chakra: tokens, semantic tokens, the system

createSystem(defaultConfig, yours) keeps Chakra's tokens and component recipes and merges your brand on top; semantic tokens carry the light/dark switch.

import { createSystem, defaultConfig, defineConfig } from "@chakra-ui/react";

const v = (value: string) => ({ value });
// A role's value per mode, as references to palette tokens.
const byMode = (light: string, dark: string) =>
  ({ value: { base: `{colors.${light}}`, _dark: `{colors.${dark}}` } });

const config = defineConfig({
  theme: {
    tokens: {
      colors: {
        brand: { 100: v("#dbeafe"), 200: v("#bfdbfe"), 300: v("#93c5fd"), 400: v("#60a5fa"),
          500: v("#3b82f6"), 700: v("#1d4ed8"), 800: v("#1e40af"), 900: v("#1e3a8a") },
      },
      radii: { card: v("12px") },
    },
    semanticTokens: {
      colors: {
        surface: byMode("white", "gray.900"),
        // All eight keys a colorPalette needs: Button and Badge read six (not emphasized or
        // focusRing), and inputs, tabs, sliders and steps read those two.
        brand: {
          solid: byMode("brand.700", "brand.500"),
          contrast: byMode("white", "white"),
          fg: byMode("brand.700", "brand.300"),
          muted: byMode("brand.200", "brand.800"),
          subtle: byMode("brand.100", "brand.900"),
          emphasized: byMode("brand.300", "brand.700"),
          focusRing: byMode("brand.500", "brand.400"),
          border: byMode("brand.500", "brand.400"),
        },
      },
    },
  },
});
// In src/main.tsx: <ChakraProvider value={system}><App /></ChakraProvider>
export const system = createSystem(defaultConfig, config);

const hex = (reference: string) => system.token(reference.slice(1, -1));   // "{colors.white}" → "#FFFFFF"
for (const role of ["surface", "brand.solid", "brand.muted"]) {
  const { base, _dark } = system.tokens.getByName(`colors.${role}`)!.extensions.conditions!;
  console.log(`${role}: light ${hex(base)}, dark ${hex(_dark)}`);
}
Result
surface: light #FFFFFF, dark #18181b
brand.solid: light #1d4ed8, dark #3b82f6
brand.muted: light #bfdbfe, dark #1e40af
Setup
  1. A React app: npm create vite@latest shop -- --template react-ts, then npm i @chakra-ui/react @emotion/react
  2. tsconfig: "moduleResolution": "Bundler" (Vite's default, and what Chakra's install guide requires) — Chakra 3's type declarations do not resolve under nodenext
  3. In the app: save as src/theme.tsx without the last block, and wrap the app in <ChakraProvider value={system}> in src/main.tsx
  4. To run this file alone: save as main.tsx and run npx tsx main.tsx in a package with "type": "module", beside a tsconfig.json with "jsx": "react-jsx" and "moduleResolution": "Bundler"
  5. Optional: npx @chakra-ui/cli typegen ./src/theme.tsx so your own token and recipe names autocomplete and type-check

Chakra: style props on a real component

One-off layout goes in style props, each naming a token or role — never a hex value or a pixel length.

import { Badge, Box, Button, createSystem, defaultConfig, Flex, Heading, Stack, Text }
  from "@chakra-ui/react";

// The two theme tokens this card uses, from the card above.
const surface = { value: { base: "{colors.white}", _dark: "{colors.gray.900}" } };
const system = createSystem(defaultConfig, {
  theme: { tokens: { radii: { card: { value: "12px" } } }, semanticTokens: { colors: { surface } } },
});

type Order = { id: string; customer: string; total: string; late: boolean };

export function OrderCard({ order, onTrack }: { order: Order; onTrack: () => void }) {
  return (
    <Box as="article" bg="surface" borderWidth="1px" borderColor="border" rounded="card"
      p={{ base: "3", md: "5" }} _hover={{ shadow: "md" }}>
      <Flex justify="space-between" align="center" gap="3">
        <Stack gap="0.5">
          <Heading size="sm">Order #{order.id}</Heading>
          <Text color="fg.muted" textStyle="sm">{order.customer}</Text>
        </Stack>
        {order.late && <Badge colorPalette="red">Late</Badge>}
      </Flex>
      <Flex mt="4" justify="space-between" align="center">
        <Text fontWeight="semibold">{order.total}</Text>
        <Button size="sm" colorPalette="blue" onClick={onTrack}>Track</Button>
      </Flex>
    </Box>
  );
}

// What the article's style props become: tokens, and a mobile-first media query.
const cardCss = system.css({ bg: "surface", rounded: "card", p: { base: "3", md: "5" } });
console.log(JSON.stringify(cardCss, null, 2));
console.log("padding resolves to", system.token("spacing.3"), "then", system.token("spacing.5"));

Chakra: a recipe for a reusable style

When the same element recurs with a few named looks (an order-status badge), make the looks variants of one recipe instead of repeating style props.

import { chakra, defaultSystem, defineRecipe, type RecipeVariantProps } from "@chakra-ui/react";

const statusBadgeRecipe = defineRecipe({
  base: { display: "inline-flex", alignItems: "center", gap: "1", rounded: "full", fontWeight: "medium" },
  variants: {
    status: {
      placed: { bg: "gray.subtle", color: "gray.fg" },
      shipped: { bg: "blue.subtle", color: "blue.fg" },
      delivered: { bg: "green.subtle", color: "green.fg" },
      cancelled: { bg: "red.subtle", color: "red.fg", textDecoration: "line-through" },
    },
    size: {
      sm: { px: "2", py: "0.5", textStyle: "xs" },
      md: { px: "3", py: "1", textStyle: "sm" },
    },
  },
  compoundVariants: [{ status: "cancelled", size: "md", css: { fontWeight: "normal" } }],
  defaultVariants: { status: "placed", size: "sm" },
});

// The variants become typed props: <StatusBadge status="shipped">; status="tasty" does not compile.
export const StatusBadge = chakra("span", statusBadgeRecipe);
type StatusBadgeVariants = RecipeVariantProps<typeof statusBadgeRecipe>;

// To theme it centrally instead: add `recipes: { statusBadge: statusBadgeRecipe }` to
// defineConfig's theme, then read it anywhere with `useRecipe({ key: "statusBadge" })`.

const badgeCss = defaultSystem.cva(statusBadgeRecipe);
const cases: Array<[label: string, variants: StatusBadgeVariants]> = [
  ["defaults", {}],
  ["cancelled", { status: "cancelled" }],
  ["cancelled md", { status: "cancelled", size: "md" }],
];
for (const [label, variants] of cases) {
  const css = badgeCss(variants)["@layer recipes"] ?? {};   // the compound variant sets the weight
  console.log(`${label.padEnd(12)} weight ${css.fontWeight}, decoration ${css.textDecoration ?? "none"}`);
}
Result
defaults     weight var(--chakra-font-weights-medium), decoration none
cancelled    weight var(--chakra-font-weights-medium), decoration line-through
cancelled md weight var(--chakra-font-weights-normal), decoration line-through

Chakra: reading and switching the colour mode

Prefer _dark, semantic tokens and currentColor (pure CSS, right on first paint); useColorModeValue is for values CSS never reaches, such as a canvas chart's options.

import { Box, chakra, ChakraProvider, ClientOnly, IconButton, Skeleton, Text } from "@chakra-ui/react";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";
import { ColorModeProvider, DarkMode, useColorMode, useColorModeValue } from "./components/ui/color-mode";
import { system } from "./theme";

export function Providers({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <ChakraProvider value={system}>
      <ColorModeProvider defaultTheme="system">{children}</ColorModeProvider>   {/* next-themes */}
    </ChakraProvider>
  );
}

function ToggleButton() {
  const { colorMode, toggleColorMode } = useColorMode();
  const next = colorMode === "dark" ? "light" : "dark";
  return (
    <IconButton aria-label={`Switch to ${next} mode`} variant="ghost" onClick={toggleColorMode}>
      {colorMode === "dark" ? "☾" : "☀"}
    </IconButton>
  );
}

// The mode is unknown until the client mounts: a placeholder first, as Chakra's ColorModeButton does.
export const ThemeToggle = () =>
  <ClientOnly fallback={<Skeleton boxSize="9" />}><ToggleButton /></ClientOnly>;

export const RevenueLegend = () => (
  <Box>
    {/* stroke follows `color`, which CSS switches per mode */}
    <chakra.svg viewBox="0 0 24 4" w="6" h="1" color={{ base: "brand.700", _dark: "brand.300" }} aria-hidden>
      <line x1="0" y1="2" x2="24" y2="2" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth="4" />
    </chakra.svg>
    <Text as="span" ms="2">Revenue</Text>
    <DarkMode><Box bg="surface" p="3">Always dark: a video overlay</Box></DarkMode>
  </Box>
);

// A canvas chart (Chart.js options) never sees CSS: hand it the value for the current mode.
export const useChartGridColour = () => useColorModeValue("#e5e7eb", "#374151");
Result

The toggle flips the .dark class on <html> and every semantic token, _dark value and currentColor stroke follows; the choice persists across reloads, the DarkMode box stays dark in both modes, and a server render shows the skeleton instead of a guessed icon.

  2. Save as src/ThemeToggle.tsx; wrap the app in Providers instead of a bare ChakraProvider

Chakra: responsive values and breakpoints

Mobile-first values (base is every width, each key applies from that breakpoint up), with custom breakpoints written in px, the unit Chakra's defaults use.

import { Box, createSystem, defaultConfig, Grid, Text } from "@chakra-ui/react";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";

// Chakra 3 sorts breakpoints by the bare number, and its defaults are px (sm 480px … 2xl 1536px):
// write yours in px too. "120rem" is read as 120 and sorts before sm.
const system = createSystem(defaultConfig, { theme: { breakpoints: { "3xl": "1920px" } } });
const misordered = createSystem(defaultConfig, { theme: { breakpoints: { "3xl": "120rem" } } });

type Props = { filters: ReactNode; pageSize: number; children: ReactNode };
export function OrdersLayout({ filters, pageSize, children }: Props) {
  return (
    <Grid templateColumns={{ base: "1fr", lg: "16rem 1fr" }} gap={{ base: "3", md: "6" }}>
      <Box as="aside" hideBelow="lg">{filters}</Box>
      <Box>
        <Text textStyle={{ base: "sm", md: "md" }} color="fg.muted">Showing {pageSize} orders</Text>
        <Grid templateColumns={{ base: "1fr", md: "repeat(2, 1fr)", xl: "repeat(3, 1fr)" }} gap="4">
          {children}
        </Grid>
        <Text hideFrom="md" fontWeight={{ smOnly: "semibold" }}>Swipe a card to archive it</Text>
      </Box>
    </Grid>
  );
}

const order = (s: typeof system) => s.breakpoints.values.map((b) => `${b.name}>=${b.min}`).join(" ");
console.log("px:  ", order(system));
console.log("rem: ", order(misordered));
const columns = { base: "1fr", md: "repeat(2, 1fr)", xl: "repeat(3, 1fr)" };
console.log(JSON.stringify(system.css({ gridTemplateColumns: columns }), null, 2));

Chakra: useBreakpointValue without the double render

Use it only when JavaScript needs the value (how many rows to fetch), and pass { ssr: false } in a client-only app, because the default gives the base value on the first render even in the browser.

import { ChakraProvider, defaultSystem, useBreakpointValue } from "@chakra-ui/react";
import { JSDOM } from "jsdom";
import { act } from "react";

function OrdersPage({ ssr }: { ssr: boolean }) {
  // With ssr: true the first render (server AND browser) gets base: a fetch keyed on
  // pageSize would request 10 rows, then 25. ssr: false reads the viewport at once.
  const pageSize = useBreakpointValue({ base: 10, lg: 25 }, { ssr }) ?? 10;
  console.log(`ssr: ${ssr} -> render with pageSize ${pageSize}`);
  return <p>Showing {pageSize} orders</p>;
}

// A 1280px-wide browser window: jsdom has no layout, so matchMedia is a stand-in.
const { window } = new JSDOM("<!doctype html><main></main>");
const minWidthPx = (query: string) =>
  parseFloat(/min-width: ([\d.]+)/.exec(query)?.[1] ?? "0") * (query.includes("rem") ? 16 : 1);
const matchMedia = (query: string) =>
  ({ media: query, matches: minWidthPx(query) <= 1280, addEventListener() {}, removeEventListener() {} });
Object.assign(window, { matchMedia });
Object.assign(globalThis, { window, document: window.document, IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT: true });
const { createRoot } = await import("react-dom/client");   // it probes the DOM when it loads

for (const ssr of [true, false]) {
  const root = createRoot(window.document.querySelector("main")!);
  const page = <ChakraProvider value={defaultSystem}><OrdersPage ssr={ssr} /></ChakraProvider>;
  await act(async () => root.render(page));
  await act(async () => root.unmount());
}
Result
ssr: true -> render with pageSize 10
ssr: true -> render with pageSize 25
ssr: false -> render with pageSize 25

Rules and pitfalls

What a design-system review checks first.

  • Components name roles (surface, fg.muted, --color-accent), never palette steps or hex values — then dark mode and a rebrand are one-file changes.
  • Sizes in rem, so a reader who enlarges text gets a larger page, not clipped labels (WCAG 1.4.4).
  • Set the scheme class in an inline <head> script (next-themes does this for Chakra): applying it after hydration flashes the wrong theme.
  • A custom colorPalette defines all eight keys: solid, contrast, fg, muted, subtle, emphasized, focusRing, border — between them the built-in recipes read each one.
  • useColorModeValue for anything CSS can switch: it needs JavaScript and the resolved mode, which the server does not have — use _dark, a semantic token or currentColor.
  • Custom breakpoints in a unit other than px: Chakra 3.38 sorts by the bare number, so "3xl": "120rem" lands before sm: "480px" and smOnly / lgDown compute wrong ranges. Write them in px, like the defaults.
  • A recipe for a one-off, or style props copied across five files: one-offs are style props, repeats are recipes.
  • Chakra 3's types need moduleResolution: "bundler"; under nodenext every import from @chakra-ui/react type-checks as missing.
  • Your own token, breakpoint and recipe names are typed only after npx @chakra-ui/cli typegen; until then a custom breakpoint key in a style prop is a type error.

Styling — Tailwind CSS

Tailwind 4: tokens declared in CSS with @theme, utilities composed in components, dark mode and variants without writing selectors.

  • browser
  • tailwindcss >=4.0 <5
  • typescript >=5.5
  • react >=18
  • a browser page whose CSS is built by Tailwind CSS 4 (the Vite plugin or the PostCSS plugin)

Sources: Theme variables — Tailwind CSS · Styling with utility classes — Tailwind CSS · Upgrade guide (v3 to v4) — Tailwind CSS

Tailwind 4's model, against Tailwind 3

Tailwind 4 configures in CSS; most answers online still show Tailwind 3's tailwind.config.js, so know which one you are reading.

ConcernTailwind 4 (current)Tailwind 3
Entry point@import "tailwindcss"; in your CSS@tailwind base; @tailwind components; @tailwind utilities;
Design tokens@theme { --color-brand-700: #1d4ed8; } in CSStheme.extend.colors in tailwind.config.js
Build@tailwindcss/vite, or @tailwindcss/postcss; prefixing built inthe tailwindcss PostCSS plugin plus autoprefixer
Which files are scannedautomatic (skips .gitignored files and node_modules); @source adds a pathcontent: ["./src//*.tsx"]
Class-based dark mode@custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *));darkMode: "class"
Your own utility@utility content-auto { content-visibility: auto; } — works with every variant@layer utilities { … } or a plugin
Tokens at run timetheme values become CSS variables once used; @theme static { … } emits them alltheme() inside CSS only
Breakpoints--breakpoint-* in rem (md is 48rem); max-md: and @container / @md: built inscreens in px; container queries via a plugin
Renamed scalesshadow-xs is 3's shadow-sm, shadow-sm is 3's shadow (same for rounded-*, blur-*)shadow-sm, shadow
hover:only where the device can hover: @media (hover: hover)on every device, so taps left sticky hovers

Tokens in @theme

Each variable in a namespace (--color-*, --radius-*, --breakpoint-*) creates its utilities, and is emitted as a CSS variable once something uses it.

@import "tailwindcss";

@theme {
  /* bg-brand-700, text-brand-100, ring-brand-700, from-brand-700 … */
  --color-brand-100: #dbeafe;
  --color-brand-700: #1d4ed8;
  --color-brand-800: #1e40af;

  /* font-sans now means Inter; font-mono is untouched */
  --font-sans: "Inter", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif;

  /* rounded-control, rounded-card */
  --radius-control: 0.375rem;
  --radius-card: 0.75rem;

  /* a 3xl: variant above the built-in 2xl (96rem) */
  --breakpoint-3xl: 120rem;
}

/* Only variables something uses reach the output; a var() in your own CSS counts as a use. */
.receipt-print-header {
  border-bottom: 2px solid var(--color-brand-700);
}

/* Read only from JavaScript (a canvas chart's colours)? Emit them always with static. */
@theme static {
  --color-chart-revenue: #1d4ed8;
  --color-chart-refunds: #b91c1c;
}

/* p-4 is calc(var(--spacing) * 4): the whole spacing scale is one value (0.25rem). */
Result

bg-brand-700, rounded-card, font-sans and 3xl:grid-cols-4 work in any component, the default palette (bg-gray-100…) is still available, and getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue("--color-chart-revenue") returns #1d4ed8 even though no class uses it; to drop a whole default namespace, start a block with --color-*: initial;.

Setup
  1. A Vite + React app: npm create vite@latest shop -- --template react-ts, then npm i tailwindcss @tailwindcss/vite
  2. vite.config.ts: import tailwindcss from "@tailwindcss/vite" and add tailwindcss() to plugins
  3. Save as src/app.css and import it once from src/main.tsx

Excerpt, not compiled or run here: it needs a Vite (or PostCSS) build with Tailwind CSS 4.

Dark mode with semantic roles

Name roles once (bg-surface) and switch their values per scheme, instead of pairing bg-white dark:bg-gray-900 on every element.

/* src/app.css, after @import "tailwindcss" and the @theme block */

/* dark: follows a .dark ancestor instead of the OS setting (the default) */
@custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *));

:root {
  --surface: #ffffff;
  --subtle: #f3f4f6;
  --fg: #111827;
  --muted: #4b5563;
  --border: #e5e7eb;
  --danger: #b91c1c;
  color-scheme: light;
}
.dark {
  --surface: #111827;
  --subtle: #1f2937;
  --fg: #f3f4f6;
  --muted: #9ca3af;
  --border: #374151;
  --danger: #f87171;
  color-scheme: dark;
}

/* inline: the utility uses var(--surface) itself, so it follows the scheme at run time */
@theme inline {
  --color-surface: var(--surface);
  --color-subtle: var(--subtle);
  --color-fg: var(--fg);
  --color-muted: var(--muted);
  --color-border: var(--border);
  --color-danger: var(--danger);
}

/* Components now write  bg-surface text-fg ring-border  and never need dark:.
   Keep dark: for genuine exceptions:  shadow-sm dark:shadow-none  */
Result

Toggling dark on <html> swaps every bg-surface, text-muted and ring-border at once, and native form controls follow through color-scheme.

Utility-first, in a real component

The component is the unit of reuse: its classes are written once, here, and every order on the page is a loop over it.

import { renderToStaticMarkup } from "react-dom/server";

type Order = { id: string; customer: string; items: number; total: string };

// Mobile first: unprefixed classes apply everywhere, md: from 48rem up.
function OrderSummary({ order }: { order: Order }) {
  return (
    <article className="rounded-card bg-surface p-4 shadow-sm ring-1 ring-border md:p-6">
      <header className="flex items-baseline justify-between gap-3">
        <h2 className="text-lg font-semibold text-fg">Order #{order.id}</h2>
        <span className="text-sm text-muted">{order.items} items</span>
      </header>
      <p className="mt-1 text-sm text-muted">{order.customer}</p>
      <p className="mt-4 text-2xl font-bold tabular-nums text-fg">{order.total}</p>
    </article>
  );
}

const html = renderToStaticMarkup(
  <OrderSummary order={{ id: "1042", customer: "Ada Lovelace", items: 3, total: "$42.50" }} />,
);
console.log(html.replaceAll("><", ">\n<"));   // one element per line, for reading

Responsive and state variants

Prefix a utility with the condition it needs — breakpoint, interaction, a parent's or sibling's state, an attribute — and let the element's real state drive the style.

type Status = "processing" | "shipped" | "late";
type Order = { id: string; status: Status };

// Long class lists split into named strings; every class is still a complete literal.
const rowClass =
  "group/row flex flex-col gap-2 rounded-card p-4 hover:bg-subtle " +
  "sm:flex-row sm:items-center sm:justify-between";
const linkClass =
  "font-medium text-fg group-hover/row:underline " +
  "focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-brand-700";
const statusClass = "text-sm text-muted data-[status=late]:font-semibold data-[status=late]:text-danger";
// Shown on hover or keyboard focus of the row; always on touch screens, which cannot hover.
const archiveClass =
  "hidden rounded-control px-3 py-1 text-sm ring-1 ring-border " +
  "group-hover/row:block group-focus-within/row:block pointer-coarse:block pointer-coarse:py-2";

export function OrderRow({ order }: { order: Order }) {
  return (
    <li className={rowClass}>
      <a href={`/orders/${order.id}`} className={linkClass}>Order #{order.id}</a>
      <span data-status={order.status} className={statusClass}>{order.status}</span>
      <button aria-label={`Archive order ${order.id}`} className={archiveClass}>Archive</button>
    </li>
  );
}

const inputClass = "peer rounded-control bg-surface px-3 py-2 ring-1 ring-border user-invalid:ring-danger";

export function ReceiptEmailField() {
  return (
    <label className="grid gap-1">
      <span className="text-sm font-medium text-fg">Email for receipts</span>
      <input type="email" required className={inputClass} />
      <span className="invisible text-sm text-danger peer-user-invalid:visible">
        Enter an address like ada@example.com
      </span>
    </label>
  );
}
Result

Rows stack on phones and line up from sm; a late order's status turns bold red; Archive appears on hover or focus (always on touch); the email hint shows only after the user leaves an invalid address.

Variants are maps of whole class names

Tailwind scans your source as text: a class assembled at run time prints the same string but never gets any CSS.

Interpolated — no CSS for red
import type { ButtonHTMLAttributes } from "react";
import { renderToStaticMarkup } from "react-dom/server";

type Tone = "blue" | "red";
type Props = ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement> & { tone: Tone };

function Button({ tone, className = "", ...rest }: Props) {
  // Built at run time: "bg-red-700" never appears in the source.
  const colours = `bg-${tone}-700 hover:bg-${tone}-800`;
  const classes = `rounded-control px-4 py-2 text-white ${colours} ${className}`.trim();
  return <button className={classes} {...rest} />;
}

console.log(renderToStaticMarkup(<Button tone="blue">Pay</Button>));
console.log(renderToStaticMarkup(<Button tone="red">Cancel order</Button>));
Mapped — every class is a literal
import type { ButtonHTMLAttributes } from "react";
import { renderToStaticMarkup } from "react-dom/server";

type Tone = "blue" | "red";
type Props = ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement> & { tone: Tone };

// `satisfies` fails the build when a new tone has no classes.
const toneClasses = {
  blue: "bg-blue-700 hover:bg-blue-800",
  red: "bg-red-700 hover:bg-red-800",
} satisfies Record<Tone, string>;

function Button({ tone, className = "", ...rest }: Props) {
  const classes = `rounded-control px-4 py-2 text-white ${toneClasses[tone]} ${className}`.trim();
  return <button className={classes} {...rest} />;
}

console.log(renderToStaticMarkup(<Button tone="blue">Pay</Button>));
console.log(renderToStaticMarkup(<Button tone="red">Cancel order</Button>));
Result
<button class="rounded-control px-4 py-2 text-white bg-blue-700 hover:bg-blue-800">Pay</button>
<button class="rounded-control px-4 py-2 text-white bg-red-700 hover:bg-red-800">Cancel order</button>

Composing conditional classes

Attribute-backed state (aria-pressed, disabled) belongs in variants; props with no attribute (density) are chosen in code with a clsx-style helper.

import { renderToStaticMarkup } from "react-dom/server";

// clsx in miniature: keep truthy strings and the keys whose value is true.
type ClassValue = string | false | null | undefined | Record<string, boolean | undefined>;
function cx(...values: ClassValue[]): string {
  return values
    .flatMap((v) => (typeof v === "object" && v !== null ? Object.keys(v).filter((k) => v[k]) : [v]))
    .filter(Boolean)
    .join(" ");
}

type ChipProps = { label: string; count: number; active: boolean; compact?: boolean };

function FilterChip({ label, count, active, compact = false }: ChipProps) {
  return (
    <button
      aria-pressed={active}
      disabled={count === 0}
      className={cx(
        "rounded-full bg-surface text-fg ring-1 ring-border hover:bg-subtle",
        // Styled from the attributes, so what a screen reader hears and what is drawn agree.
        "aria-pressed:bg-brand-700 aria-pressed:text-white disabled:opacity-50",
        { "px-2 py-0.5 text-xs": compact, "px-3 py-1 text-sm": !compact },
      )}
    >
      {label} ({count})
    </button>
  );
}

console.log(renderToStaticMarkup(<FilterChip label="Open" count={12} active />));
console.log(renderToStaticMarkup(<FilterChip label="Returned" count={0} active={false} compact />));

<button aria-pressed="true" class="rounded-full bg-surface text-fg ring-1 ring-border hover:bg-subtle aria-pressed:bg-brand-700 aria-pressed:text-white disabled:opacity-50 px-3 py-1 text-sm">Open (12)</button>
<button aria-pressed="false" disabled="" class="rounded-full bg-surface text-fg ring-1 ring-border hover:bg-subtle aria-pressed:bg-brand-700 aria-pressed:text-white disabled:opacity-50 px-2 py-0.5 text-xs">Returned (0)</button>

Extract a component, not an @apply class

When markup repeats across files, the reusable unit is a component; @apply re-creates the naming problem utilities removed.

A class rebuilt from utilities
@import "tailwindcss";

@layer components {
  .btn-primary {
    @apply rounded-control bg-brand-700 px-4 py-2 font-medium text-white;
    @apply hover:bg-brand-800 focus-visible:outline-2 disabled:opacity-50;
  }
}

/* Every caller still writes the markup by hand:
   <button class="btn-primary" type="submit">Place order</button>
   and the icon, spinner and aria-busy are copied too. */
The component owns markup and styles
import type { ButtonHTMLAttributes } from "react";

type Props = ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement> & { busy?: boolean };

const buttonClass =
  "inline-flex items-center gap-2 rounded-control bg-brand-700 px-4 py-2 font-medium text-white " +
  "hover:bg-brand-800 focus-visible:outline-2 disabled:opacity-50";
// Reduced motion stops the spin but keeps the ring: still a visible busy cue.
const spinnerClass =
  "size-4 animate-spin rounded-full border-2 border-white/40 border-t-white motion-reduce:animate-none";

export function PrimaryButton({ busy = false, className = "", children, ...rest }: Props) {
  // A caller's className is added, not dropped (tailwind-merge if it may conflict).
  return (
    <button
      {...rest}
      aria-busy={busy}
      disabled={busy || rest.disabled}
      className={`${buttonClass} ${className}`.trim()}
    >
      {busy && <span className={spinnerClass} />}
      {children}
    </button>
  );
}
Result

Both draw the same button; only the component also carries the busy state and spinner, so changing them is a one-file edit.

One token idea, three spellings

The same design decision in plain CSS, Tailwind 4 and Chakra UI 3, for a design system that ships to more than one app (the Design Tokens sheet adds the SwiftUI column).

IdeaCSS custom propertiesTailwind 4Chakra UI 3
Palette step--blue-700: #1d4ed8@theme { --color-brand-700 } → bg-brand-700tokens.colors.brand.700 → bg="brand.700"
Role per scheme--surface, redefined under .dark@theme inline { --color-surface: var(--surface) } → bg-surfacesemanticTokens.colors.surface { base, _dark } → bg="surface"
Spacing--space-4: 1rem--spacing: 0.25rem → p-4 is 1remtokens.spacing → p="4"
Radius--radius-card: 12px--radius-card → rounded-cardtokens.radii.card → rounded="card"
Type size--text-lg: 1.125rem--text-lg (and --text-lg--line-height) → text-lgtokens.fontSizes or textStyles → textStyle="lg"
Breakpoint@media (width >= 48rem)--breakpoint-md → md:theme.breakpoints.md → { md: … }
Dark mode[data-theme="dark"] or .dark@custom-variant dark (…) → dark:the .dark class → _dark
Reusable looka classa component with a variant map (or cva)defineRecipe variants
One-off valueinline stylep-[13px], or bg-(--brand-from-api)a style prop or the css prop

Rules and pitfalls

What reviewers flag in Tailwind code.

  • Complete class names only, chosen from maps; for values that really come from data, set a custom property inline and use bg-(--brand-colour).
  • Style state from the element's attributes (aria-pressed:, disabled:, data-[status=late]:, peer-user-invalid:) so accessibility and appearance cannot drift apart.
  • Semantic roles in @theme inline, so components rarely need dark: at all.
  • Two utilities for one property on one element (px-4 px-6): the one later in the stylesheet wins, not the one later in the attribute. Merge with tailwind-merge when callers may override.
  • @apply everywhere: it rebuilds the hand-named class layer utilities were meant to remove. A genuinely new single-purpose class is an @utility, so every variant works with it.
  • Copying a Tailwind 3 answer: tailwind.config.js, darkMode: "class" and @tailwind base are not how 4 is configured (@config can still load an old file while migrating).
  • Anything revealed on hover: needs a second path in Tailwind 4, where hover styles never apply on touch screens: group-focus-within:, pointer-coarse:, or a control that is always visible.

Redux — Core Loop

State → action → reducer → new state → subscribers; effects in middleware. Plain redux 5, written by hand once, so Redux Toolkit holds no mysteries.

  • browser
  • node
  • redux
  • typescript >=5.5
  • node >=22.18
  • redux >=5.0
  • any ES2022+ engine; the examples run on Node.js

Sources: Redux Fundamentals — Redux · Redux Style Guide — Redux · createStore (deprecated) — Redux

The nouns, and their TCA twins

Every Redux answer starts here, and this sheet shows them in the legacy core (redux alone) so the loop is visible before Redux Toolkit writes it for you.

NounIn ReduxTCA counterpart
Stateone plain, serialisable object tree, replaced — never mutated — on every change@ObservableState struct State
Actiona plain object { type: "cart/productAdded", payload }; a discriminated union in TypeScriptenum Action
Reducer(state, action) => newState: pure, synchronous, no I/O, no Date.now()Reduce { state, action in … }
Storeholds the state, runs the reducer on dispatch, notifies subscribe listenersStore / StoreOf<Feature>
dispatchstore.dispatch(action) — the only way state changesstore.send(.action)
Selector(state) => value that reads or derives; memoised when the derivation is costlyreading store.count; computed properties
Middlewarewraps dispatch: logging, thunks, effects that react to actions and dispatch resultsEffect (.run, .cancellable) and @Dependency
Subscribera view that re-reads its selection after every dispatch and re-renders if it changedSwiftUI observation of the store
Golden rulereducers are pure and synchronous; effects never touch state, they dispatchthe same

A minimal feature, end to end

How Redux works underneath — learn the loop once here, then write it with Redux Toolkit (next sheet), because createStore is deprecated.

// Legacy core, shown to make the loop visible: createStore is deprecated in favour of
// Redux Toolkit's configureStore, and the legacy_ alias only removes the strikethrough.
import { legacy_createStore as createStore } from "redux";

type Line = { sku: string; name: string; unitPrice: number; qty: number };
type CartState = { lines: Line[] };

// Everything that can happen to the cart, as events in the past tense.
type CartAction =
  | { type: "cart/productAdded"; payload: { sku: string; name: string; unitPrice: number } }
  | { type: "cart/quantityChanged"; payload: { sku: string; qty: number } };

function cartReducer(state: CartState = { lines: [] }, action: CartAction): CartState {
  switch (action.type) {
    case "cart/productAdded": {
      const existing = state.lines.find((l) => l.sku === action.payload.sku);
      if (!existing) return { lines: [...state.lines, { ...action.payload, qty: 1 }] };
      return { lines: state.lines.map((l) => (l === existing ? { ...l, qty: l.qty + 1 } : l)) };
    }
    case "cart/quantityChanged": {
      const { sku, qty } = action.payload;
      if (qty <= 0) return { lines: state.lines.filter((l) => l.sku !== sku) };
      return { lines: state.lines.map((l) => (l.sku === sku ? { ...l, qty } : l)) };
    }
    default:
      return state;   // Redux's own @@INIT action, and anything another feature dispatches
  }
}

const store = createStore(cartReducer);
const total = (s: CartState) => s.lines.reduce((sum, l) => sum + l.unitPrice * l.qty, 0);

store.subscribe(() => {
  const state = store.getState();
  console.log(`${state.lines.length} lines, total ${total(state).toFixed(2)}`);
});

const mug = { sku: "MUG", name: "Mug", unitPrice: 12.5 };
store.dispatch({ type: "cart/productAdded", payload: mug });
store.dispatch({ type: "cart/productAdded", payload: mug });
store.dispatch({ type: "cart/productAdded", payload: { sku: "TEE", name: "T-shirt", unitPrice: 20 } });
store.dispatch({ type: "cart/quantityChanged", payload: { sku: "MUG", qty: 0 } });
// store.dispatch({ type: "cart/addItem" }) does not compile: not a CartAction
Result
1 lines, total 12.50
1 lines, total 25.00
2 lines, total 45.00
1 lines, total 20.00
Setup
  1. Node.js 22.18 or later (it runs .mts files directly by stripping the types)
  2. npm i redux
  3. Save as main.mts and run node main.mts

Ran with Node 24.16.0, TypeScript 5.9.3 on 2026-11-16: the output matched the result shown.

Actions are events, not setters

Name what happened (productAdded), not what to write (setLines), so the rule lives once in the reducer instead of in every click handler.

Setter — logic in the handler
import { legacy_createStore as createStore } from "redux";

type Product = { sku: string; unitPrice: number };
type Line = Product & { qty: number };
type CartAction = { type: "cart/setLines"; payload: Line[] };

function cartReducer(lines: Line[] = [], action: CartAction): Line[] {
  return action.type === "cart/setLines" ? action.payload : lines;
}

const store = createStore(cartReducer);

// The rule is copied into every "Add" button; the action log only says "lines changed".
function onAddClicked(product: Product) {
  const lines = store.getState();
  const next = lines.some((l) => l.sku === product.sku)
    ? lines.map((l) => (l.sku === product.sku ? { ...l, qty: l.qty + 1 } : l))
    : [...lines, { ...product, qty: 1 }];
  store.dispatch({ type: "cart/setLines", payload: next });
}

onAddClicked({ sku: "MUG", unitPrice: 12.5 });
onAddClicked({ sku: "MUG", unitPrice: 12.5 });
console.log(JSON.stringify(store.getState()));
Event — logic in the reducer
import { legacy_createStore as createStore } from "redux";

type Product = { sku: string; unitPrice: number };
type Line = Product & { qty: number };
type CartAction = { type: "cart/productAdded"; payload: Product };

function cartReducer(lines: Line[] = [], action: CartAction): Line[] {
  if (action.type !== "cart/productAdded") return lines;
  const p = action.payload;
  return lines.some((l) => l.sku === p.sku)
    ? lines.map((l) => (l.sku === p.sku ? { ...l, qty: l.qty + 1 } : l))
    : [...lines, { ...p, qty: 1 }];
}

const store = createStore(cartReducer);

// Any button, a keyboard shortcut or a test sends the same event.
const onAddClicked = (product: Product) => store.dispatch({ type: "cart/productAdded", payload: product });

onAddClicked({ sku: "MUG", unitPrice: 12.5 });
onAddClicked({ sku: "MUG", unitPrice: 12.5 });
console.log(JSON.stringify(store.getState()));
Result
[{"sku":"MUG","unitPrice":12.5,"qty":2}]

Immutable updates

Copy each object on the path to the change and share the rest, so === tells a subscriber exactly what changed — and freeze state in tests to catch a slip.

type Line = { sku: string; qty: number };
type Order = { id: string; shipping: { city: string; express: boolean }; lines: Line[] };

const changeQty = (order: Order, sku: string, qty: number): Order =>
  ({ ...order, lines: order.lines.map((l) => (l.sku === sku ? { ...l, qty } : l)) });

const chooseExpress = (order: Order): Order =>
  ({ ...order, shipping: { ...order.shipping, express: true } });

// In development and tests: an accidental mutation throws instead of silently not rendering.
function deepFreeze<T>(value: T): T {
  if (typeof value === "object" && value !== null) {
    Object.values(value).forEach(deepFreeze);
    Object.freeze(value);
  }
  return value;
}

const before = deepFreeze<Order>({
  id: "1042",
  shipping: { city: "Lisbon", express: false },
  lines: [{ sku: "MUG", qty: 1 }, { sku: "TEE", qty: 2 }],
});

const after = chooseExpress(changeQty(before, "TEE", 3));
console.log("new order object:", after !== before);
console.log("MUG line shared:", after.lines[0] === before.lines[0]);
console.log("TEE line copied:", after.lines[1] !== before.lines[1], after.lines[1]?.qty);
console.log("before untouched:", before.lines[1]?.qty, before.shipping.express);

function buggyChangeQty(order: Order, sku: string, qty: number): Order {
  const line = order.lines.find((l) => l.sku === sku);
  if (line) line.qty = qty;      // same references out: every === check says "nothing changed"
  return order;
}

try {
  buggyChangeQty(before, "MUG", 5);
} catch (e) {
  console.log((e as TypeError).message);
}
Result
new order object: true
MUG line shared: true
TEE line copied: true 3
before untouched: 2 false
Cannot assign to read only property 'qty' of object '#<Object>'

Middleware by hand — a thunk with injected dependencies

Async work never runs in a reducer: a thunk is a function you dispatch, and middleware runs it with dispatch, getState and injected dependencies.

import { applyMiddleware, legacy_createStore as createStore, type Dispatch, type Middleware } from "redux";

type CheckoutState = { status: "idle" | "submitting" | "placed" | "failed"; orderId?: string };
type CheckoutAction =
  | { type: "checkout/submitted" }
  | { type: "checkout/orderPlaced"; payload: { orderId: string } }
  | { type: "checkout/orderFailed"; payload: { error: string } };

function checkoutReducer(state: CheckoutState = { status: "idle" }, action: CheckoutAction): CheckoutState {
  switch (action.type) {
    case "checkout/submitted": return { status: "submitting" };
    case "checkout/orderPlaced": return { status: "placed", orderId: action.payload.orderId };
    case "checkout/orderFailed": return { status: "failed" };
    default: return state;
  }
}

// Injected once: the app passes the real HTTP client, tests pass a fake.
type Deps = { api: { placeOrder(cartId: string): Promise<string> } };
type Thunk = (dispatch: Dispatch<CheckoutAction>, getState: () => CheckoutState, deps: Deps) => Promise<void>;

// Middleware sees every dispatch first: a function is run, anything else goes on to the reducer.
const thunkWith = (deps: Deps): Middleware<{ (thunk: Thunk): Promise<void> }, CheckoutState> =>
  (api) => (next) => (action) =>
    typeof action === "function" ? (action as Thunk)(api.dispatch, api.getState, deps) : next(action);

const placeOrder = (cartId: string): Thunk => async (dispatch, getState, { api }) => {
  if (getState().status === "submitting") return;  // a double click places one order
  dispatch({ type: "checkout/submitted" });
  let orderId: string;
  try {
    orderId = await api.placeOrder(cartId);
  } catch (e) {
    dispatch({ type: "checkout/orderFailed", payload: { error: (e as Error).message } });
    return;
  }
  // Outside the try: a bug in a reducer or subscriber is not reported as "card declined".
  dispatch({ type: "checkout/orderPlaced", payload: { orderId } });
};

const fakeApi = { placeOrder: async (cartId: string) => `ORD-for-${cartId}` };
const store = createStore(checkoutReducer, applyMiddleware(thunkWith({ api: fakeApi })));
store.subscribe(() => console.log("status:", store.getState().status));

// A double click: the second dispatch finds "submitting" and does nothing.
await Promise.all([store.dispatch(placeOrder("cart-7")), store.dispatch(placeOrder("cart-7"))]);
console.log(store.getState());
Result
status: submitting
status: placed
{ status: 'placed', orderId: 'ORD-for-cart-7' }

Effects that react to actions, with cancellation

TCA's .cancellable(id:, cancelInFlight: true) by hand: the effect runs after the reducer, aborts the superseded request, skips an empty field, and reports every outcome as an action for the reducer (next card) to judge.

import { applyMiddleware, legacy_createStore as createStore, type Middleware } from "redux";
import { setTimeout as sleep } from "node:timers/promises";

type CheckFinished = { code: string; discount: number | null; failed: boolean };
type PromoAction =
  | { type: "promo/codeEdited"; payload: string }
  | { type: "promo/checkFinished"; payload: CheckFinished };

const lastResult = (state: CheckFinished | null = null, action: PromoAction) =>
  action.type === "promo/checkFinished" ? action.payload : state;

type ValidatePromo = (code: string, signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<number | null>;

const promoEffects = (validatePromo: ValidatePromo): Middleware => (api) => {
  let inFlight: AbortController | undefined;
  return (next) => (action) => {
    const result = next(action);
    const edited = action as PromoAction;
    if (edited.type !== "promo/codeEdited") return result;

    inFlight?.abort();     // the user typed again: drop the old check (a real field also debounces)
    if (!edited.payload) return result;          // a cleared field needs no check
    const { signal } = (inFlight = new AbortController());
    const finish = (discount: number | null, failed = false) =>
      api.dispatch({ type: "promo/checkFinished", payload: { code: edited.payload, discount, failed } });

    validatePromo(edited.payload, signal).then(finish, () => {
      if (!signal.aborted) finish(null, true);    // the network failed: "try again", not "invalid"
    });
    return result;
  };
};

const fakeValidatePromo: ValidatePromo = (code, signal) => {
  console.log("request for", code);
  return sleep(20, code === "SAVE20" ? 20 : null, { signal }).catch((error: unknown) => {
    console.log("request aborted for", code);
    throw error;
  });
};

const store = createStore(lastResult, applyMiddleware(promoEffects(fakeValidatePromo)));
const edit = (code: string) => store.dispatch({ type: "promo/codeEdited", payload: code });

for (const code of ["SAVE2", "SAVE20"]) edit(code);
await sleep(50);
console.log(store.getState());

edit("");                          // cleared: no request is sent
console.log("after clearing: no new request");
Result
request for SAVE2
request for SAVE20
request aborted for SAVE2
{ code: 'SAVE20', discount: 20, failed: false }
after clearing: no new request

Stale, failed and cleared results in the reducer

The reducer decides what an effect's answer means: an answer for an older code is ignored, a network failure is not "invalid", and an empty field is not "checking".

type CheckFinished = { code: string; discount: number | null; failed: boolean };
type PromoAction =
  | { type: "promo/codeEdited"; payload: string }
  | { type: "promo/checkFinished"; payload: CheckFinished };

type Status = "empty" | "checking" | "checked" | "unreachable";
type PromoState = { code: string; status: Status; discount: number | null };

const initial: PromoState = { code: "", status: "empty", discount: null };

function promoReducer(state = initial, action: PromoAction): PromoState {
  if (action.type === "promo/codeEdited") {
    return { code: action.payload, status: action.payload ? "checking" : "empty", discount: null };
  }
  if (action.type !== "promo/checkFinished" || action.payload.code !== state.code) return state;
  const { discount, failed } = action.payload;
  return { ...state, status: failed ? "unreachable" : "checked", discount };
}

const actions: PromoAction[] = [
  { type: "promo/codeEdited", payload: "SAVE20" },
  { type: "promo/checkFinished", payload: { code: "SAVE2", discount: null, failed: false } },   // stale
  { type: "promo/checkFinished", payload: { code: "SAVE20", discount: null, failed: true } },
  { type: "promo/codeEdited", payload: "" },
];

let state = initial;
for (const action of actions) {
  state = promoReducer(state, action);
  console.log(state.status.padEnd(12), JSON.stringify(state));
}
Result
checking     {"code":"SAVE20","status":"checking","discount":null}
checking     {"code":"SAVE20","status":"checking","discount":null}
unreachable  {"code":"SAVE20","status":"unreachable","discount":null}
empty        {"code":"","status":"empty","discount":null}

Selectors and derived state

Store the minimum, derive totals and flags in selectors, and memoise a costly one on its input reference so unrelated actions do not recompute it.

import { combineReducers, legacy_createStore as createStore } from "redux";

type Line = { sku: string; unitPrice: number; qty: number };
type Action = { type: "cart/productAdded"; payload: Omit<Line, "qty"> } | { type: "ui/themeToggled" };

const cart = (lines: Line[] = [], action: Action): Line[] =>
  action.type === "cart/productAdded" ? [...lines, { ...action.payload, qty: 1 }] : lines;

const darkMode = (on = false, action: Action): boolean => (action.type === "ui/themeToggled" ? !on : on);

const rootReducer = combineReducers({ cart, darkMode });
type RootState = ReturnType<typeof rootReducer>;

// Immutable updates make a reference check exact: same array in, same answer out.
function memoizeOne<A, R>(compute: (input: A) => R): (input: A) => R {
  let last: { input: A; result: R } | undefined;
  return (input) => {
    if (last && Object.is(last.input, input)) return last.result;
    last = { input, result: compute(input) };
    return last.result;
  };
}

let computed = 0;
const selectLines = (s: RootState) => s.cart;
const summarise = memoizeOne((lines: Line[]) => {
  computed++;
  const subtotal = lines.reduce((sum, l) => sum + l.unitPrice * l.qty, 0);
  return { count: lines.length, subtotal, freeShipping: subtotal >= 50 };   // derived, never stored
});
const selectCartSummary = (s: RootState) => summarise(selectLines(s));

const store = createStore(rootReducer);
store.dispatch({ type: "cart/productAdded", payload: { sku: "LAMP", unitPrice: 45 } });
const first = selectCartSummary(store.getState());

store.dispatch({ type: "ui/themeToggled" });
console.log("same object after an unrelated action:", selectCartSummary(store.getState()) === first);

store.dispatch({ type: "cart/productAdded", payload: { sku: "BULB", unitPrice: 8 } });
console.log(selectCartSummary(store.getState()), "computed", computed, "times");
Result
same object after an unrelated action: true
{ count: 2, subtotal: 53, freeShipping: true } computed 2 times

Subscribing a UI

subscribe fires after every dispatch, so a view selects its slice, compares it with the last value and renders only on change — exactly what useSelector does.

import { JSDOM } from "jsdom";
import { legacy_createStore as createStore, type Store } from "redux";

type State = { lines: { sku: string; qty: number }[]; promoCode: string };
type Action = { type: "cart/productAdded"; payload: string } | { type: "promo/codeEdited"; payload: string };

function reducer(state: State = { lines: [], promoCode: "" }, action: Action): State {
  switch (action.type) {
    case "cart/productAdded": return { ...state, lines: [...state.lines, { sku: action.payload, qty: 1 }] };
    case "promo/codeEdited": return { ...state, promoCode: action.payload };
    default: return state;
  }
}

function observe<S, T>(store: Store<S>, select: (s: S) => T, render: (value: T) => void): () => void {
  let current = select(store.getState());
  render(current);
  return store.subscribe(() => {
    const next = select(store.getState());
    if (Object.is(next, current)) return;
    current = next;
    render(next);
  });
}

const { document } = new JSDOM(`<button id="cart">Cart <span id="badge"></span></button>`).window;
const badge = document.querySelector("#badge")!;
const store = createStore(reducer);

const unsubscribe = observe(store, (s) => s.lines.length, (count) => {
  badge.textContent = String(count);
  console.log("badge rendered:", badge.textContent);
});

store.dispatch({ type: "cart/productAdded", payload: "MUG" });
store.dispatch({ type: "promo/codeEdited", payload: "SAVE" });   // count unchanged: no render
store.dispatch({ type: "cart/productAdded", payload: "TEE" });
unsubscribe();                                                    // the view went away
store.dispatch({ type: "cart/productAdded", payload: "CAP" });
console.log("store has", store.getState().lines.length, "lines; badge shows", badge.textContent);
Result
badge rendered: 0
badge rendered: 1
badge rendered: 2
store has 3 lines; badge shows 2

Testing a reducer and an effect

A reducer and a thunk are both plain functions, so test the first with state in and state out, and the second with a recording dispatch and a fake API.

import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { test } from "node:test";

// The reducer and thunk from the middleware card, repeated because the runner needs one file.
type CheckoutState = { status: "idle" | "submitting" | "placed" | "failed"; orderId?: string };
type CheckoutAction =
  | { type: "checkout/submitted" } | { type: "checkout/orderFailed" }
  | { type: "checkout/orderPlaced"; payload: { orderId: string } };

function checkoutReducer(state: CheckoutState = { status: "idle" }, action: CheckoutAction): CheckoutState {
  switch (action.type) {
    case "checkout/submitted": return { status: "submitting" };
    case "checkout/orderPlaced": return { status: "placed", orderId: action.payload.orderId };
    case "checkout/orderFailed": return { status: "failed" };
    default: return state;
  }
}

type Deps = { api: { placeOrder(cartId: string): Promise<string> } };
type GetState = () => CheckoutState;
type Thunk = (dispatch: (a: CheckoutAction) => void, getState: GetState, deps: Deps) => Promise<void>;

const placeOrder = (cartId: string): Thunk => async (dispatch, getState, deps) => {
  if (getState().status === "submitting") return;
  dispatch({ type: "checkout/submitted" });
  let orderId: string;
  try {
    orderId = await deps.api.placeOrder(cartId);
  } catch {
    dispatch({ type: "checkout/orderFailed" });
    return;
  }
  dispatch({ type: "checkout/orderPlaced", payload: { orderId } });
};

test("reducer: a placed order records its id", () => {
  const placed: CheckoutAction = { type: "checkout/orderPlaced", payload: { orderId: "ORD-1" } };
  assert.deepEqual(checkoutReducer({ status: "submitting" }, placed), { status: "placed", orderId: "ORD-1" });
});

test("effect: a declined card dispatches submitted, then failed", async () => {
  const dispatched: string[] = [];
  const api = { placeOrder: async () => Promise.reject(new Error("card declined")) };
  await placeOrder("cart-7")((a) => dispatched.push(a.type), () => ({ status: "idle" }), { api });
  assert.deepEqual(dispatched, ["checkout/submitted", "checkout/orderFailed"]);
});
Result

Two passing tests (ℹ pass 2, ℹ fail 0); the process exits 0.

Testing the double-click guard

A guard that reads getState is tested by handing the thunk the state it guards against, and a fake API that fails the test if it is called.

import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { test } from "node:test";

// The thunk from the middleware card, repeated because the runner needs one file.
type CheckoutState = { status: "idle" | "submitting" | "placed" | "failed"; orderId?: string };
type CheckoutAction =
  | { type: "checkout/submitted" } | { type: "checkout/orderFailed" }
  | { type: "checkout/orderPlaced"; payload: { orderId: string } };

type Deps = { api: { placeOrder(cartId: string): Promise<string> } };
type GetState = () => CheckoutState;
type Thunk = (dispatch: (a: CheckoutAction) => void, getState: GetState, deps: Deps) => Promise<void>;

const placeOrder = (cartId: string): Thunk => async (dispatch, getState, deps) => {
  if (getState().status === "submitting") return;  // a double click places one order
  dispatch({ type: "checkout/submitted" });
  let orderId: string;
  try {
    orderId = await deps.api.placeOrder(cartId);
  } catch {
    dispatch({ type: "checkout/orderFailed" });
    return;
  }
  dispatch({ type: "checkout/orderPlaced", payload: { orderId } });
};

test("a second click while submitting sends nothing", async () => {
  const dispatched: string[] = [];
  const api = { placeOrder: async () => assert.fail("must not call the API") };
  await placeOrder("cart-7")((a) => dispatched.push(a.type), () => ({ status: "submitting" }), { api });
  assert.deepEqual(dispatched, []);
});

test("the first click goes through", async () => {
  const dispatched: string[] = [];
  const api = { placeOrder: async () => "ORD-1042" };
  await placeOrder("cart-7")((a) => dispatched.push(a.type), () => ({ status: "idle" }), { api });
  assert.deepEqual(dispatched, ["checkout/submitted", "checkout/orderPlaced"]);
});

Rules and pitfalls

The tradeoffs to examine during code review.

  • Reducers are pure and synchronous: no fetch, no Date.now(), no Math.random() — pass such values in the action's payload.
  • Keep state minimal and serialisable (no class instances, Map, Date or promises); derive the rest in selectors.
  • Prefix action types with the feature (cart/productAdded) so the log reads as a story and two features never collide.
  • Dispatch the success action outside the try that awaits the request: otherwise a reducer bug is reported to the user as a failed request.
  • Mutating state in a reducer: subscribers compare with ===, so the view silently does not update. Copy, or let Redux Toolkit's Immer do it.
  • Throwing in a reducer's default branch: Redux dispatches its own @@redux/INIT… action, and other features' actions reach every reducer.
  • Two dispatches for one event (setLines then setTotal): a subscriber can render the moment between them.
  • Plain redux with createStore is legacy and for learning the loop; new code uses Redux Toolkit (configureStore, createSlice), which writes all of the above for you.

Redux Toolkit — Slices, Effects, Testing

How small slices become an app store: Immer reducers, cancellable thunks with injected dependencies, listeners, memoised selectors, entities, RTK Query, typed hooks and tests.

createSlice and configureStore

A slice generates its action creators and reducer from one object, and configureStore adds thunks, DevTools and dev-only mutation checks.

import { configureStore, createSlice, type PayloadAction } from "@reduxjs/toolkit";

type Line = { sku: string; name: string; unitPrice: number; qty: number };

const cartSlice = createSlice({
  name: "cart",
  initialState: { lines: [] as Line[] },
  reducers: {
    // Immer: write to a draft as if mutating; the store receives a new, frozen state.
    productAdded(state, action: PayloadAction<Omit<Line, "qty">>) {
      const line = state.lines.find((l) => l.sku === action.payload.sku);
      if (line) line.qty += 1;
      else state.lines.push({ ...action.payload, qty: 1 });
    },
    quantityChanged(state, action: PayloadAction<{ sku: string; qty: number }>) {
      const { sku, qty } = action.payload;
      const line = state.lines.find((l) => l.sku === sku);
      if (qty <= 0) state.lines = state.lines.filter((l) => l.sku !== sku);
      else if (line) line.qty = qty;
    },
    emptied: () => ({ lines: [] }),     // or return a whole new state
  },
  selectors: {
    selectItemCount: (cart) => cart.lines.reduce((n, l) => n + l.qty, 0),
    selectTotal: (cart) => cart.lines.reduce((sum, l) => sum + l.unitPrice * l.qty, 0),
  },
});

export const { productAdded, quantityChanged, emptied } = cartSlice.actions;
export const { selectItemCount, selectTotal } = cartSlice.selectors;

export const store = configureStore({ reducer: { cart: cartSlice.reducer } });
export type RootState = ReturnType<typeof store.getState>;
export type AppDispatch = typeof store.dispatch;

const mug = { sku: "MUG", name: "Mug", unitPrice: 12.5 };
console.log(productAdded(mug));

store.dispatch(productAdded(mug));
store.dispatch(productAdded(mug));
store.dispatch(productAdded({ sku: "TEE", name: "T-shirt", unitPrice: 20 }));
store.dispatch(quantityChanged({ sku: "TEE", qty: 0 }));
console.log("items:", selectItemCount(store.getState()), "total:", selectTotal(store.getState()));
console.log("state is frozen:", Object.isFrozen(store.getState().cart.lines));
Result
{
  type: 'cart/productAdded',
  payload: { sku: 'MUG', name: 'Mug', unitPrice: 12.5 }
}
items: 2 total: 25
state is frozen: true

createAsyncThunk — injected API, cancellation, no double submit

The thunk reads its API from extra (swap it in tests), passes signal down so promise.abort() cancels the request (it still ends in rejected, with meta.aborted set, which is not an error), and condition skips a second submit.

import { configureStore, createAsyncThunk, createSlice } from "@reduxjs/toolkit";

type CheckoutState = { status: "idle" | "submitting" | "placed" | "failed"; orderId?: string };
type Extra = { api: { placeOrder(cartId: string, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<{ orderId: string }> } };

const orderSubmitted = createAsyncThunk.withTypes<{ state: { checkout: CheckoutState }; extra: Extra }>()(
  "checkout/orderSubmitted",
  (cartId: string, { extra, signal }) => extra.api.placeOrder(cartId, signal),
  { condition: (_, { getState }) => getState().checkout.status !== "submitting" },
);

const checkoutSlice = createSlice({
  name: "checkout",
  initialState: { status: "idle" } as CheckoutState,
  reducers: {},
  extraReducers: (builder) => {
    builder
      .addCase(orderSubmitted.pending, () => ({ status: "submitting" }))
      .addCase(orderSubmitted.fulfilled, (_state, { payload }) => ({ status: "placed", ...payload }))
      .addCase(orderSubmitted.rejected, (_state, { meta }) => ({ status: meta.aborted ? "idle" : "failed" }));
  },
});

const slowApi: Extra["api"] = {
  placeOrder: (cartId, signal) => new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const timer = setTimeout(() => resolve({ orderId: `ORD-for-${cartId}` }), 10);
    signal.addEventListener("abort", () => {
      console.log("the API saw the abort");
      clearTimeout(timer);
      reject(signal.reason);
    });
  }),
};

const store = configureStore({
  reducer: { checkout: checkoutSlice.reducer },
  middleware: (getDefault) => getDefault({ thunk: { extraArgument: { api: slowApi } satisfies Extra } }),
});

const first = store.dispatch(orderSubmitted("cart-7"));
const duplicate = await store.dispatch(orderSubmitted("cart-7"));   // condition returned false: never ran
console.log("second click skipped:", orderSubmitted.rejected.match(duplicate) && duplicate.meta.condition);

first.abort("left the checkout page");
console.log((await first).type, store.getState().checkout.status);

const placed = await store.dispatch(orderSubmitted("cart-7")).unwrap();   // the payload, or throws
console.log(placed.orderId, store.getState().checkout.status);
Result
second click skipped: true
the API saw the abort
checkout/orderSubmitted/rejected idle
ORD-for-cart-7 placed
Setup

  2. npm i @reduxjs/toolkit
  3. Save as main.mts and run node main.mts

Listener middleware — debounce and cancel

For effects that react to actions (search as you type, autosave), cancelActiveListeners plus delay is TCA's debounce with cancelInFlight.

import { configureStore, createListenerMiddleware, createSlice, type PayloadAction } from "@reduxjs/toolkit";

const searchSlice = createSlice({
  name: "orderSearch",
  initialState: { results: [] as string[] },
  reducers: {
    queryChanged(state, action: PayloadAction<string>) {
      if (!action.payload) state.results = [];    // a cleared box clears its results at once
    },
    resultsLoaded(state, action: PayloadAction<string[]>) {
      state.results = action.payload;
    },
  },
});

const { queryChanged, resultsLoaded } = searchSlice.actions;

type Extra = { searchOrders(query: string, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<string[]> };

const fakeExtra: Extra = {
  async searchOrders(query) {
    console.log("request:", query);
    return ["ORD-1042 Desk lamp", "ORD-1077 Lamp shade"].filter((o) => o.toLowerCase().includes(query));
  },
};

const listener = createListenerMiddleware({ extra: fakeExtra });
const store = configureStore({
  reducer: { orderSearch: searchSlice.reducer },
  middleware: (getDefault) => getDefault().prepend(listener.middleware),
});

// api.extra is typed from the options above; startListening.withTypes<…>() also types getState.
listener.startListening({
  actionCreator: queryChanged,
  effect: async (action, api) => {
    api.cancelActiveListeners();          // a newer keystroke cancels this run at its next await
    if (!action.payload) return;
    await api.delay(250);                 // the debounce: throws if cancelled meanwhile
    const results = await api.pause(api.extra.searchOrders(action.payload, api.signal));
    api.dispatch(resultsLoaded(results));
  },
});

for (const q of ["l", "la", "lamp"]) store.dispatch(queryChanged(q));
await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 400));
console.log("lamp:", store.getState().orderSearch.results.join(" | "));
Result
request: lamp
lamp: ORD-1042 Desk lamp | ORD-1077 Lamp shade

  2. npm i @reduxjs/toolkit
  3. Save as main.mts and run node main.mts

Testing a debounced listener with mock timers

TCA's TestClock, in Node: t.mock.timers makes the 250 ms wait instant and lets the test step to just before and just after it.

import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { test } from "node:test";
import { configureStore, createAction, createListenerMiddleware } from "@reduxjs/toolkit";

// The listener from the card above, trimmed and repeated: the runner needs one file.
const queryChanged = createAction<string>("orderSearch/queryChanged");

type Extra = { searchOrders(query: string): Promise<string[]> };

test("typing fast sends one request, 250 ms after the last keystroke", async (t) => {
  t.mock.timers.enable({ apis: ["setTimeout"] });      // t.mock is undone when the test ends
  const searchOrders = t.mock.fn(async (query: string) => [`ORD-1042 ${query}`]);
  const listener = createListenerMiddleware({ extra: { searchOrders } satisfies Extra });
  listener.startListening({
    actionCreator: queryChanged,
    effect: async (action, api) => {
      api.cancelActiveListeners();
      await api.delay(250);
      await api.pause(api.extra.searchOrders(action.payload));
    },
  });
  const store = configureStore({
    reducer: () => null,                               // only the effect is under test
    middleware: (getDefault) => getDefault().prepend(listener.middleware),
  });
  const requested = () => searchOrders.mock.calls.map((call) => call.arguments[0]);

  for (const q of ["l", "la", "lamp"]) store.dispatch(queryChanged(q));
  t.mock.timers.tick(249);
  await new Promise(setImmediate);                 // let any effect that could run, run
  assert.deepEqual(requested(), []);               // still inside the debounce window

  t.mock.timers.tick(1);
  await new Promise(setImmediate);                 // let the effect's awaits run
  assert.deepEqual(requested(), ["lamp"]);
});
Result

One passing test (ℹ pass 1, ℹ fail 0) in a few milliseconds, not 250; the process exits 0.

Setup

  2. npm i @reduxjs/toolkit

Entity adapters and createSelector

Normalise collections (ids + entities) for O(1) updates, and memoise derived lists so a view gets the same array until an input changes.

import { configureStore, createEntityAdapter, createSelector, createSlice, type PayloadAction }
  from "@reduxjs/toolkit";

type Status = "open" | "shipped" | "delivered";
type Order = { id: string; customer: string; status: Status };

const ordersAdapter = createEntityAdapter<Order>({ sortComparer: (a, b) => a.id.localeCompare(b.id) });

const ordersSlice = createSlice({
  name: "orders",
  initialState: ordersAdapter.getInitialState({ statusFilter: "open" as Status }),
  reducers: {
    ordersReceived: ordersAdapter.setAll,
    orderShipped(state, action: PayloadAction<string>) {
      ordersAdapter.updateOne(state, { id: action.payload, changes: { status: "shipped" } });
    },
    statusFilterChanged(state, action: PayloadAction<Status>) {
      state.statusFilter = action.payload;
    },
  },
});

const { ordersReceived, orderShipped, statusFilterChanged } = ordersSlice.actions;

const store = configureStore({ reducer: { orders: ordersSlice.reducer } });
type RootState = ReturnType<typeof store.getState>;

const orderSelectors = ordersAdapter.getSelectors((s: RootState) => s.orders);
const selectStatusFilter = (s: RootState) => s.orders.statusFilter;
const selectVisibleOrders = createSelector([orderSelectors.selectAll, selectStatusFilter], (orders, status) =>
  orders.filter((o) => o.status === status),
);

store.dispatch(ordersReceived([
  { id: "1077", customer: "Grace", status: "open" },
  { id: "1042", customer: "Ada", status: "open" },
  { id: "1050", customer: "Alan", status: "delivered" },
]));
const visible = selectVisibleOrders(store.getState());
console.log(visible.map((o) => o.id));
console.log("same array on re-select:", selectVisibleOrders(store.getState()) === visible);

store.dispatch(orderShipped("1042"));
console.log("1042 is", orderSelectors.selectById(store.getState(), "1042")?.status);

store.dispatch(statusFilterChanged("shipped"));
console.log("shipped:", selectVisibleOrders(store.getState()).map((o) => `${o.id} ${o.customer}`));
console.log("recomputations:", selectVisibleOrders.recomputations());
Result
[ '1042', '1077' ]
same array on re-select: true
1042 is shipped
shipped: [ '1042 Ada' ]
recomputations: 2

Composing slices with a shared event

Features stay separate slices, and an event none of them owns (createAction) lets each react in its own reducer — TCA's parent observing a child's delegate action.

import { combineSlices, configureStore, createAction, createSlice, type PayloadAction }
  from "@reduxjs/toolkit";

// An event several features care about, owned by none of them.
const orderPlaced = createAction<{ orderId: string }>("checkout/orderPlaced");

const cartSlice = createSlice({
  name: "cart",
  initialState: { skus: [] as string[] },
  reducers: {
    productAdded(state, action: PayloadAction<string>) {
      state.skus.push(action.payload);
    },
  },
  extraReducers: (builder) => {
    builder.addCase(orderPlaced, (state) => {
      state.skus = [];
    });
  },
});

const historySlice = createSlice({
  name: "orderHistory",
  initialState: { orderIds: [] as string[] },
  reducers: {},
  extraReducers: (builder) => {
    builder.addCase(orderPlaced, (state, action) => {
      state.orderIds.unshift(action.payload.orderId);
    });
  },
});

const store = configureStore({ reducer: combineSlices(cartSlice, historySlice) });

store.dispatch(cartSlice.actions.productAdded("MUG"));
store.dispatch(orderPlaced({ orderId: "ORD-1042" }));
console.log("cart:", store.getState().cart.skus, "history:", store.getState().orderHistory.orderIds);
Result
cart: [] history: [ 'ORD-1042' ]
