Lazy-loaded slices

A code-split feature brings its slice with its route and injects it into the running store, typed in advance with withLazyLoadedSlices.

import { combineSlices, configureStore, createSlice, type PayloadAction, type WithSlice }
  from "@reduxjs/toolkit";

const cartSlice = createSlice({
  name: "cart",
  initialState: { skus: [] as string[] },
  reducers: {},
});

// Shipped in the "Returns" route's chunk, not at start-up.
const returnsSlice = createSlice({
  name: "returns",
  initialState: { requested: [] as string[] },
  reducers: {
    returnRequested(state, action: PayloadAction<string>) {
      state.requested.push(action.payload);
    },
  },
});

const rootReducer = combineSlices(cartSlice).withLazyLoadedSlices<WithSlice<typeof returnsSlice>>();
const store = configureStore({ reducer: rootReducer });
console.log("at start-up:", Object.keys(store.getState()));

// In the route's module, when it loads:
const returns = returnsSlice.injectInto(rootReducer);
store.dispatch(returns.actions.returnRequested("ORD-1042"));
console.log("after the route loads:", Object.keys(store.getState()));
console.log("requested:", returns.selectSlice(store.getState()).requested);
Result
at start-up: [ 'cart' ]
after the route loads: [ 'cart', 'returns' ]
requested: [ 'ORD-1042' ]

Typed hooks with react-redux

Declare useAppDispatch and useAppSelector once, and a component re-renders only when the value it selects changes.

import { configureStore, createSlice, type PayloadAction } from "@reduxjs/toolkit";
import { JSDOM } from "jsdom";
import { act } from "react";
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";
import { Provider, useDispatch, useSelector } from "react-redux";

const cartSlice = createSlice({
  name: "cart",
  initialState: { skus: [] as string[], giftNote: "" },
  reducers: {
    productAdded(state, action: PayloadAction<string>) {
      state.skus.push(action.payload);
    },
    giftNoteEdited(state, action: PayloadAction<string>) {
      state.giftNote = action.payload;
    },
  },
});

const store = configureStore({ reducer: { cart: cartSlice.reducer } });

// hooks.ts — import these everywhere instead of the untyped originals.
const useAppDispatch = useDispatch.withTypes<typeof store.dispatch>();
const useAppSelector = useSelector.withTypes<ReturnType<typeof store.getState>>();

function CartBadge() {
  const count = useAppSelector((s) => s.cart.skus.length);
  console.log("CartBadge rendered with", count);
  return <span aria-label="Items in cart">{count}</span>;
}

function AddToCartButton({ sku }: { sku: string }) {
  const dispatch = useAppDispatch();
  return <button onClick={() => dispatch(cartSlice.actions.productAdded(sku))}>Add {sku}</button>;
}

// In the app, main.tsx renders this into the page; here jsdom provides the page.
const { window } = new JSDOM("<!doctype html><div id=root></div>");
Object.assign(globalThis, { window, document: window.document, IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT: true });
const root = createRoot(window.document.getElementById("root")!);
const app = <Provider store={store}><CartBadge /><AddToCartButton sku="MUG" /></Provider>;

await act(async () => root.render(app));
await act(async () => window.document.querySelector("button")!.click());
await act(async () => store.dispatch(cartSlice.actions.giftNoteEdited("Happy birthday")));   // no re-render
console.log(window.document.getElementById("root")!.innerHTML);
await act(async () => root.unmount());
Result
CartBadge rendered with 0
CartBadge rendered with 1
<span aria-label="Items in cart">1</span><button>Add MUG</button>

RTK Query in brief

For server data, declare endpoints instead of hand-writing thunks and loading flags, and the cache, deduplication and refetch-after-mutation come with them.

import { configureStore } from "@reduxjs/toolkit";
import { createApi, fetchBaseQuery } from "@reduxjs/toolkit/query";
import { createServer } from "node:http";              // a stand-in backend on a free local port
import type { AddressInfo } from "node:net";

type Order = { id: string; status: "open" | "shipped" };

const orders: Order[] = [{ id: "1042", status: "open" }];
let requests = 0;
const server = createServer((req, res) => {
  requests++;
  if (req.method === "PATCH") orders[0]!.status = "shipped";
  res.setHeader("content-type", "application/json").end(JSON.stringify(orders));
});
await new Promise<void>((resolve) => server.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", resolve));

const ordersApi = createApi({
  reducerPath: "ordersApi",
  baseQuery: fetchBaseQuery({ baseUrl: `http://127.0.0.1:${(server.address() as AddressInfo).port}` }),
  tagTypes: ["Order"],
  endpoints: (build) => ({
    getOrders: build.query<Order[], void>({ query: () => "/orders", providesTags: ["Order"] }),
    shipOrder: build.mutation<Order[], string>({
      query: (id) => ({ url: `/orders/${id}/ship`, method: "PATCH" }),
      invalidatesTags: ["Order"],     // cached getOrders results refetch after this succeeds
    }),
  }),
});

const store = configureStore({
  reducer: { [ordersApi.reducerPath]: ordersApi.reducer },
  middleware: (getDefault) => getDefault().concat(ordersApi.middleware),
});

// From "@reduxjs/toolkit/query/react", createApi adds hooks: ordersApi.useGetOrdersQuery().
const first = store.dispatch(ordersApi.endpoints.getOrders.initiate());
const second = store.dispatch(ordersApi.endpoints.getOrders.initiate());   // deduplicated: no request
console.log((await first).data, (await second).data === (await first).data);

await store.dispatch(ordersApi.endpoints.shipOrder.initiate("1042"));
await Promise.all(store.dispatch(ordersApi.util.getRunningQueriesThunk()));
console.log(ordersApi.endpoints.getOrders.select()(store.getState()).data, "requests:", requests);

first.unsubscribe();       // what a component's unmount does; the cache entry expires later
second.unsubscribe();
store.dispatch(ordersApi.util.resetApiState());
server.close();
Result
[ { id: '1042', status: 'open' } ] true
[ { id: '1042', status: 'shipped' } ] requests: 3
Setup

  2. npm i @reduxjs/toolkit
  3. Save as main.mts and run node main.mts

Testing a reducer and a thunk with a fake dependency

Reduce actions over the initial state for reducer tests, and build a fresh store around a fake extraArgument for each thunk test — the TestStore + withDependencies move.

import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { test } from "node:test";
import { configureStore, createAsyncThunk, createSlice, type PayloadAction } from "@reduxjs/toolkit";

type Line = { sku: string; qty: number };
type Extra = { api: { placeOrder(lines: Line[]): Promise<string> } };

const checkoutSubmitted = createAsyncThunk.withTypes<{ state: { cart: { lines: Line[] } }; extra: Extra }>()(
  "cart/checkout",
  (_: void, { getState, extra }) => extra.api.placeOrder(getState().cart.lines),
);

const cartSlice = createSlice({
  name: "cart",
  initialState: { lines: [] as Line[], orderId: "" },
  reducers: {
    productAdded(state, action: PayloadAction<string>) {
      const line = state.lines.find((l) => l.sku === action.payload);
      if (line) line.qty++;
      else state.lines.push({ sku: action.payload, qty: 1 });
    },
  },
  extraReducers: (builder) => {
    builder.addCase(checkoutSubmitted.fulfilled, (_state, { payload }) => ({ lines: [], orderId: payload }));
  },
});

const { productAdded } = cartSlice.actions;

test("reducer: adding the same product twice increments its quantity", () => {
  const actions = [productAdded("MUG"), productAdded("MUG")];
  const state = actions.reduce(cartSlice.reducer, cartSlice.getInitialState());
  assert.deepEqual(state.lines, [{ sku: "MUG", qty: 2 }]);
});

test("thunk: sends the cart to the API, then empties it and records the id", async (t) => {
  const placeOrder = t.mock.fn(async (_lines: Line[]) => "ORD-1042");
  const store = configureStore({                      // a fresh store per test, around the fake
    reducer: { cart: cartSlice.reducer },
    middleware: (getDefault) => getDefault({ thunk: { extraArgument: { api: { placeOrder } } } }),
  });
  store.dispatch(productAdded("MUG"));
  await store.dispatch(checkoutSubmitted());
  assert.deepEqual(placeOrder.mock.calls.map((call) => call.arguments[0]), [[{ sku: "MUG", qty: 1 }]]);
  assert.deepEqual(store.getState().cart, { lines: [], orderId: "ORD-1042" });
});
Result

Two passing tests (ℹ pass 2, ℹ fail 0); the process exits 0.

Common Redux Toolkit pitfalls

The tradeoffs to examine during code review.

SymptomCauseFix
"A non-serializable value was detected"a Date, Map, class instance or promise in state or an actionstore ISO strings or ids; keep live objects outside the store
Reducer change does nothingImmer: reassigned the state parameter (state = …)mutate the draft, or return the new state — never both
Component re-renders on every dispatcha selector returning a new array/object each call (filter, map, {…})createSelector, or select primitives separately
Stale search results overwrite newer onesearlier requests are never cancelledcancelActiveListeners() + signal, or promise.abort() on the thunk
Double order on a double clickthe thunk runs twicecondition: (_, { getState }) => status !== "submitting"
rejected shown as an error after navigating awayan aborted thunk dispatches rejected toocheck action.meta.aborted in the reducer
Hand-written isLoading / data / error per endpointserver cache modelled as client stateRTK Query createApi
A debounce test that sleeps 250 ms, or is flakyreal timers in testsmock.timers.enable({ apis: ["setTimeout"] }) and tick(ms)
Tests leak state between casesone module-level store shared by every testa makeStore(extra) factory, called per test

MVVM & Lightweight Stores

A framework-free view model — snapshot, subscribe, intents — bound to React with useSyncExternalStore, the same model in Zustand, and tests with no UI at all.

  • react >=18
  • any ES2022+ engine; the React cards need React 18 or later

Sources: useSyncExternalStore — React · Choosing the state structure — React · Zustand — GitHub

Where should this state live?

Pick the smallest home that works, and move state outward only when a second consumer, a test or a lifetime demands it.

HomeReach for it whenWhat it costs
Local useState / useReducerone component owns it: an open menu, a draft before submitlogic is tested through the component; lost on unmount
Contexta rarely changing value many components read: theme, locale, the signed-in userevery consumer re-renders on every change; not a store
View model (a class + useSyncExternalStore)a screen with real logic — validation, loading, cancellation — you want to test without Reactyou write subscribe / getSnapshot; one per screen instance
Zustandstate shared across screens with little ceremony: a cart, a player, filtersconventions are yours; selector discipline (useShallow) matters
Redux Toolkita large app: many features reacting to one event log, DevTools time travel, strict conventionsthe most structure and boilerplate
Server cache (RTK Query, TanStack Query)the data lives on a server: lists, details, mutationsa dependency; do not mirror it into any of the above
The URLshareable or bookmarkable state: search, filters, the selected tabstrings only; parse and validate

A framework-free view model

Like a SwiftUI @Observable class: an immutable snapshot, subscribe for change, intents as methods — and no import of React or the DOM.

// The part every view model shares: one snapshot, change notification, nothing UI.
abstract class ViewModel<S extends object> {
  #state: S;
  #listeners = new Set<() => void>();

  constructor(initial: S) {
    this.#state = initial;
  }

  readonly getSnapshot = (): S => this.#state;

  readonly subscribe = (listener: () => void) => {
    this.#listeners.add(listener);
    return () => { this.#listeners.delete(listener); };
  };

  protected update(change: Partial<S>): void {
    this.#state = { ...this.#state, ...change };   // a new object: views compare with ===
    this.#listeners.forEach((notify) => notify());
  }
}

type Order = { id: string; shipped: boolean };

class OrdersViewModel extends ViewModel<{ showShipped: boolean; orders: Order[]; visible: Order[] }> {
  constructor(orders: Order[]) {
    super({ showShipped: false, orders, visible: orders.filter((o) => !o.shipped) });
  }

  // Intents: what the user did. The view calls these and nothing else.
  showShippedToggled() {
    this.#show(!this.getSnapshot().showShipped, this.getSnapshot().orders);
  }

  orderShipped(id: string) {
    const orders = this.getSnapshot().orders.map((o) => (o.id === id ? { ...o, shipped: true } : o));
    this.#show(this.getSnapshot().showShipped, orders);
  }

  #show(showShipped: boolean, orders: Order[]) {
    this.update({ showShipped, orders, visible: orders.filter((o) => showShipped || !o.shipped) });
  }
}

const vm = new OrdersViewModel([
  { id: "1042", shipped: false }, { id: "1050", shipped: true }, { id: "1077", shipped: false },
]);

vm.subscribe(() => console.log("visible:", vm.getSnapshot().visible.map((o) => o.id).join(", ")));
vm.orderShipped("1042");
vm.showShippedToggled();
Result
visible: 1077
visible: 1042, 1050, 1077

Binding to React with useSyncExternalStore

One hook connects any subscribe + getSnapshot object to React, tear-free under concurrent rendering, and the view only reads the snapshot and calls intents.

import { JSDOM } from "jsdom";
import { useState, useSyncExternalStore } from "react";

type Order = { id: string; shipped: boolean };

class OrdersViewModel extends EventTarget {
  #state: { showShipped: boolean; visible: Order[] };
  readonly #all: Order[];

  constructor(all: Order[]) {
    super();
    this.#all = all;
    this.#state = { showShipped: false, visible: all.filter((o) => !o.shipped) };
  }

  readonly getSnapshot = () => this.#state;

  readonly subscribe = (listener: () => void) => {
    this.addEventListener("change", listener);
    return () => this.removeEventListener("change", listener);
  };

  showShippedToggled() {
    const showShipped = !this.#state.showShipped;
    this.#state = { showShipped, visible: this.#all.filter((o) => showShipped || !o.shipped) };
    this.dispatchEvent(new Event("change"));
  }
}

function OrdersScreen({ orders }: { orders: Order[] }) {
  const [vm] = useState(() => new OrdersViewModel(orders));          // one per mounted screen
  const { showShipped, visible } = useSyncExternalStore(vm.subscribe, vm.getSnapshot);
  return (
    <section>
      <button aria-pressed={showShipped} onClick={() => vm.showShippedToggled()}>Show shipped</button>
      <ul>{visible.map((o) => <li key={o.id}>#{o.id}</li>)}</ul>
    </section>
  );
}

const { window } = new JSDOM("<!doctype html><body></body>");     // jsdom provides the page
Object.assign(globalThis, { window, document: window.document });
const { render, fireEvent } = await import("@testing-library/react");   // react-dom probes the DOM on load

const orders = [{ id: "1042", shipped: false }, { id: "1050", shipped: true }];
const page = render(<OrdersScreen orders={orders} />);
console.log(page.container.innerHTML);
fireEvent.click(page.getByRole("button"));
console.log(page.container.innerHTML);

A form field's view model

The field keeps exactly what was typed, judges it only once the user leaves it or submits, and derives the error so it can never disagree with the value.

type FieldState = { email: string; touched: boolean; sentTo: string | null };

// Derived, not stored: an error only once the field was left, and only while the value is wrong.
function errorOf({ email, touched }: FieldState): string | null {
  if (!touched || /^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$/.test(email)) return null;
  return "Enter an address like ada@example.com";
}

class ReceiptEmailViewModel extends EventTarget {
  #state: FieldState = { email: "", touched: false, sentTo: null };

  readonly getSnapshot = () => this.#state;

  readonly subscribe = (listener: () => void) => {
    this.addEventListener("change", listener);
    return () => this.removeEventListener("change", listener);
  };

  // Not trimmed while typing: rewriting a controlled value on every keystroke moves the caret.
  emailChanged = (email: string) => this.#set({ email });

  emailBlurred = () => this.#set({ email: this.#state.email.trim(), touched: true });

  // The form: <form onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); vm.submitted(); }}> — no page reload.
  submitted = () => {
    this.emailBlurred();
    if (errorOf(this.#state) !== null) return;
    this.#set({ sentTo: this.#state.email });      // the app calls its API here
  };

  #set(change: Partial<FieldState>) {
    this.#state = { ...this.#state, ...change };
    this.dispatchEvent(new Event("change"));
  }
}

const vm = new ReceiptEmailViewModel();
const show = (step: string) => {
  const state = vm.getSnapshot();
  console.log(`${step.padEnd(6)} "${state.email}" error: ${errorOf(state) ?? "none"}`);
};

vm.emailChanged(" Ada@Example");
show("typing");
vm.emailBlurred();
show("left");
vm.emailChanged("ada@example.com");
show("fixed");
vm.submitted();
console.log("sent to:", vm.getSnapshot().sentTo);
Result
typing " Ada@Example" error: none
left   "Ada@Example" error: Enter an address like ada@example.com
fixed  "ada@example.com" error: none
sent to: ada@example.com

Two-way binding of a form field

The input's value comes from the view model and every edit and blur goes back through an intent, with the message linked by aria-describedby and announced once by aria-live="polite" instead of a role="alert" on each keystroke.

import { JSDOM } from "jsdom";
import { useState, useSyncExternalStore } from "react";

type FieldState = { email: string; touched: boolean };

const errorOf = ({ email, touched }: FieldState) =>
  touched && !/^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$/.test(email) ? "Enter an address like ada@example.com" : null;

class ReceiptEmailViewModel extends EventTarget {
  #state: FieldState = { email: "", touched: false };
  readonly getSnapshot = () => this.#state;
  readonly subscribe = (listener: () => void) => {
    this.addEventListener("change", listener);
    return () => this.removeEventListener("change", listener);
  };
  emailChanged = (email: string) => this.#set({ email });
  emailBlurred = () => this.#set({ email: this.#state.email.trim(), touched: true });
  #set(change: Partial<FieldState>) {
    this.#state = { ...this.#state, ...change };
    this.dispatchEvent(new Event("change"));
  }
}

function ReceiptEmailField() {
  const [vm] = useState(() => new ReceiptEmailViewModel());
  const state = useSyncExternalStore(vm.subscribe, vm.getSnapshot);
  return (
    <label>
      Email for receipts
      <input value={state.email} onChange={(e) => vm.emailChanged(e.target.value)} onBlur={vm.emailBlurred}
        aria-invalid={errorOf(state) !== null} aria-describedby="email-error" />
      <span id="email-error" aria-live="polite">{errorOf(state)}</span>
    </label>
  );
}

Object.assign(globalThis, { window, document: window.document });

const input = render(<ReceiptEmailField />).getByLabelText("Email for receipts") as HTMLInputElement;

fireEvent.change(input, { target: { value: " Ada@Example" } });
console.log(`typing: "${input.value}" error: ${error()}`);
fireEvent.blur(input);
console.log(`left:   "${input.value}" error: ${error()}`);

Async loading as a discriminated union

idle | loading | loaded | failed in one field rules out isLoading && error contradictions, and the compiler makes the view draw every case.

type Order = { id: string; customer: string; total: number };

type Load<T> =
  | { status: "idle" }
  | { status: "loading"; id: string }
  | { status: "loaded"; data: T }
  | { status: "failed"; id: string; message: string };

// Each case carries only what exists in it: no `data` while loading, the id that failed for Retry.
function describe(state: Load<Order>): string {
  switch (state.status) {
    case "idle":
      return "Pick an order";
    case "loading":
      return `Loading #${state.id}…`;
    case "loaded":
      return `#${state.data.id} for ${state.data.customer}: ${state.data.total.toFixed(2)}`;
    case "failed":
      return `Could not load #${state.id} (${state.message}) [Retry]`;
  }
}
// Add a case to Load and describe() stops compiling until it draws it.

const states: Load<Order>[] = [
  { status: "idle" },
  { status: "loading", id: "1042" },
  { status: "failed", id: "1042", message: "timeout" },
  { status: "loaded", data: { id: "1042", customer: "Ada", total: 42.5 } },
];

for (const state of states) console.log(describe(state));
Result
Pick an order
Loading #1042…
Could not load #1042 (timeout) [Retry]
#1042 for Ada: 42.50

A view model that loads and retries

The view model moves through the union's states, keeps the failure's message for the view, remembers what to retry, and exposes subscribe and getSnapshot for useSyncExternalStore.

import { mock } from "node:test";

type Order = { id: string; customer: string };
type Load<T> =
  | { status: "idle" } | { status: "loading"; id: string }
  | { status: "loaded"; data: T }
  | { status: "failed"; id: string; message: string };
type OrdersRepository = { fetchOrder(id: string): Promise<Order> };

class OrderDetailsViewModel extends EventTarget {
  #state: Load<Order> = { status: "idle" };
  readonly #repo: OrdersRepository;      // injected: the app passes HTTP, tests pass a fake

  constructor(repo: OrdersRepository) {
    super();
    this.#repo = repo;
  }

  readonly getSnapshot = () => this.#state;

  readonly subscribe = (listener: () => void) => {
    this.addEventListener("change", listener);
    return () => this.removeEventListener("change", listener);
  };

  async orderOpened(id: string): Promise<void> {
    this.#set({ status: "loading", id });
    await this.#repo.fetchOrder(id).then(
      (data) => this.#set({ status: "loaded", data }),
      (error: unknown) => this.#set({ status: "failed", id, message: String(error) }),
    );
  }

  async retryTapped(): Promise<void> {
    if (this.#state.status === "failed") await this.orderOpened(this.#state.id);
  }

  #set(state: Load<Order>) {
    this.#state = state;
    this.dispatchEvent(new Event("change"));
  }
}

const fetchOrder = mock.fn(async (id: string) => ({ id, customer: "Ada" }));
fetchOrder.mock.mockImplementationOnce(async () => Promise.reject(new Error("timeout")));

const vm = new OrderDetailsViewModel({ fetchOrder });
vm.subscribe(() => console.log(JSON.stringify(vm.getSnapshot())));
await vm.orderOpened("1042");
await vm.retryTapped();
Result
{"status":"loading","id":"1042"}
{"status":"failed","id":"1042","message":"Error: timeout"}
{"status":"loading","id":"1042"}
{"status":"loaded","data":{"id":"1042","customer":"Ada"}}

Cancelling a load the user has moved on from

Opening another order aborts the request in flight and drops any late answer, and dispose() stops the work when the view unmounts.

import { setTimeout as sleep } from "node:timers/promises";

type Order = { id: string; customer: string };
type Load = { status: "idle" | "loading" } | { status: "loaded"; data: Order };
type OrdersRepository = { fetchOrder(id: string, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<Order> };

class OrderDetailsViewModel extends EventTarget {
  #state: Load = { status: "idle" };
  #inFlight?: AbortController;
  readonly #repo: OrdersRepository;

  constructor(repo: OrdersRepository) {
    super();
    this.#repo = repo;
  }

  readonly getSnapshot = () => this.#state;

  async orderOpened(id: string): Promise<void> {
    this.#inFlight?.abort();                       // the user opened another order
    const { signal } = (this.#inFlight = new AbortController());
    this.#set({ status: "loading" });
    const data = await this.#repo.fetchOrder(id, signal).catch(() => null);
    if (data && !signal.aborted) this.#set({ status: "loaded", data });   // a late answer is dropped
  }

  dispose = () => this.#inFlight?.abort();         // the view calls it on unmount

  #set(state: Load) {
    this.#state = state;
    this.dispatchEvent(new Event("change"));
  }
}

// The first order is slow to load, the second fast; the fetch honours the abort signal.
const customers: Record<string, string> = { "1042": "Ada", "1077": "Grace" };
const slowFirst: OrdersRepository = {
  fetchOrder: (id, signal) => {
    const order = { id, customer: customers[id] ?? "?" };
    return sleep(id === "1042" ? 30 : 5, order, { signal });
  },
};

const vm = new OrderDetailsViewModel(slowFirst);
vm.addEventListener("change", () => console.log(JSON.stringify(vm.getSnapshot())));
const first = vm.orderOpened("1042");
await vm.orderOpened("1077");
await first;
vm.dispose();
Result
{"status":"loading"}
{"status":"loading"}
{"status":"loaded","data":{"id":"1077","customer":"Grace"}}

The same model with Zustand

When the state is shared across screens, keep state and intents in one store, let components subscribe to the slice they draw, and call intents from anywhere.

import { JSDOM } from "jsdom";
import { create } from "zustand";
import { useShallow } from "zustand/react/shallow";

type Order = { id: string; shipped: boolean };
type OrdersState = {
  orders: Order[];
  showShipped: boolean;
  showShippedToggled(): void;
  orderShipped(id: string): void;
};

// `set` merges what each intent returns into the state.
const useOrdersStore = create<OrdersState>()((set) => ({
  orders: [{ id: "1042", shipped: false }, { id: "1050", shipped: true }],
  showShipped: false,
  showShippedToggled: () => set((s) => ({ showShipped: !s.showShipped })),
  orderShipped: (id) =>
    set((s) => ({ orders: s.orders.map((o) => (o.id === id ? { ...o, shipped: true } : o)) })),
}));

function OrdersScreen() {
  const showShipped = useOrdersStore((s) => s.showShipped);
  const toggle = useOrdersStore((s) => s.showShippedToggled);
  // filter() returns a new array each time: useShallow compares the items, not the array.
  const visible = useOrdersStore(useShallow((s) => s.orders.filter((o) => showShipped || !o.shipped)));
  return (
    <section>
      <button aria-pressed={showShipped} onClick={toggle}>Show shipped</button>
      <ul>{visible.map((o) => <li key={o.id}>#{o.id}</li>)}</ul>
    </section>
  );
}

const { window } = new JSDOM("<!doctype html><body></body>");
Object.assign(globalThis, { window, document: window.document });
const { act, render, fireEvent } = await import("@testing-library/react");   // after the page exists

const page = render(<OrdersScreen />);
act(() => useOrdersStore.getState().orderShipped("1042"));        // an intent from outside React
console.log(page.container.innerHTML);
fireEvent.click(page.getByRole("button"));
console.log(page.container.innerHTML);
page.unmount();
Result
<section><button aria-pressed="false">Show shipped</button><ul></ul></section>
<section><button aria-pressed="true">Show shipped</button><ul><li>#1042</li><li>#1050</li></ul></section>

Testing the view model without any UI

Record the states a view would draw while driving intents against a fake repository, so loading, loaded and failed are each asserted with no React in sight.

import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { test } from "node:test";

// The view model from the loads-and-retries card, without retry: repeated because the runner needs one file.
type Order = { id: string; customer: string };
type Load =
  | { status: "idle" | "loading" }
  | { status: "loaded"; data: Order } | { status: "failed"; message: string };
type OrdersRepository = { fetchOrder(id: string): Promise<Order> };

class OrderDetailsViewModel extends EventTarget {
  #state: Load = { status: "idle" };
  readonly #repo: OrdersRepository;

  constructor(repo: OrdersRepository) {
    super();
    this.#repo = repo;
  }

  readonly getSnapshot = () => this.#state;

  async orderOpened(id: string): Promise<void> {
    this.#set({ status: "loading" });
    await this.#repo.fetchOrder(id).then(
      (data) => this.#set({ status: "loaded", data }),
      (error: unknown) => this.#set({ status: "failed", message: String(error) }),
    );
  }

  #set(state: Load) {
    this.#state = state;
    this.dispatchEvent(new Event("change"));
  }
}

test("shows loading, then the order", async () => {
  const vm = new OrderDetailsViewModel({ fetchOrder: async (id) => ({ id, customer: "Ada" }) });
  const seen: string[] = [];                         // every state a view would draw, in order
  vm.addEventListener("change", () => seen.push(vm.getSnapshot().status));
  await vm.orderOpened("1042");
  assert.deepEqual(seen, ["loading", "loaded"]);
});

test("a failure becomes a state the view can draw, not an exception", async () => {
  const vm = new OrderDetailsViewModel({ fetchOrder: async () => Promise.reject(new Error("404")) });
  await vm.orderOpened("9999");
  assert.deepEqual(vm.getSnapshot(), { status: "failed", message: "Error: 404" });
});
Result

Two passing tests (ℹ pass 2, ℹ fail 0); the process exits 0.

Testing the race a UI test rarely catches

Hold each fake response until the test releases it, answer the newer request first, and assert that the slow old answer arriving last changes nothing.

import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { test } from "node:test";

// The view model from the cancelling card, repeated because the runner needs one file.
type Order = { id: string; customer: string };
type Load = { status: "idle" | "loading" } | { status: "loaded"; data: Order };
type OrdersRepository = { fetchOrder(id: string, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<Order> };

class OrderDetailsViewModel extends EventTarget {
  #state: Load = { status: "idle" };
  #inFlight?: AbortController;
  readonly #repo: OrdersRepository;

  constructor(repo: OrdersRepository) {
    super();
    this.#repo = repo;
  }

  readonly getSnapshot = () => this.#state;

  async orderOpened(id: string): Promise<void> {
    this.#inFlight?.abort();
    const { signal } = (this.#inFlight = new AbortController());
    this.#set({ status: "loading" });
    const data = await this.#repo.fetchOrder(id, signal).catch(() => null);
    if (data && !signal.aborted) this.#set({ status: "loaded", data });
  }

  #set(state: Load) {
    this.#state = state;
    this.dispatchEvent(new Event("change"));
  }
}

// A repository that ignores the signal, like a server that answers anyway; the test decides the order.
test("a superseded load never overwrites the newer one", async () => {
  const respond = new Map<string, (order: Order) => void>();
  const fetchOrder = (id: string) => new Promise<Order>((resolve) => respond.set(id, resolve));
  const vm = new OrderDetailsViewModel({ fetchOrder });
  const slow = vm.orderOpened("1042");
  const fast = vm.orderOpened("1077");
  respond.get("1077")!({ id: "1077", customer: "Grace" });
  await fast;
  respond.get("1042")!({ id: "1042", customer: "Ada" });     // the old request answers last
  await slow;
  assert.deepEqual(vm.getSnapshot(), { status: "loaded", data: { id: "1077", customer: "Grace" } });
});
Result

One passing test (ℹ pass 1, ℹ fail 0); the process exits 0.

Rules and pitfalls

What keeps a view model a view model.

  • No React, DOM or router imports in a view model: it takes plain data and dependencies in, and exposes a snapshot and intents out.
  • Return the same snapshot object until something changes: useSyncExternalStore compares with Object.is, and a fresh object per call fails with an infinite-loop error.
  • Make subscribe and getSnapshot stable (arrow fields or bound once): a new subscribe each render makes React resubscribe every render.
  • Create a per-screen view model in useState(() => new …), not in the render body, and stop its work on unmount: useEffect(() => () => vm.dispose(), [vm]).
  • Judge a field when the user leaves it or submits, not on every keystroke; link the message with aria-describedby and announce it once with aria-live="polite", not a role="alert" per keystroke.
  • Mirroring props or server data into a view model by hand: derive from inputs, and leave server data to a server cache.
  • A Zustand selector returning a new array or object (filter, { a, b }) without useShallow: Zustand 5 throws "Maximum update depth exceeded".
  • Rendering on the server: useSyncExternalStore needs a third argument, getServerSnapshot, which must match what the client renders first.

RxJS — Core

Observable → operators → Subscription. Cold until subscribed, push-only, and an error ends the stream.

  • browser
  • node
  • RxJS
  • typescript >=5.5
  • node >=22.18
  • rxjs >=7.8
  • Node.js or a browser

Creating observables — and getting values back out

defer for anything that should run per subscriber; firstValueFrom / lastValueFrom to hand a result to async code.

import { defer, EMPTY, EmptyError, firstValueFrom, from, lastValueFrom, reduce } from "rxjs";

type Order = { id: number; total: number };
let requests = 0;
async function fetchOrder(id: number): Promise<Order> {
  requests++;
  return { id, total: 40 + id };
}

const eager$ = from(fetchOrder(1));            // the promise has already started: one request for everyone
const lazy$ = defer(() => fetchOrder(2));      // a new request per subscriber, only once subscribed
console.log("requests before subscribing:", requests);
console.log(await firstValueFrom(lazy$), await firstValueFrom(lazy$), "requests:", requests);
console.log(await firstValueFrom(eager$), "requests:", requests);

async function* orderPages() {                 // any async iterable (or array) becomes an observable
  yield [{ id: 1, total: 10 }, { id: 2, total: 15 }];
  yield [{ id: 3, total: 5 }];
}

const revenue = await lastValueFrom(
  from(orderPages()).pipe(reduce((sum, page) => sum + page.reduce((s, o) => s + o.total, 0), 0)),
);
console.log("revenue:", revenue);

console.log(await firstValueFrom(EMPTY, { defaultValue: "no orders" }));
try {
  await firstValueFrom(EMPTY);                 // completed without a value
} catch (e) {
  console.log("EmptyError:", e instanceof EmptyError);
}
Result
requests before subscribing: 1
{ id: 2, total: 42 } { id: 2, total: 42 } requests: 3
{ id: 1, total: 41 } requests: 3
revenue: 30
no orders
EmptyError: true

Subjects — the imperative bridge

Keep the subject private and expose asObservable(), so only the owner can push.

import { BehaviorSubject, type Observable, ReplaySubject, Subject } from "rxjs";

type Status = "pending" | "paid" | "shipped";

class OrderTracker {
  readonly #status = new BehaviorSubject<Status>("pending");   // always holds a current value
  readonly #events = new Subject<string>();                    // fire-and-forget, no memory
  readonly #history = new ReplaySubject<Status>(2);            // the last 2, for late subscribers

  readonly status$: Observable<Status> = this.#status.asObservable();   // read-only to callers
  readonly events$ = this.#events.asObservable();
  readonly history$ = this.#history.asObservable();

  get status(): Status {
    return this.#status.getValue();
  }
  advance(next: Status) {
    this.#status.next(next);
    this.#events.next(`moved to ${next}`);
    this.#history.next(next);
  }
}

const tracker = new OrderTracker();
tracker.advance("paid");
tracker.status$.subscribe((s) => console.log("status:", s));   // gets "paid" at once
tracker.events$.subscribe((e) => console.log("event:", e));    // "moved to paid" is gone
tracker.advance("shipped");
tracker.history$.subscribe((h) => console.log("late history:", h));
console.log("current:", tracker.status);
Result
status: paid
status: shipped
event: moved to shipped
late history: paid
late history: shipped
current: shipped

switchMap vs mergeMap vs concatMap vs exhaustMap

The most-asked RxJS question: what happens to the inner request when a new outer value arrives.

import { concatMap, exhaustMap, map, mergeMap, type OperatorFunction, switchMap, timer } from "rxjs";
import { TestScheduler } from "rxjs/testing";

// "Save" is clicked at 0 ms (a), 10 ms (b) and 40 ms (c); each request takes 25 ms.
const saveDraft = (draft: string) => timer(25).pipe(map(() => `saved ${draft}`));

const strategies: [string, OperatorFunction<string, string>][] = [
  ["mergeMap  ", mergeMap(saveDraft)],     // all in parallel, in completion order
  ["switchMap ", switchMap(saveDraft)],    // cancel the previous one: the latest wins
  ["concatMap ", concatMap(saveDraft)],    // a queue: one at a time, in order
  ["exhaustMap", exhaustMap(saveDraft)],   // ignore clicks while one is in flight
];

for (const [name, flatten] of strategies) {
  const scheduler = new TestScheduler(() => {});   // virtual time, starting at 0; no assertions here
  const log = scheduler.run(({ hot }) => {
    const out: string[] = [];
    hot("a 9ms b 29ms c").pipe(flatten).subscribe((v) => out.push(`${v} @${scheduler.now()}`));
    return out;                                  // filled when run() flushes the virtual clock
  });
  console.log(name, log.join(", "));
}
Result
mergeMap   saved a @25, saved b @35, saved c @65
switchMap  saved b @35, saved c @65
concatMap  saved a @25, saved b @50, saved c @75
exhaustMap saved a @25, saved c @65

combineLatest vs zip vs merge vs withLatestFrom

Which input triggers an emission, whether it waits for the others, and when the result completes.

import { combineLatest, map, merge, Subject, withLatestFrom, zip } from "rxjs";

const cartTotal$ = new Subject<number>();
const shippingFee$ = new Subject<number>();
const payClicks$ = new Subject<void>();

// combineLatest: a change of EITHER recomputes, once each has emitted; completes when ALL complete
combineLatest([cartTotal$, shippingFee$])
  .pipe(map(([total, fee]) => total + fee))
  .subscribe((quote) => console.log("combineLatest  quote", quote));

// zip: pairs the n-th value of each (1 + 1 -> 1); completes once ANY input completes and is drained
zip([cartTotal$, shippingFee$]).subscribe((pair) => console.log("zip            pair", pair));

// merge: one stream of both, interleaved as they arrive; completes when ALL complete
merge(cartTotal$, shippingFee$).subscribe((v) => console.log("merge          value", v));

// withLatestFrom: only the click triggers, the cart is sampled; completes with the clicks
// (forkJoin, for requests: waits for ALL to complete, then emits each one's LAST value once)
payClicks$
  .pipe(withLatestFrom(cartTotal$))
  .subscribe(([, total]) => console.log("withLatestFrom charge", total));

cartTotal$.next(30);
shippingFee$.next(5);
cartTotal$.next(45);
payClicks$.next();
Result
merge          value 30
combineLatest  quote 35
zip            pair [ 30, 5 ]
merge          value 5
combineLatest  quote 50
merge          value 45
withLatestFrom charge 45

A networking pipeline with retry and a fallback

fromFetch aborts on unsubscribe; retry only what can succeed next time, fall back to a value only for an outage, and let a 4xx reach the caller.

import { createServer } from "node:http";
import type { AddressInfo } from "node:net";
import { catchError, firstValueFrom, of, retry, throwError, timer } from "rxjs";
import { fromFetch } from "rxjs/fetch";

type Order = { id: number; status: "open" | "closed" };
class HttpError extends Error {
  status: number;
  constructor(status: number) {
    super(`HTTP ${status}`);
    this.status = status;
  }
}

const isRetryable = (e: unknown) => !(e instanceof HttpError && e.status < 500);   // 4xx: no retry

const orders$ = (url: string) =>
  fromFetch(url, {
    selector: async (response) => {                // unsubscribing aborts the request
      if (!response.ok) throw new HttpError(response.status);
      return (await response.json()) as Order[];
    },
  }).pipe(
    retry({ count: 3, delay: (e, n) => (isRetryable(e) ? timer(10 * 2 ** n) : throwError(() => e)) }),
    // Out of retries on an outage: show an empty list. A 401/404 is a real error: let it through.
    catchError((e) => (isRetryable(e) ? of<Order[]>([]) : throwError(() => e))),
  );

let hits = 0;                                      // down for two requests; /admin needs a login
const server = createServer((req, res) => {
  if (req.url === "/admin") res.writeHead(401).end();
  else if (++hits <= 2) res.writeHead(503).end();
  else res.writeHead(200, { "content-type": "application/json" }).end('[{"id":7,"status":"open"}]');
});

await new Promise<void>((resolve) => server.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", resolve));
const base = `http://127.0.0.1:${(server.address() as AddressInfo).port}`;
console.log(await firstValueFrom(orders$(`${base}/orders`)), "after", hits, "attempts");
await firstValueFrom(orders$(`${base}/admin`)).catch((e: Error) => console.log("admin:", e.message));
server.close();
server.closeAllConnections();
Result
[ { id: 7, status: 'open' } ] after 3 attempts
admin: HTTP 401

  2. npm i rxjs
  3. Save as main.mts and run node main.mts

Subscription lifetime: unsubscribe, teardown, takeUntil

A new Observable returns its teardown; takeUntil(destroy$), placed last, ends every stream of a screen at once.

import { finalize, Observable, Subject, takeUntil } from "rxjs";

const socket = new EventTarget();                      // stands in for a WebSocket
const push = (channel: string, message: string) =>
  socket.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent(channel, { detail: message }));

function updates$(channel: string): Observable<string> {
  return new Observable<string>((subscriber) => {
    console.log(`listen ${channel}`);
    const onMessage = (e: Event) => subscriber.next((e as CustomEvent<string>).detail);
    socket.addEventListener(channel, onMessage);
    return () => {                                     // runs on unsubscribe, error or complete
      socket.removeEventListener(channel, onMessage);
      console.log(`stop ${channel}`);
    };
  });
}

// Imperative: keep the Subscription and end it yourself.
const subscription = updates$("orders").subscribe((m) => console.log("dashboard:", m));
push("orders", "order 1 paid");
subscription.unsubscribe();
push("orders", "order 2 paid");                        // no one is listening any more

// Declarative: one destroy$ for the screen. takeUntil goes LAST in the pipe.
const destroy$ = new Subject<void>();
updates$("refunds")
  .pipe(finalize(() => console.log("refunds finalized")), takeUntil(destroy$))
  .subscribe((m) => console.log("refund panel:", m));
push("refunds", "refund 9 approved");
destroy$.next();
destroy$.complete();
push("refunds", "refund 10 approved");
Result
listen orders
dashboard: order 1 paid
stop orders
listen refunds
refund panel: refund 9 approved
stop refunds
refunds finalized

Sharing one execution: share vs shareReplay

Cold means one request per subscriber, share multicasts while someone listens, and shareReplay also replays to late subscribers — with refCount deciding what happens when everyone leaves before completion.

import { defer, lastValueFrom, map, type MonoTypeOperatorFunction, type Observable } from "rxjs";
import { share, shareReplay, timer } from "rxjs";

type Profile = { name: string };
let requests = 0;
const profile$ = defer(() => {                         // cold: each subscription starts a request
  requests++;
  return timer(10).pipe(map((): Profile => ({ name: "Ada" })));   // the response comes after 10 ms
});

async function stayUntilDone(source$: Observable<Profile>) {
  await Promise.all([lastValueFrom(source$), lastValueFrom(source$)]);   // header + sidebar, at once
  await lastValueFrom(source$);                                          // settings screen, later
}

async function leaveEarly(source$: Observable<Profile>) {
  const header = source$.subscribe();
  await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 5));
  header.unsubscribe();                  // the user leaves before the response arrives…
  await lastValueFrom(source$);          // …for a screen that needs the profile too
}

const variants: [string, MonoTypeOperatorFunction<Profile>][] = [
  ["cold          ", (source$) => source$],   // stay 3: one request per subscriber
  ["share()       ", share()],                // 2 and 2: no replay; leaving early cancels the request
  ["shareReplay(1)", shareReplay(1)],         // 1 and 1: replays, and keeps running with no one left
  ["refCount: true", shareReplay({ bufferSize: 1, refCount: true })],
  // refCount: true keeps the replay once the source has completed (stay: 1) but resets when every
  // subscriber leaves BEFORE completion (leave-early: 2) — exactly right for an endless source.
];
console.log("requests:      stay leave-early");
for (const [name, operator] of variants) {
  const counts: number[] = [];
  for (const scenario of [stayUntilDone, leaveEarly]) {
    requests = 0;
    await scenario(profile$.pipe(operator));    // a fresh shared observable per scenario
    counts.push(requests);
  }
  console.log(name, counts.join("    "));
}
Result
requests:      stay leave-early
cold           3    2
share()        2    2
shareReplay(1) 1    1
refCount: true 1    2

RxJS gotchas

What reviewers flag first.

  • An error inside the outer pipe ends it for good. Put catchError on the inner observable — inside switchMap(q => search(q).pipe(catchError(...))) — so the search box keeps working after one failed request.
  • Nested subscribe calls: a subscribe inside a subscribe leaks and races. Flatten with switchMap/mergeMap/concatMap instead.
  • takeUntil before a switchMap or shareReplay does not stop what comes after it. Keep takeUntil the last operator.
  • from(promise) is eager — the work started when the promise was created. Use defer(() => load()) for per-subscriber, retryable work: retry re-subscribes, and only defer re-runs the request.
  • toPromise() is deprecated: firstValueFrom for the first value, lastValueFrom for the last one; both reject with EmptyError on an empty stream unless given { defaultValue }.
  • shareReplay(1) on an endless source keeps it running after everyone leaves; pass { bufferSize: 1, refCount: true } — it still replays a request that has completed, and resets only when everyone leaves before completion.
  • Expose Observable<T> (via asObservable()) from a service, never the Subject — callers should not be able to next your state.
  • Pass combineLatest an array — combineLatest([a$, b$]); the rest-parameter form is deprecated and goes in v8.
  • Plain async/await is simpler for one request and one response. Reach for RxJS when values arrive over time and you need to cancel, combine or rate-limit them.

RxJS + React — Wiring Them Together

Streams live outside the component; React reads them through useSyncExternalStore or an effect that unsubscribes.

  • browser
  • React
  • RxJS
  • typescript >=5.5
  • react >=18
  • rxjs >=7.8
  • node >=22.18
  • a React app in the browser; the examples run in Node.js with jsdom

Sources: useSyncExternalStore — React · useEffect — React · RxJS — Overview

The connection points

There are only a handful, and you should know all of them.

  • Streams live outside render. Build pipelines in a view model, a module or a useState(() => create()) initialiser — never in the component body, where every render would build and subscribe a new one.
  • State with a current value (BehaviorSubject, or a pipeline fed into one) → useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getSnapshot). It is tear-free under concurrent rendering and needs no effect.
  • Server rendering (Next.js, Remix): pass useSyncExternalStore a third argument, getServerSnapshot, or React throws while rendering on the server.
  • Any other observable (derived, events, a timer) → useEffect that subscribes and returns () => subscription.unsubscribe().
  • Inputs go in through methods: an event handler calls vm.search(text), which nexts a private Subject. The component never sees the subject.
  • RxJS is the ObservableObject of this world, minus the magic: React does not know about observables, so every subscription is one you wrote, and one you must end.
  • Before React 18 a useEffect + useState pair was the only way: it renders the initial value first and the real one after the effect. Keep it for streams with no current value.

A view model that exposes observables

Queries in, one state$ out — debounced, de-duplicated, latest-wins, and an error that does not kill the search box.

import { BehaviorSubject, catchError, debounceTime, defer, distinctUntilChanged } from "rxjs";
import { map, of, startWith, Subject, switchMap } from "rxjs";

type SearchState = { status: "idle" | "loading" | "done" | "failed"; results: string[] };

function createProductSearch(api: (query: string) => Promise<string[]>, debounceMs = 300) {
  const queries = new Subject<string>();
  const state = new BehaviorSubject<SearchState>({ status: "idle", results: [] });

  const pipeline = queries.pipe(
    debounceTime(debounceMs),
    distinctUntilChanged(),
    switchMap((q) =>                                         // a newer query discards the older response
      defer(() => api(q)).pipe(
        map((results): SearchState => ({ status: "done", results })),
        catchError(() => of<SearchState>({ status: "failed", results: [] })),   // inside: the box lives on
        startWith<SearchState>({ status: "loading", results: state.getValue().results }),
      )),
  );

  return {
    state$: state.asObservable(),                            // read-only to the view
    search: (text: string) => queries.next(text),           // the view's only input
    getSnapshot: () => state.getValue(),                     // what useSyncExternalStore reads
    connect(): () => void {                                  // React: useEffect(() => vm.connect(), [vm])
      const subscription = pipeline.subscribe((next) => state.next(next));
      return () => subscription.unsubscribe();
    },
  };
}

const vm = createProductSearch(async (q) => {
  if (q === "xx") throw new Error("HTTP 503");
  return ["Mug", "Mug rack", "Teapot"].filter((name) => name.toLowerCase().includes(q));
}, 20);
vm.state$.subscribe(({ status, results }) => console.log(status.padEnd(7), results.join(", ")));
const disconnect = vm.connect();
const pause = () => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 50));

for (const text of ["m", "mu", "mug"]) vm.search(text);     // one burst, one request
await pause();

vm.search("xx");                                             // this request fails…
await pause();

vm.search("mu");                                             // …and the box still works
await pause();
disconnect();
Result
idle    
loading 
done    Mug, Mug rack
loading Mug, Mug rack
failed  
loading 
done    Mug, Mug rack

Subscribing a component: useSyncExternalStore vs an effect

A BehaviorSubject has a current value, so React can read it directly; a derived stream does not, so an effect subscribes and its cleanup unsubscribes.

useSyncExternalStore — a BehaviorSubject
import { JSDOM } from "jsdom";
import { useSyncExternalStore } from "react";
import { BehaviorSubject } from "rxjs";

const { window } = new JSDOM("<!doctype html><body></body>");
Object.assign(globalThis, { window, document: window.document });
const { render, act, cleanup } = await import("@testing-library/react");

type Line = { sku: string; qty: number };
const cart$ = new BehaviorSubject<Line[]>([]);

// Module-level: stable identities, so React subscribes once.
const subscribe = (onChange: () => void) => {
  const subscription = cart$.subscribe(onChange);
  return () => subscription.unsubscribe();
};

const getSnapshot = () => cart$.getValue();   // same object until it changes

function CartBadge() {
  const lines = useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getSnapshot);
  const count = lines.reduce((n, l) => n + l.qty, 0);
  return <span>{count} items</span>;
}

const { container } = render(<CartBadge />);
console.log(container.innerHTML);
act(() => cart$.next([{ sku: "mug", qty: 2 }]));
console.log(container.innerHTML);
cleanup();                                    // unmount
console.log("subscribed after unmount:", cart$.observed);
useEffect + useState — any observable
import { JSDOM } from "jsdom";
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { BehaviorSubject, map, type Observable } from "rxjs";

const { window } = new JSDOM("<!doctype html><body></body>");
Object.assign(globalThis, { window, document: window.document });
const { render, act, cleanup } = await import("@testing-library/react");

type Line = { sku: string; qty: number };
const cart$ = new BehaviorSubject<Line[]>([]);
const itemCount$ = cart$.pipe(map((lines) => lines.reduce((n, l) => n + l.qty, 0)));

function useObservable<T>(source$: Observable<T>, initial: T): T {
  const [value, setValue] = useState(initial);
  useEffect(() => {
    const subscription = source$.subscribe(setValue);
    return () => subscription.unsubscribe();  // the cleanup is the teardown
  }, [source$]);                              // so source$ must be stable
  return value;
}

function CartBadge() {
  const count = useObservable(itemCount$, 0);
  return <span>{count} items</span>;
}

const { container } = render(<CartBadge />);
console.log(container.innerHTML);
act(() => cart$.next([{ sku: "mug", qty: 2 }]));
console.log(container.innerHTML);
cleanup();                                    // unmount

Derived and validated form state

combineLatest over the fields, one derived view object, and distinctUntilChanged so the form re-renders only when a message or the button changes.

import { BehaviorSubject, combineLatest, distinctUntilChanged, map, type Observable } from "rxjs";

type Field = "email" | "password" | "confirmation";
type SignUpView = { canSubmit: boolean; emailError: string | null; passwordHint: string | null };
const sameView = (a: SignUpView, b: SignUpView) =>
  a.canSubmit === b.canSubmit && a.emailError === b.emailError && a.passwordHint === b.passwordHint;

class SignUpForm {
  readonly #email = new BehaviorSubject("");
  readonly #password = new BehaviorSubject("");
  readonly #confirmation = new BehaviorSubject("");

  readonly view$: Observable<SignUpView> = combineLatest([
    this.#email, this.#password, this.#confirmation,
  ]).pipe(
    map(([email, password, confirmation]) => {
      const emailOk = /^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$/.test(email);
      return {
        canSubmit: emailOk && password.length >= 8 && password === confirmation,
        emailError: email === "" || emailOk ? null : "Enter a valid email",   // quiet until they type
        passwordHint: password.length >= 8 ? null : "At least 8 characters",
      };
    }),
    distinctUntilChanged(sameView),
  );

  update(field: Field, value: string) {
    const subjects = { email: this.#email, password: this.#password, confirmation: this.#confirmation };
    subjects[field].next(value);
  }
}

const form = new SignUpForm();
form.view$.subscribe((v) =>
  console.log(v.canSubmit ? "ready  " : "blocked", "|", v.emailError ?? "-", "|", v.passwordHint ?? "-"));
form.update("email", "ada@");
form.update("email", "ada@example.com");
form.update("password", "correct horse");
form.update("confirmation", "correct hors");       // nothing visible changed: no emission
form.update("confirmation", "correct horse");
Result
blocked | - | At least 8 characters
blocked | Enter a valid email | At least 8 characters
blocked | - | At least 8 characters
blocked | - | -
ready   | - | -

Search-as-you-type, end to end

The results are a derived stream with no current value, so an effect subscribes on mount, unsubscribes on unmount, and treats a failed request as a state rather than the end of the stream.

import { JSDOM } from "jsdom";
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { catchError, debounceTime, defer, of, Subject, switchMap } from "rxjs";

const { window } = new JSDOM("<!doctype html><body></body>");
Object.assign(globalThis, { window, document: window.document });   // before React DOM loads: it sees a DOM
const { render, screen, fireEvent, cleanup } = await import("@testing-library/react");

async function searchApi(q: string): Promise<string[]> {
  if (q === "x") throw new Error("HTTP 503");
  return ["Mug", "Mug rack", "Teapot"].filter((name) => name.toLowerCase().includes(q));
}

function createProductSearch(debounceMs = 300) {
  const queries = new Subject<string>();
  const results$ = queries.pipe(
    debounceTime(debounceMs),
    switchMap((q) => defer(() => searchApi(q)).pipe(catchError(() => of(null)))),   // inside: it lives on
  );
  return { search: (text: string) => queries.next(text), results$ };
}

function ProductSearch({ debounceMs }: { debounceMs: number }) {
  const [search] = useState(() => createProductSearch(debounceMs));   // once per mounted component
  const [results, setResults] = useState<string[] | null>([]);       // null: the last search failed
  useEffect(() => {                                                    // the effect starts the pipeline…
    const subscription = search.results$.subscribe(setResults);
    return () => subscription.unsubscribe();                           // …and its cleanup stops it
  }, [search]);
  return (
    <>
      <input type="search" onChange={(e) => search.search(e.target.value)} />
      {results === null ? <p role="alert">Search failed — keep typing to retry</p>
        : <ul>{results.map((name) => <li key={name}>{name}</li>)}</ul>}
    </>
  );
}

render(<ProductSearch debounceMs={20} />);

const type = (value: string) => fireEvent.change(screen.getByRole("searchbox"), { target: { value } });
type("x");
console.log((await screen.findByRole("alert")).textContent);

type("mug");
console.log((await screen.findAllByRole("listitem")).map((li) => li.textContent));
cleanup();
Result
Search failed — keep typing to retry
[ 'Mug', 'Mug rack' ]

When a store is the simpler tool

State that only changes when the user acts is not a stream; a store and a plain derived function read the same, with nothing to unsubscribe in React.

RxJS — streams for plain state
import { BehaviorSubject, combineLatest, distinctUntilChanged, map } from "rxjs";

type Line = { sku: string; price: number; qty: number };

class Cart {
  readonly #lines = new BehaviorSubject<Line[]>([]);
  readonly #discount = new BehaviorSubject(0);
  readonly total$ = combineLatest([this.#lines, this.#discount]).pipe(
    map(([lines, discount]) => lines.reduce((s, l) => s + l.price * l.qty, 0) * (1 - discount)),
    distinctUntilChanged(),
  );
  add(line: Line) {
    this.#lines.next([...this.#lines.getValue(), line]);
  }
  applyDiscount(rate: number) {
    this.#discount.next(rate);
  }
}

const cart = new Cart();
const subscription = cart.total$.subscribe((total) => console.log("total:", total));
cart.add({ sku: "mug", price: 12, qty: 2 });
cart.applyDiscount(0.5);
subscription.unsubscribe();
// In React: a custom hook over total$, and its cleanup.
A store — state plus a plain function
import { createStore } from "zustand/vanilla";

type Line = { sku: string; price: number; qty: number };
type CartState = {
  lines: Line[];
  discount: number;
  add: (line: Line) => void;
  applyDiscount: (rate: number) => void;
};

const cart = createStore<CartState>()((set) => ({
  lines: [],
  discount: 0,
  add: (line) => set((s) => ({ lines: [...s.lines, line] })),
  applyDiscount: (rate) => set({ discount: rate }),
}));

const total = (s: CartState) => s.lines.reduce((sum, l) => sum + l.price * l.qty, 0) * (1 - s.discount);

console.log("total:", total(cart.getState()));
const unsubscribe = cart.subscribe((state) => console.log("total:", total(state)));
cart.getState().add({ sku: "mug", price: 12, qty: 2 });
cart.getState().applyDiscount(0.5);
unsubscribe();
// In React: const cartTotal = useStore(cart, total) — from "zustand".
Result
total: 0
total: 24
total: 12

The same wiring in SolidJS

Solid's from turns an observable into a signal and unsubscribes when its owner is disposed; observable(signal) goes the other way.

import { debounceTime, distinctUntilChanged, finalize, map, type Observable } from "rxjs";
import { from as fromInterop } from "rxjs";                 // aliased: Solid has its own `from`
import { createEffect, createRoot, createSignal, from, observable } from "solid-js";

const catalog = ["Mug", "Mug rack", "Teapot"];

// The same view-model idea: queries in, results out.
function productResults$(query$: Observable<string>): Observable<string[]> {
  return query$.pipe(
    debounceTime(20),
    distinctUntilChanged(),
    map((q) => (q ? catalog.filter((name) => name.toLowerCase().includes(q)) : [])),
    finalize(() => console.log("unsubscribed")),
  );
}

const dispose = createRoot((dispose) => {
  const [query, setQuery] = createSignal("");             // the component's own state
  const query$ = fromInterop(observable(query));          // signal -> RxJS, via Symbol.observable
  const results = from(productResults$(query$), []);      // RxJS -> signal, unsubscribed on dispose
  createEffect(() => console.log("render:", results().join(", ") || "(none)"));
  setQuery("mu");
  setQuery("mug");
  return dispose;
});

await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 50));
dispose();                                                // what unmounting the component does
Result
render: (none)
render: Mug, Mug rack
unsubscribed

Component ← observable cheat table

GoalCode
Read a BehaviorSubject in a componentuseSyncExternalStore(subscribe, () => subject.getValue())
Read any observableuseEffect(() => { const s = obs$.subscribe(setValue); return () => s.unsubscribe(); }, [obs$])
One view model per componentconst [vm] = useState(() => createProductSearch(api)) + useEffect(() => vm.connect(), [vm])
App-wide streama module-level observable, or one passed down through context
Push user input inonChange={(e) => vm.search(e.target.value)}
Fire a side effect (toast, navigation)subscribe in useEffect to an events Subject; never store events in state
Values from props into a streamuseEffect(() => { query$.next(props.query); }, [props.query])
Test itjsdom + Testing Library: fireEvent.change, then await screen.findAllByRole(...)
SolidJSsolid-js from(obs$, initial) → signal; RxJS from(observable(signal)) → observable

RxJS + React pitfalls

  • Subscribing in render — obs$.subscribe(...) in the component body runs on every render and never unsubscribes. Subscribe in useEffect or useSyncExternalStore, nowhere else.
  • Building the pipeline in render — useObservable(query$.pipe(debounceTime(300))) is a new observable each render, so the effect resubscribes and the debounce never fires. Create it once (useMemo, useState initialiser, or a module).
  • Missing teardown — an effect that subscribes but returns nothing leaks a subscription per mount and calls setState after unmount.
  • Stale closures — useEffect(() => { clicks$.subscribe(() => save(draft)); }, []) saves the first draft for ever. Put the value into the stream (withLatestFrom(draft$)) or list it in the dependencies.
  • A new snapshot every call — getSnapshot: () => ({ ...subject.getValue() }) makes React re-render in a loop. Return the stored object itself.
  • An error reaching the outer pipeline ends the stream; the component simply stops updating. catchError inside the switchMap.
  • Disposing in a cleanup what render created — useEffect(() => vm.dispose, [vm]) with vm from useState: StrictMode runs the cleanup, re-runs the effect, and the view model stays dead. Subscribe in the effect (useEffect(() => vm.connect(), [vm])) so a re-run restarts it.
  • StrictMode mounts, unmounts and remounts every component in development. Correct teardown makes that invisible; a missing one shows up as doubled requests.
  • Keep RxJS for what it is good at — debouncing, cancelling, combining events over time — and plain state (useState, a store, Solid signals) for everything else.

Timers & Async Patterns

Delays, tickers, polling, deadlines, debounce and throttle, concurrency limits — with AbortSignal for cancellation and an injected clock for tests.

Which scheduler runs when: browser vs Node

Pick by when the callback must run relative to rendering and I/O, not by habit.

APIWhereRunsReach for it to…
queueMicrotask(fn), await, .thenbothright after the current task, before rendering, timers or I/Ofinish a state change consistently — never in a loop: it starves the page
process.nextTick(fn)Nodeinside a callback or CommonJS: before the promise microtasks; at the top level of an ES module, after themlibrary internals; prefer queueMicrotask
setTimeout(fn, ms)botha task after at least ms; browsers clamp deeply nested ones to 4 ms and hidden tabs to about 1 sdelays, debounce, deadlines
setInterval(fn, ms)bothrepeating; never catches up after the loop was blockeda UI clock; use a deadline loop for anything that must not drift
requestAnimationFrame(fn)browserjust before the next paint (60–120 Hz); paused in hidden tabsanimation, reading layout once per frame
requestIdleCallback(fn, { timeout })browser, not Baselinewhen the frame has spare time, or by timeoutanalytics, prefetching, low-priority cleanup — feature-detect it
scheduler.postTask(fn, { priority, signal })browser, not Baselinea task at user-blocking, user-visible or background priority; cancellablesplitting long work by importance — feature-detect globalThis.scheduler
setImmediate(fn)Nodethe check phase, after pending I/O callbacksyielding to I/O inside a long loop
node:timers/promisesNodesetTimeout, setInterval (async iterator), scheduler.wait (experimental) — all accept { signal }awaitable, cancellable timers without hand-written promises
timer.unref()Nodethe timer no longer keeps the process alivebackground refreshes in a CLI or a server that must be able to exit

A one-shot delay as a promise, with AbortSignal

Every await on a delay is a cancellation point, and the abort listener must go when the timer wins, or each delay leaks one.

import { setTimeout as sleep } from "node:timers/promises";

// Browser and Node: a cancellable delay, written once.
function delay(ms: number, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<void> {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    signal?.throwIfAborted();
    const onAbort = () => {
      clearTimeout(timer);
      reject(signal!.reason);
    };

    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
      signal?.removeEventListener("abort", onAbort);
      resolve();
    }, ms);
    signal?.addEventListener("abort", onAbort, { once: true });
  });
}

async function showToast(message: string, signal: AbortSignal) {
  console.log("show:", message);
  try {
    await delay(30, signal);
    console.log("hide:", message);
  } catch (e) {
    console.log(`dropped "${message}":`, (e as DOMException).name);   // the screen went away first
  }
}

const screen = new AbortController();               // one per screen; abort it on navigation
await showToast("Order placed", screen.signal);
const pending = showToast("Courier assigned", screen.signal);
screen.abort();
await pending;

// Node's built-in: the same cancellation, but it rejects with AbortError and the reason in `cause`.
await sleep(50, undefined, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5) }).catch((e: Error) =>
  console.log("node:timers/promises:", e.name, "caused by", (e.cause as DOMException).name));
Result
show: Order placed
hide: Order placed
show: Courier assigned
dropped "Courier assigned": AbortError
node:timers/promises: AbortError caused by TimeoutError

A repeating timer without drift

Sleeping for the interval adds every tick's work to the period, so sleep until an absolute deadline, skip the slots you missed, and end quietly when aborted mid-sleep.

import { setTimeout as sleep } from "node:timers/promises";

type Clock = { now(): number; sleep(ms: number, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<unknown> };
type Tick = (at: number) => Promise<void>;
const realClock: Clock = { now: () => performance.now(), sleep: (ms, signal) => sleep(ms, null, { signal }) };

async function naiveTicker(clock: Clock, intervalMs: number, tick: Tick, signal: AbortSignal) {
  while (!signal.aborted) {
    await clock.sleep(intervalMs, signal).catch(() => {});   // WRONG: interval + however long tick() took
    if (!signal.aborted) await tick(clock.now());
  }
}

async function ticker(clock: Clock, intervalMs: number, tick: Tick, signal: AbortSignal) {
  let next = clock.now();
  while (!signal.aborted) {
    next += intervalMs;
    const now = clock.now();
    if (now > next) next += Math.ceil((now - next) / intervalMs) * intervalMs;   // fell behind: skip slots
    await clock.sleep(next - now, signal).catch(() => {});   // stopped mid-sleep: end quietly, no AbortError
    if (!signal.aborted) await tick(clock.now());
  }
}

for (const [name, run] of [["naive   ", naiveTicker], ["deadline", ticker]] as const) {
  let t = 0;                                               // a virtual clock: sleeping only moves a number
  const clock: Clock = {
    now: () => t,
    sleep: async (ms) => {
      t += ms;
    },
  };
  const stop = new AbortController();
  const ticks: number[] = [];
  await run(clock, 1000, async (at) => {
    ticks.push(at);
    t += ticks.length === 2 ? 1500 : 40;                   // each refresh takes 40 ms; one takes 1.5 s
    if (ticks.length === 5) stop.abort();
  }, stop.signal);
  console.log(name, ticks.join(", "));
}

// In the app: the real clock, stopped from outside while it sleeps.
await ticker(realClock, 20, async () => {}, AbortSignal.timeout(50));
console.log("real clock: stopped mid-sleep, resolved without an error");
Result
naive    1000, 2040, 4540, 5580, 6620
deadline 1000, 2000, 4000, 5000, 6000
real clock: stopped mid-sleep, resolved without an error

Polling until a condition, and a countdown

Back off while nothing changes and bound the whole poll with one deadline signal (in a browser, use the delay above instead of node:timers/promises).

import { setInterval as every, setTimeout as sleep } from "node:timers/promises";

type Delivery = { status: "preparing" | "on the way" | "delivered" };

async function pollUntil<T>(
  load: (signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<T>,
  isDone: (value: T) => boolean,
  { intervalMs, maxIntervalMs, signal }: { intervalMs: number; maxIntervalMs: number; signal: AbortSignal },
): Promise<T> {
  for (let wait = intervalMs; ; wait = Math.min(wait * 2, maxIntervalMs)) {   // back off: 5, 10, 20, 20…
    const value = await load(signal);
    if (isDone(value)) return value;
    await sleep(wait, undefined, { signal });          // rejects at once when the signal aborts
  }
}

const statuses: Delivery["status"][] = ["preparing", "preparing", "on the way", "delivered"];
const fetchDelivery = async (_signal: AbortSignal): Promise<Delivery> => {
  const status = statuses.shift() ?? "delivered";      // stand-in for fetch(url, { signal })
  console.log("poll:", status);
  return { status };
};

const delivery = await pollUntil(fetchDelivery, (d) => d.status === "delivered", {
  intervalMs: 5,
  maxIntervalMs: 20,
  signal: AbortSignal.timeout(2_000),                  // give up after 2 s overall
});

console.log("done:", delivery.status);

const SECOND = 10;                                     // 10 ms so the example is instant; 1_000 in the app
let remaining = 3;                                     // "you can still cancel the order for 3 s"
for await (const _ of every(SECOND, undefined, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10 * SECOND) })) {
  console.log("cancel window:", remaining, "s");
  if (--remaining === 0) break;                        // break ends the interval
}
Result
poll: preparing
poll: preparing
poll: on the way
poll: delivered
done: delivered
cancel window: 3 s
cancel window: 2 s
cancel window: 1 s

A timeout on an operation

AbortSignal.timeout stops the work itself; Promise.race only stops you waiting — the loser runs on.

import { createServer } from "node:http";
import type { AddressInfo } from "node:net";

const server = createServer(() => {});                 // accepts requests and never answers
await new Promise<void>((resolve) => server.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", resolve));
const url = `http://127.0.0.1:${(server.address() as AddressInfo).port}/api/eta`;

try {                                                  // 1. a deadline that also cancels the request
  await fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(30) });
} catch (e) {
  console.log("deadline:", (e as DOMException).name);
}

const cancelButton = new AbortController();            // 2. the deadline OR the user, whichever is first
setTimeout(() => cancelButton.abort(), 10);
try {
  await fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.any([cancelButton.signal, AbortSignal.timeout(5_000)]) });
} catch (e) {
  console.log("user or deadline:", (e as DOMException).name);
}

function withTimeout<T>(work: Promise<T>, ms: number): Promise<T> {   // 3. no signal to pass: race it
  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
  const deadline = new Promise<never>((_, reject) => {
    timer = setTimeout(() => reject(new Error(`timed out after ${ms} ms`)), ms);
  });
  return Promise.race([work, deadline]).finally(() => clearTimeout(timer));   // don't leave it armed
}

const legacyGeocode = () => new Promise<string>((resolve) => setTimeout(() => resolve("52.52,13.40"), 100));
await withTimeout(legacyGeocode(), 20).catch((e: Error) => console.log("race:", e.message));
console.log("fast enough:", await withTimeout(Promise.resolve("cached"), 20));

server.closeAllConnections();
server.close();
Result
deadline: TimeoutError
user or deadline: AbortError
race: timed out after 20 ms
fast enough: cached

Debounce and throttle — tested with mock timers

Debounce waits for a pause and keeps the last call, throttle fires at once and then at most once per window with the latest value, and mock.timers makes the test instant.

import { mock } from "node:test";

function debounce<A extends unknown[]>(fn: (...args: A) => void, waitMs: number) {
  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
  const debounced = (...args: A) => {
    clearTimeout(timer);                                  // every call restarts the quiet period
    timer = setTimeout(() => fn(...args), waitMs);
  };
  return Object.assign(debounced, { cancel: () => clearTimeout(timer) });
}

function throttle<A extends unknown[]>(fn: (...args: A) => void, ms: number, now = () => performance.now()) {
  let last = -Infinity;                                   // `now`: monotonic; the test passes Date.now
  let trailing: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
  const fire = (args: A) => {
    last = now();
    fn(...args);
  };
  const throttled = (...args: A) => {
    clearTimeout(trailing);
    const wait = ms - (now() - last);
    if (wait <= 0) fire(args);                            // leading edge: at once
    else trailing = setTimeout(() => fire(args), wait);   // trailing edge: the latest call
  };
  return Object.assign(throttled, { cancel: () => clearTimeout(trailing) });
}

mock.timers.enable({ apis: ["setTimeout", "Date"] });     // test clock: time moves only on tick()
const advanceTo = (ms: number) => {
  while (Date.now() < ms) mock.timers.tick(10);
};

const search = debounce((q: string) => console.log(`${Date.now()} ms  search "${q}"`), 300);
const saveScroll = throttle((y: number) => console.log(`${Date.now()} ms  save scroll ${y}`), 100, Date.now);

for (const [at, q] of [[0, "p"], [100, "pi"], [200, "piz"], [700, "pizza"]] as const) {
  advanceTo(at);
  search(q);                                              // typing, then a pause
}

for (let y = 0; y <= 250; y += 50) {
  advanceTo(2000 + y);
  saveScroll(y);                                          // a scroll event every 50 ms
}

advanceTo(3000);
for (const handler of [search, saveScroll]) handler.cancel();   // on unmount: nothing fires late

Cache, then network

An async generator yields the cached copy at once, then the fresh one; offline, the cached copy is the answer, not an error.

type Order = { id: string; status: string };

async function* cacheThenNetwork(
  id: string,
  cache: Map<string, Order>,
  fetchOrder: (id: string) => Promise<Order>,
): AsyncGenerator<{ order: Order; source: "cache" | "network" }> {
  const cached = cache.get(id);
  if (cached) yield { order: cached, source: "cache" };       // paint at once
  try {
    const fresh = await fetchOrder(id);
    cache.set(id, fresh);
    yield { order: fresh, source: "network" };                // then correct it
  } catch (error) {
    if (!cached) throw error;                                 // nothing to show: a real failure
    console.log("offline: keeping the cached copy");
  }
}

const cache = new Map([["A-17", { id: "A-17", status: "preparing" }]]);
const online = async (id: string) => ({ id, status: "on the way" });
const offline = async (): Promise<Order> => {
  throw new TypeError("fetch failed");
};

for (const fetchOrder of [online, offline]) {
  for await (const { order, source } of cacheThenNetwork("A-17", cache, fetchOrder)) {
    console.log(`render ${order.id}: ${order.status} (${source})`);
  }
}

try {
  for await (const _ of cacheThenNetwork("B-2", cache, offline));
} catch (e) {
  console.log("B-2 failed:", (e as Error).message);
}
Result
render A-17: preparing (cache)
render A-17: on the way (network)
render A-17: on the way (cache)
offline: keeping the cached copy
B-2 failed: fetch failed

N jobs — serial, parallel, or with a concurrency limit

for…of + await is serial, Promise.all is everything at once; a small worker pool is the usual answer for uploads and API fan-out.

import { setTimeout as sleep } from "node:timers/promises";

let inFlight = 0;
let peak = 0;
async function uploadPhoto(name: string): Promise<string> {
  peak = Math.max(peak, ++inFlight);
  await sleep(name.length * 3);                         // stand-in for the upload
  inFlight--;
  return name;
}

// A pool of `limit` workers pulling from one queue; results keep the input order. If one item rejects,
// the call rejects — but the other workers keep taking items: pass a signal to stop them too.
async function mapWithLimit<T, R>(
  items: readonly T[], limit: number, work: (item: T) => Promise<R>, signal?: AbortSignal,
): Promise<R[]> {
  const results = new Array<R>(items.length);
  let next = 0;
  const worker = async () => {
    while (next < items.length && !signal?.aborted) {
      const index = next++;                             // claimed synchronously: no two workers take one
      results[index] = await work(items[index]!);
    }
  };
  await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: Math.min(limit, items.length) }, worker));
  signal?.throwIfAborted();                             // stopped early: reject, never a sparse array
  return results;
}

const photos = ["front", "label", "doorstep", "signature", "box"];
const runs: [string, () => Promise<string[]>][] = [
  ["serial  ", () => mapWithLimit(photos, 1, uploadPhoto)],      // = for…of with await
  ["parallel", () => Promise.all(photos.map(uploadPhoto))],
  ["limit 2 ", () => mapWithLimit(photos, 2, uploadPhoto)],
];
for (const [name, run] of runs) {
  peak = 0;
  const results = await run();
  console.log(name, "peak in flight:", peak, "|", results.join(" "));
}

const stop = AbortSignal.timeout(5);                    // e.g. the user cancels the upload sheet
await mapWithLimit(photos, 2, uploadPhoto, stop).catch((e: Error) => console.log("cancelled run:", e.name));
Result
serial   peak in flight: 1 | front label doorstep signature box
parallel peak in flight: 5 | front label doorstep signature box
limit 2  peak in flight: 2 | front label doorstep signature box
cancelled run: TimeoutError
