Text scaling, forced colours and reduced motion

Size in rem so text and targets grow with the reader's font setting; keep borders visible in forced-colours mode; skip motion when they ask for less.

const sheet = new CSSStyleSheet();
sheet.replaceSync(`
  html { font-size: 100%; }                  /* never a px root: it overrides the reader's setting */
  .order-total { font-size: 1.25rem; }
  .icon-button { min-inline-size: 2.75rem; min-block-size: 2.75rem; }   /* 44 px at the default size */
  @media (forced-colors: active) {           /* Windows High Contrast: backgrounds and shadows vanish */
    .icon-button { border: 1px solid ButtonText; }
  }
  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
    *, ::before, ::after {
      animation-duration: 0.01ms !important;
      transition-duration: 0.01ms !important;
      scroll-behavior: auto !important;
    }
  }
`);
document.adoptedStyleSheets = [...document.adoptedStyleSheets, sheet];

// motion started from script is not covered by the CSS above: ask the same question
const reducedMotion = matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)");

function openCart(panel: HTMLElement): void {
  panel.hidden = false;
  // everyone gets the scroll; only the smoothness and the slide depend on the preference
  panel.scrollIntoView({ behavior: reducedMotion.matches ? "auto" : "smooth", block: "nearest" });
  if (reducedMotion.matches) return;          // appear in place
  const slideIn = [{ transform: "translateX(100%)" }, { transform: "none" }];
  panel.animate(slideIn, { duration: 250, easing: "ease-out" });
}

const cart = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#cart")!;
document.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>("#open-cart")?.addEventListener("click", () => openCart(cart));
Result

With the OS setting "reduce motion" on, the cart appears without sliding; in Windows forced-colours mode icon buttons keep a visible border; at a 200% browser font size the totals and icon buttons grow with the text.

Setup
  1. A page with an .order-total, icon buttons, a #open-cart button and a #cart panel
  2. Compile with tsc (lib including DOM) or a bundler, and load the output with <script type="module">

Compiled with TypeScript 5.9.3 (lib DOM) on 2026-11-16; not run here — running it needs a browser page with the elements named in the setup.

React: htmlFor, fragments, useId, focus on route change

useId gives each field instance its own ids; fragments keep labels, lists and tables free of wrapper divs; after a client-side navigation — not on first load — move focus to the new page's heading.

import { StrictMode, useEffect, useId, useRef } from "react";
import { JSDOM } from "jsdom";

const { window } = new JSDOM("<!doctype html><body></body>");
Object.assign(globalThis, { window, document: window.document, IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT: true });
const { render, screen } = await import("@testing-library/react");

function EmailField({ error }: { error?: string }) {
  const id = useId();                        // unique per instance, identical on server and client
  return (
    <>
      <label htmlFor={`${id}-input`}>Email</label>
      <input id={`${id}-input`} type="email" aria-invalid={error ? true : undefined}
        aria-describedby={error ? `${id}-error` : undefined} />
      {error && <p id={`${id}-error`}>{error}</p>}
    </>
  );
}

function Page({ title }: { title: string }) {
  const heading = useRef<HTMLHeadingElement>(null);
  const shownTitle = useRef(title);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (shownTitle.current === title) return;   // first load, even StrictMode's re-run: focus stays put
    shownTitle.current = title;
    heading.current?.focus();                   // client-side navigation: announce the new page
  }, [title]);
  const error = title === "Checkout" ? "Enter your email." : undefined;
  return <main><h1 ref={heading} tabIndex={-1}>{title}</h1><EmailField error={error} /></main>;
}

const app = (title: string) => <StrictMode><Page title={title} /></StrictMode>;   // as Vite's main.tsx
const { rerender } = render(app("Cart"));
const invalid = () => screen.getByRole("textbox", { name: "Email" }).getAttribute("aria-invalid");
console.log("focus:", document.activeElement?.tagName, "invalid:", invalid());
rerender(app("Checkout"));                       // what a router does on navigation
screen.getByRole("textbox", { name: "Email", description: "Enter your email." });   // throws if not linked
console.log("focus:", document.activeElement?.textContent, "invalid:", invalid());
Result
focus: BODY invalid: null
focus: Checkout invalid: true
Setup
  1. A React project: npm create vite@latest app -- --template react-ts
  2. To run it in Node as here: npm i react react-dom jsdom @testing-library/react @testing-library/dom, and npm i -D tsx
  3. Put a tsconfig.json with "compilerOptions": { "jsx": "react-jsx" } next to the file (tsx takes JSX settings only from tsconfig; without it, React is not defined), save as main.tsx, and run npx tsx main.tsx

Automated audit with axe in Playwright

Scan every key page — and each state a page can be in, such as an open drawer — in CI; fail on any WCAG A or AA violation.

import { test, expect } from "@playwright/test";
import AxeBuilder from "@axe-core/playwright";

const wcagAA = ["wcag2a", "wcag2aa", "wcag21a", "wcag21aa", "wcag22aa"];

for (const path of ["/", "/cart", "/checkout"]) {
  test(`${path} has no WCAG A/AA violations`, async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto(path);
    await expect(page.getByRole("main")).toBeVisible();
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(wcagAA)
      .exclude("#support-chat")              // a third-party widget, audited by its vendor
      .analyze();
    // ids and counts make the failure message readable: "color-contrast: 3"
    expect(results.violations.map((v) => `${v.id}: ${v.nodes.length}`)).toEqual([]);
  });
}

test("the open cart drawer has no violations", async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto("/");
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Open cart" }).click();
  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page }).include("#cart").withTags(wcagAA).analyze();
  expect(results.violations).toEqual([]);
});
Result

Each page and the open drawer are scanned; a violation fails the test with its rule id and how many elements break it.

Setup
  1. A Playwright project (npm init playwright@latest) with the app served at baseURL
  2. npm i -D @axe-core/playwright; save under tests/ as a11y.spec.ts and run npx playwright test

Excerpt, not compiled or run here: it needs a Playwright project with @axe-core/playwright (not among this catalog's example libraries) and browsers installed.

Test it, and the pitfalls

Automated checks find the mechanical failures; only a keyboard and a screen reader find the rest.

  • Use a real screen reader on each platform you ship: VoiceOver (macOS, iOS), NVDA or JAWS (Windows), TalkBack (Android), Narrator; Orca on Linux. Then do every flow with the keyboard alone.
  • Run axe in CI (the audit card above) and fail on new violations. It catches many issues, never all: names that make no sense, focus order and announcements need a person.
  • Query by role and accessible name in tests (getByRole("button", { name: "Play" })): a test that needs a test id is a hint the control has no name.
  • Target WCAG 2.2 AA: 4.5:1 text contrast (3:1 for large text and UI parts), targets at least 24×24 px, a visible focus indicator, content usable at 200% text and 400% zoom.
  • <div onclick> and <span role="button"> without tabindex and key handlers; a positive tabindex; outline: none with no replacement focus style.
  • Images without alt, aria-hidden="true" on something focusable, a placeholder as the only label, colour as the only signal of an error.
  • No ARIA is better than bad ARIA: a wrong role overrides the native one and breaks what the element did by itself.

Localization with Intl

Messages in catalogs, plurals by rule, every date, number and list formatted by Intl with the locale and time zone pinned — and layouts that survive RTL and long text.

  • browser
  • node
  • typescript >=5.5
  • node >=22.18
  • any ES2024+ engine with full ICU data; the examples run on Node.js

Sources: Intl — MDN · i18next documentation · Internationalization — W3C

The toolbox

Text comes from a catalog; everything else is formatted by Intl — given a locale and, for time, a time zone.

NeedUsePin or watch
strings in the user's languagea catalog per locale, looked up by key: a typed object, i18next, FormatJSnever build a sentence from fragments
plurals and agreementIntl.PluralRules; i18next _one/_other keys and context; ICU plural and selectPolish has few and many, Arabic six forms — count === 1 is English
dates and timesIntl.DateTimeFormat with dateStyle / timeStylelocale and timeZone, every time
"yesterday", "in 3 hours"Intl.RelativeTimeFormat with numeric: "auto"it formats; you pick the unit from an injected now
numbers, money, units, percentIntl.NumberFormat with style: "currency" | "unit" | "percent"the currency comes from the data, never from the locale
lists, language and region namesIntl.ListFormat, Intl.DisplayNames"a, b, and c" is English only
which localenavigator.languages or Accept-Language, negotiated against what you shipfall back by language, then to a default
sorting, searching, word countsIntl.Collator, Intl.Segmenterthe order of ä, ø and aa changes per language
right-to-left<html lang dir>, <bdi> around user text, logical CSS (margin-inline-start, inset-inline-end, text-align: start)left and right in CSS are bugs in Arabic and Hebrew

A typed message catalog with plurals

Every locale must have every key — the type says so — and plural forms are chosen by Intl.PluralRules, never by count === 1.

type Plural = Partial<Record<Intl.LDMLPluralRule, string>> & { other: string };

const en = {
  "cart.title": "Your cart",
  "cart.greeting": "Welcome back, {name}!",
  "cart.items": { one: "{count} item", other: "{count} items" },
} satisfies Record<string, string | Plural>;

type Key = keyof typeof en;
type Catalog = { [K in Key]: (typeof en)[K] extends string ? string : Plural };

const pl: Catalog = {                      // a missing key here is a compile error
  "cart.title": "Twój koszyk",
  "cart.greeting": "Witaj ponownie, {name}!",
  "cart.items": {
    one: "{count} produkt", few: "{count} produkty", many: "{count} produktów", other: "{count} produktu",
  },
};

function translator(locale: string, catalog: Catalog) {
  const plurals = new Intl.PluralRules(locale);   // built once per locale, reused by every call
  const numbers = new Intl.NumberFormat(locale);
  return (key: Key, params: Record<string, string | number> = {}): string => {
    const message = catalog[key];
    const forms: Plural = typeof message === "string" ? { other: message } : message;
    const template = forms[plurals.select(Number(params.count))] ?? forms.other;
    return template.replace(/\{(\w+)\}/g, (_, name: string) => {
      const value = params[name];
      return typeof value === "number" ? numbers.format(value) : (value ?? `{${name}}`);
    });
  };
}

const show = (t: ReturnType<typeof translator>, counts: number[]) => {
  const items = counts.map((count) => t("cart.items", { count })).join(" | ");
  console.log(t("cart.greeting", { name: "Ada" }), items);
};
show(translator("en", en), [1, 2, 1500]);
show(translator("pl", pl), [1, 2, 5, 22, 1.5]);
Result
Welcome back, Ada! 1 item | 2 items | 1,500 items
Witaj ponownie, Ada! 1 produkt | 2 produkty | 5 produktów | 22 produkty | 1,5 produktu

  2. Save as main.mts and run node main.mts
  3. Optional type-check: npm i -D typescript @types/node, then npx tsc --noEmit --strict --target es2024 --module nodenext main.mts

i18next — lookup, interpolation, plurals, context, fallback

Reach for a library once you need lazy-loaded namespaces, fallbacks and tooling; createInstance keeps it out of global state.

import i18next from "i18next";

const i18n = i18next.createInstance();
await i18n.init({
  lng: "en",
  fallbackLng: "en",
  interpolation: { escapeValue: false },   // React and textContent escape; keep true when building HTML
  resources: {
    en: {
      translation: {
        greeting: "Hello, {{name}}!",
        orders_one: "{{count}} order",
        orders_other: "{{count}} orders",
        shipped: "They shipped your order",
        shipped_female: "She shipped your order",
        help: "Need help? Call us.",
      },
    },
    pl: {
      translation: {
        greeting: "Cześć, {{name}}!",
        orders_one: "{{count}} zamówienie",
        orders_few: "{{count}} zamówienia",
        orders_many: "{{count}} zamówień",
        orders_other: "{{count}} zamówienia",
      },
    },
  },
});

console.log(i18n.t("greeting", { name: "Ada" }), [1, 5].map((count) => i18n.t("orders", { count })));
console.log(i18n.t("shipped", { context: "female" }), "/", i18n.t("shipped", { context: "unknown" }));
await i18n.changeLanguage("pl");
console.log(i18n.t("greeting", { name: "Ada" }), [1, 2, 5, 22].map((count) => i18n.t("orders", { count })));
console.log(i18n.t("help"), i18n.dir("ar"));   // help is missing in pl: falls back to en

ICU messages — plural, select, selectordinal

ICU MessageFormat keeps a whole sentence, with its plural and gender branches, in one translatable string — the format translation tools and FormatJS speak.

import IntlMessageFormat from "intl-messageformat";

const shipped = `{courier} shipped {count, plural,
  =0 {nothing}
  one {# parcel}
  other {# parcels}
} to {gender, select,
  female {her}
  male {his}
  other {their}
} address.`;

const en = new IntlMessageFormat(shipped, "en");     // parse once, format many times
console.log(en.format({ courier: "Ada", count: 1, gender: "female" }));
console.log(en.format({ courier: "Sam", count: 3, gender: "other" }));

const place = new IntlMessageFormat(
  "You finished {rank, selectordinal, one {#st} two {#nd} few {#rd} other {#th}}.",
  "en",
);
console.log([1, 2, 3, 11, 22].map((rank) => place.format({ rank })).join(" "));
Result

Prints Ada shipped 1 parcel to her address., Sam shipped 3 parcels to their address., then You finished 1st. You finished 2nd. You finished 3rd. You finished 11th. You finished 22nd.

Setup
  1. npm i intl-messageformat (FormatJS); react-intl uses the same syntax
  2. Save as main.mts and run node main.mts

Dates, times and relative time

Store instants in UTC; format them with the reader's locale and time zone, both explicit — the server's defaults are nobody's.

const placedAt = new Date("2026-03-08T14:30:00Z");   // an instant, stored and sent as UTC

const readers = [
  ["en-US", "America/New_York"],                       // DST began that morning: UTC-4, not -5
  ["de-DE", "Europe/Berlin"],
  ["ja-JP", "Asia/Tokyo"],
] as const;
for (const [locale, timeZone] of readers) {
  const format = new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { dateStyle: "medium", timeStyle: "short", timeZone });
  console.log(locale, format.format(placedAt));
}

const delivery = new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-GB", {
  weekday: "long", day: "numeric", month: "long", timeZone: "Europe/London",
});
// the range dash is wrapped in U+2009 THIN SPACE: assert against formatter output, not typed text
console.log(delivery.formatRange(new Date("2026-03-10T09:00Z"), new Date("2026-03-12T09:00Z")));

// RelativeTimeFormat only formats: pick the unit yourself, from an injected "now"
const units: [Intl.RelativeTimeFormatUnit, number][] = [["day", 86_400], ["hour", 3_600], ["minute", 60]];
function ago(then: Date, now: Date, rtf: Intl.RelativeTimeFormat): string {
  const seconds = Math.round((then.getTime() - now.getTime()) / 1000);
  for (const [unit, size] of units) {
    if (Math.abs(seconds) >= size) return rtf.format(Math.round(seconds / size), unit);
  }
  return rtf.format(seconds, "second");
}
const english = new Intl.RelativeTimeFormat("en", { numeric: "auto" });   // one per locale, reused
const spanish = new Intl.RelativeTimeFormat("es", { numeric: "auto" });
const now = new Date("2026-03-09T15:00:00Z");
const inTwoHours = new Date("2026-03-09T17:00Z");
const relative = [ago(placedAt, now, english), ago(placedAt, now, spanish), ago(inTwoHours, now, english)];
console.log(relative.join(" | "));
Result

de-DE 08.03.2026, 15:30
ja-JP 2026/03/08 23:30
Tuesday 10 March – Thursday 12 March
yesterday | ayer | in 2 hours

Numbers, currencies, units and lists

The order says which currency; the reader's locale says how to write it.

type Order = { total: number; currency: string; weightKg: number; items: string[] };
const order: Order = { total: 1234.5, currency: "EUR", weightKg: 2.5, items: ["coffee", "tea", "cocoa"] };

// cache formatters per locale and options: building one costs far more than calling format()
function formatters(locale: string, currency: string) {
  return {
    money: new Intl.NumberFormat(locale, { style: "currency", currency }),
    weight: new Intl.NumberFormat(locale, { style: "unit", unit: "kilogram", unitDisplay: "long" }),
    list: new Intl.ListFormat(locale, { type: "conjunction" }),
  };
}

// de-DE and fr-CH put U+00A0 (no-break space) before €, fr-CH also before "kilogrammes";
// fr-CH groups thousands with an apostrophe.
// In tests, compare with the formatter's own output, never with a typed literal.
for (const locale of ["en-US", "de-DE", "fr-CH"]) {
  const f = formatters(locale, order.currency);
  console.log(locale, "|", f.money.format(order.total), "|", f.weight.format(order.weightKg));
}
console.log(formatters("en", order.currency).list.format(order.items));

// one-off demonstrations — in an app, these too would be built once and reused
const yen = new Intl.NumberFormat("ja-JP", { style: "currency", currency: "JPY" });
console.log(yen.format(1234.5), new Intl.NumberFormat("en-IN").format(12_345_678)); // no minor unit; lakh
const compact = (locale: string) => new Intl.NumberFormat(locale, { notation: "compact" }).format(1_520_000);
console.log(compact("en"), compact("es"));                                  // es: "1,5" + U+00A0 + "M"
console.log(new Intl.NumberFormat("en", { style: "percent", maximumFractionDigits: 1 }).format(0.1234));
console.log(new Intl.NumberFormat("en", { style: "unit", unit: "kilometer-per-hour" }).format(88));
console.log(new Intl.ListFormat("es", { type: "disjunction" }).format(["té", "café"]));
const languages = new Intl.DisplayNames(["en"], { type: "language" });
const regions = new Intl.DisplayNames(["es"], { type: "region" });
console.log(languages.of("pt-BR"), "/", regions.of("DE"));

Negotiate the locale, then set lang and dir

Accept-Language is untrusted input: skip anything malformed, read q in any case, count each tag once, then match exact tag, same language, default — and let the script decide <html lang dir>.

const shipped = ["en", "en-GB", "es", "pt-BR", "ar"];

// Intl throws RangeError on "en_US", "*", "" or "<script>": a bad header must never become a 500
const canonical = (tag: string) => {
  try {
    return Intl.getCanonicalLocales(tag)[0];
  } catch {
    return undefined;
  }
};

function requestedLocales(header: string): string[] {
  const weights = new Map<string, number>();                     // first mention of a tag wins
  for (const part of header.slice(0, 1_000).split(",")) {        // cap the work one header can cause
    const [rawTag = "", ...params] = part.split(";").map((p) => p.trim());
    const q = params.find((p) => p.toLowerCase().startsWith("q="));   // parameter names ignore case
    const weight = q === undefined ? 1 : Number(q.slice(2));     // "q=abc" → NaN → dropped
    const tag = canonical(rawTag);
    if (tag && weight > 0 && weight <= 1 && !weights.has(tag)) weights.set(tag, weight);
  }
  return [...weights].sort((a, b) => b[1] - a[1]).slice(0, 20).map(([tag]) => tag);
}

function negotiate(requested: string[], available: string[], fallback: string): string {
  for (const tag of requested) {
    const language = new Intl.Locale(tag).language;
    const match = available.find((a) => a.toLowerCase() === tag.toLowerCase())
      ?? available.find((a) => new Intl.Locale(a).language === language);
    if (match) return match;
  }
  return fallback;
}

const RTL_SCRIPTS = new Set(["Arab", "Hebr", "Thaa", "Syrc", "Nkoo", "Adlm", "Rohg"]);
const direction = (tag: string) =>
  RTL_SCRIPTS.has(new Intl.Locale(tag).maximize().script ?? "") ? "rtl" : "ltr";

const hostile = ["fr-FR,".repeat(25) + "es", "en_US, *, <script>, fr;q=x, pt-PT;q=0.2"];
for (const header of ["ar-EG,ar;Q=0.9", "es;Q=0.1,en;q=0.9", ...hostile]) {
  const requested = requestedLocales(header);
  const lang = negotiate(requested, shipped, "en");   // in a page: set <html lang> and dir from these two
  console.log(header.slice(0, 40).padEnd(40), JSON.stringify(requested), lang, direction(lang));
}
Result
ar-EG,ar;Q=0.9                           ["ar-EG","ar"] ar rtl
es;Q=0.1,en;q=0.9                        ["en","es"] en ltr
fr-FR,fr-FR,fr-FR,fr-FR,fr-FR,fr-FR,fr-F ["fr-FR","es"] es ltr
en_US, *, <script>, fr;q=x, pt-PT;q=0.2  ["pt-PT"] pt-BR ltr

Sorting, searching and word breaks per locale

The same list sorts three ways in three languages, and searching for "malmo" should find Malmö — Collator basics are on the Strings sheet, this is what changes per locale.

const cities = ["Zürich", "Örebro", "Aarhus", "Ängelholm", "Zaragoza", "Ølstykke", "Odense"];

for (const locale of ["de", "sv", "da"]) {               // Danish sorts "Aa" as Å, after Ø
  console.log(locale, [...cities].sort(new Intl.Collator(locale).compare).join(", "));
}

// search: base sensitivity ignores case and accents; match whole words found by the segmenter
const loose = new Intl.Collator("en", { usage: "search", sensitivity: "base" });
const words = new Intl.Segmenter("en", { granularity: "word" });
function mentions(text: string, query: string): boolean {
  return Array.from(words.segment(text)).some((s) => s.isWordLike && loose.compare(s.segment, query) === 0);
}
console.log(mentions("Ships from Malmö and Zürich", "malmo"), mentions("Ships from Malmö", "malm"));

// Japanese and Thai have no spaces between words: split(" ") finds one "word"
const japanese = new Intl.Segmenter("ja", { granularity: "word" });
const phrase = "東京駅で待ち合わせ";
const jaWords = Array.from(japanese.segment(phrase)).filter((s) => s.isWordLike).map((s) => s.segment);
console.log(phrase.split(" ").length, jaWords.join(" | "));

Pseudo-localization and testing a locale

Run the app in a fake locale before translators start: unbracketed text is hard-coded, clipped brackets are layouts that cannot grow.

const accents: Record<string, string> = {
  a: "á", e: "é", i: "ï", o: "ö", u: "ü", c: "ç", n: "ñ", A: "Å", C: "Ç", E: "É", O: "Ø", S: "Š",
};

// accent every letter, keep {placeholders} intact, and grow ~35% — German and Finnish run long
function pseudo(message: string): string {
  const body = message
    .split(/(\{\w+\})/)
    .map((part) => (part.startsWith("{") ? part : Array.from(part, (c) => accents[c] ?? c).join("")))
    .join("");
  return `[${body}${"~".repeat(Math.ceil(message.length * 0.35))}]`;
}

const en = {
  "cart.checkout": "Checkout", "cart.greeting": "Welcome back, {name}!", "order.eta": "Arrives {date}",
};
console.log(Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(en).map(([key, text]) => [key, pseudo(text)])));

// testing a locale: every catalog has every key, and no message lost a placeholder
const es: Record<string, string> = { "cart.checkout": "Pagar", "cart.greeting": "¡Hola de nuevo!" };
const placeholders = (s: string) => (s.match(/\{\w+\}/g) ?? []).sort().join();
for (const [key, source] of Object.entries(en)) {
  const translated = es[key];
  if (translated === undefined) console.log(`es: missing ${key}`);
  else if (placeholders(translated) !== placeholders(source)) {
    console.log(`es: ${key} lost ${placeholders(source)}`);
  }
}
Result
{
  'cart.checkout': '[Çhéçköüt~~~]',
  'cart.greeting': '[Wélçömé báçk, {name}!~~~~~~~~]',
  'order.eta': '[Årrïvés {date}~~~~~]'
}
es: cart.greeting lost {name}
es: missing order.eta

Rules and pitfalls

Most localization bugs are a string built in code or a format someone typed by hand.

  • Concatenating fragments: "Ordered by " + name + " on " + date — word order differs per language. Translate the whole sentence with placeholders.
  • Hard-coded formats: ${m}/${d}/${y}, toFixed(2) + " €", "s" appended for plurals. Use Intl and plural rules.
  • toLocaleString() with no arguments: the output follows the server's or the test machine's locale and time zone.
  • Calling Intl constructors on raw header or query values: they throw RangeError on malformed tags. Validate first, as in the negotiation card.
  • Pass the locale and timeZone to every formatter; in tests, pin them the same way (Playwright: locale and timezoneId options).
  • Lay out with logical CSS (margin-inline-start, padding-inline, text-align: start) and flip directional icons under [dir=rtl]; wrap user-supplied names in <bdi>.
  • Ship a pseudo-locale in development builds and run the UI tests in it: hard-coded text and clipped layouts show up before translation does.
  • Intl output contains invisible no-break and thin spaces (U+00A0, U+202F, U+2009): compare formatted strings with the formatter's own output, not a typed literal.
  • Node ships full ICU by default since version 13; a browser's data follows its version. A Node built with small-icu formats most locales as English.

UI & End-to-End Testing

Component tests that act like a user, Playwright journeys through the real app, role-based selectors, no sleeps, isolated network and state — and a suite that does not flake.

The testing trophy, by tool

Most confidence per second comes from component tests that render and interact; keep a few end-to-end journeys for what only the real app proves.

LayerToolUse it forWatch out
statictsc --noEmit, ESLint (eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y, eslint-plugin-testing-library)typos, wrong props, missing labelsproves nothing about behaviour

A component test that renders, interacts, asserts

Render the component, act through user-event — real key presses and clicks, with the disabled and visibility checks a user meets — and assert on text and roles, never on state or props.

import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { afterEach, mock, test } from "node:test";
import { useState, type FormEvent } from "react";
import { JSDOM } from "jsdom";

const { window } = new JSDOM("<!doctype html><body></body>");   // Testing Library needs a document first
Object.assign(globalThis, { window, document: window.document, IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT: true });
const { render, screen, cleanup } = await import("@testing-library/react");
const { userEvent } = await import("@testing-library/user-event");
afterEach(cleanup);

function TodoList({ save }: { save: (title: string) => Promise<void> }) {
  const [todos, setTodos] = useState<string[]>([]);
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState("");
  const [status, setStatus] = useState("");
  async function add(event: FormEvent) {
    event.preventDefault();
    setTodos([...todos, draft]);
    setDraft("");
    await save(draft);
    setStatus(`Saved "${draft}"`);
  }
  return (
    <form onSubmit={add}>
      <label htmlFor="new-todo">New to-do</label>
      <input id="new-todo" value={draft} onChange={(e) => setDraft(e.target.value)} />
      <button type="submit" disabled={!draft.trim()}>Add</button>
      <ul aria-label="To-dos">{todos.map((t) => <li key={t}>{t}</li>)}</ul>
      <p role="status">{status}</p>
    </form>
  );
}

test("adds a to-do and confirms it was saved", async () => {
  const user = userEvent.setup();
  const save = mock.fn(async (_title: string) => {});
  render(<TodoList save={save} />);
  await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Add" }));   // disabled: user-event adds nothing
  await user.type(screen.getByRole("textbox", { name: "New to-do" }), "Buy milk{Enter}");
  assert.deepEqual(screen.getAllByRole("listitem").map((li) => li.textContent), ["Buy milk"]);
  await screen.findByText('Saved "Buy milk"', { selector: "[role=status]" });   // retries: no sleep
  assert.deepEqual(save.mock.calls.map((c) => c.arguments), [["Buy milk"]]);
});
Result

✔ adds a to-do and confirms it was saved, then tests 1, pass 1, fail 0, and the process exits 0 (the timings vary).

Setup
  1. A React project: npm create vite@latest app -- --template react-ts
  2. npm i -D @testing-library/react @testing-library/dom @testing-library/user-event jsdom tsx (Vitest users: environment: "jsdom" replaces the three setup lines)
  3. Put a tsconfig.json with "compilerOptions": { "jsx": "react-jsx" } next to the file (tsx takes JSX settings only from tsconfig; without it, React is not defined), save as todo-list.test.tsx, and run npx tsx --test todo-list.test.tsx

Select by role, wait on the UI — never by layout, never by sleep

A role and accessible name survive a redesign and prove the control is usable; a web-first assertion retries until the UI is right or times out.

Layout selectors and sleeps
import { test, expect } from "@playwright/test";

test("adds a to-do", async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto("/");
  await page.locator("#app > form > input.form-control").fill("Buy milk");
  await page.locator("form .btn.btn-primary").click();
  await page.waitForTimeout(2000);                   // too long on a fast run, too short on CI
  const count = await page.locator("ul > li.todo-item").count();   // read once, never retried
  expect(count).toBe(1);
});
Roles, names and web-first assertions
import { test, expect } from "@playwright/test";

test("adds a to-do", async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto("/");
  await page.getByRole("textbox", { name: "New to-do" }).fill("Buy milk");
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Add" }).click();   // waits until visible, enabled, stable
  const todos = page.getByRole("list", { name: "To-dos" }).getByRole("listitem");
  await expect(todos).toHaveText(["Buy milk"]);              // retries until true or timeout
  await expect(page.getByRole("status")).toHaveText('Saved "Buy milk"');
});
Result

Both type-check; the first passes or fails depending on machine speed and markup, the second waits exactly as long as the app needs and survives a restyle.

Setup

  2. Set use: { baseURL: "http://localhost:5173" } and a webServer entry in playwright.config.ts so the app starts with the tests
  3. Save under tests/ as todos.spec.ts and run npx playwright test

An end-to-end journey with Playwright

One test per critical journey, through the real UI and the real server — each test with its own account, so parallel workers never share or wipe each other's data.

import { test, expect } from "@playwright/test";

test.beforeEach(async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
  // a test-build-only endpoint creates a fresh, empty account and answers with its session cookie;
  // page.request shares the page's cookie jar, so the browser is signed in as that account
  // unique per run too: testId and workerIndex repeat on every run and on every developer's machine
  const email = `e2e-${testInfo.workerIndex}-${crypto.randomUUID()}@example.test`;
  const created = await page.request.post("/api/test/users", { data: { email } });
  expect(created.ok()).toBe(true);
  await page.goto("/");
});

test("adds, completes and clears a to-do", async ({ page }) => {
  const newTodo = page.getByRole("textbox", { name: "New to-do" });
  const todos = page.getByRole("list", { name: "To-dos" }).getByRole("listitem");

  await newTodo.fill("Buy milk");
  await newTodo.press("Enter");
  await newTodo.fill("Book dentist");
  await newTodo.press("Enter");
  await expect(todos).toHaveText(["Buy milk", "Book dentist"]);

  await todos.filter({ hasText: "Buy milk" }).getByRole("checkbox").check();
  await expect(page.getByRole("status")).toHaveText("1 left");

  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Clear completed" }).click();
  await expect(todos).toHaveText(["Book dentist"]);

  await page.reload();                                             // persisted, not just rendered
  await expect(todos).toHaveText(["Book dentist"]);
});
Result

Playwright runs the journey in each configured browser, in parallel with other tests; a failure leaves a trace with DOM snapshots, network and console for every step (npx playwright show-trace).

Isolate the network with page.route

Stub the APIs a test is not about — errors, empty states, third parties — so the result depends on the app alone.

import { test, expect } from "@playwright/test";

test.beforeEach(async ({ context }) => {
  // analytics and other third parties are not under test: never let them slow or fail a run
  await context.route(/googletagmanager|segment\.io/, (route) => route.abort());
});

test("shows the empty state", async ({ page }) => {
  await page.route("**/api/todos", (route) => route.fulfill({ json: [] }));
  await page.goto("/");
  await expect(page.getByText("Nothing to do — add your first to-do")).toBeVisible();
});

test("explains a server error and recovers on retry", async ({ page }) => {
  let calls = 0;
  await page.route("**/api/todos", async (route) => {
    calls += 1;
    if (calls === 1) return route.fulfill({ status: 503, json: { error: "unavailable" } });
    return route.fulfill({ json: [{ id: 1, title: "Buy milk", done: false }] });
  });
  await page.goto("/");
  await expect(page.getByRole("alert")).toHaveText("Could not load your to-dos.");
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Try again" }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole("listitem")).toHaveText(["Buy milk"]);
});
Result

Both tests pass without a backend for /api/todos; every analytics request is aborted.

MSW for component tests

Mock at the network layer, not the fetch function: the component's real data code runs, and the same handlers serve Storybook and dev.

import { http, HttpResponse } from "msw";
import { setupServer } from "msw/node";
import { afterAll, afterEach, beforeAll, expect, test } from "vitest";
import { cleanup, render, screen } from "@testing-library/react";
import { TodoPage } from "./TodoPage";

const api = "https://api.example.com/todos";
const server = setupServer(
  http.get(api, () => HttpResponse.json([{ id: 1, title: "Buy milk", done: false }])),
);

// MSW 3 renamed onUnhandledRequest to onUnhandledFrame: "error" halts any request without a handler
beforeAll(() => server.listen({ onUnhandledFrame: "error" }));
afterEach(() => {
  server.resetHandlers();                    // per-test overrides never leak
  cleanup();                                 // Vitest without globals: RTL cannot register this itself
});
afterAll(() => server.close());

test("lists the saved to-dos", async () => {
  render(<TodoPage />);
  expect((await screen.findByRole("listitem")).textContent).toBe("Buy milk");
});

test("explains a server error", async () => {
  server.use(http.get(api, () => new HttpResponse(null, { status: 503 })));
  render(<TodoPage />);
  expect((await screen.findByRole("alert")).textContent).toBe("Could not load your to-dos.");
});
Result

Both tests pass with no server running; a request to a URL without a handler is halted with an error instead of reaching the network.

Page objects as fixtures

Put locators and multi-step actions in one class, hand it to tests as a fixture — tests then read as the journey, and a markup change is fixed once.

import { test as base, expect, type Locator, type Page } from "@playwright/test";

class TodoPage {
  readonly newTodo: Locator;
  readonly items: Locator;
  readonly remaining: Locator;

  constructor(page: Page) {
    this.newTodo = page.getByRole("textbox", { name: "New to-do" });
    this.items = page.getByRole("list", { name: "To-dos" }).getByRole("listitem");
    this.remaining = page.getByRole("status");
  }
  async add(...titles: string[]): Promise<void> {
    for (const title of titles) {
      await this.newTodo.fill(title);
      await this.newTodo.press("Enter");
    }
  }
  async complete(title: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.items.filter({ hasText: title }).getByRole("checkbox").check();
  }
}

const test = base.extend<{ todoPage: TodoPage }>({
  todoPage: async ({ page }, use) => {
    await page.goto("/");
    await use(new TodoPage(page));             // setup above, teardown below this line
  },
});

test("counts what is left", async ({ todoPage }) => {
  await todoPage.add("Buy milk", "Book dentist");
  await todoPage.complete("Buy milk");
  await expect(todoPage.remaining).toHaveText("1 left");
});
Result

The test receives a ready TodoPage on a loaded page; assertions stay in the test, locators stay in the class.

Log in once, reuse the storage state

A setup project logs in through the UI once and saves cookies and local storage; every other test starts already signed in.

import { test as setup, expect } from "@playwright/test";

const authFile = "playwright/.auth/user.json";

setup("sign in as the test user", async ({ page }) => {
  const email = process.env.E2E_USER_EMAIL;
  const password = process.env.E2E_USER_PASSWORD;   // a test account's secret, from CI — never committed
  if (!email || !password) throw new Error("Set E2E_USER_EMAIL and E2E_USER_PASSWORD");

  await page.goto("/login");
  await page.getByRole("textbox", { name: "Email" }).fill(email);
  await page.getByLabel("Password").fill(password);
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Sign in" }).click();

  // wait for proof that the session is really set before saving it
  await expect(page.getByRole("button", { name: "Account menu" })).toBeVisible();
  await page.context().storageState({ path: authFile });
});
Result

The setup project runs first and writes playwright/.auth/user.json; tests in the chromium project open already signed in. Tests that change account data should use their own account, as in the journey card.

The same flow in Cypress

Cypress commands are queued chains, not promises: never await them, and let should retry the assertion.

describe("to-dos", () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    // cy.session caches the cookies and storage of this login across the tests of a spec
    cy.session("ada", () => {
      cy.request("POST", "/api/test/login", { email: "ada@example.com" });
    });
    cy.intercept("GET", "/api/todos", { fixture: "todos.json" }).as("todos");
    cy.visit("/");
    cy.wait("@todos");
  });

  it("adds a to-do", () => {
    cy.findByRole("textbox", { name: "New to-do" }).type("Buy milk{enter}");
    cy.findByRole("list", { name: "To-dos" })
      .findAllByRole("listitem")
      .should("have.length", 3)
      .last()
      .should("have.text", "Buy milk");
    cy.findByRole("status").should("have.text", "3 left");
  });
});
Result

The test logs in once per spec run, serves /api/todos from cypress/fixtures/todos.json (two items), and passes.

The flake checklist

A test that fails one run in fifty is a test nobody believes — fix the cause, do not add retries.

  • Fixed sleeps (waitForTimeout, cy.wait(2000), setTimeout in a test). Wait for something the user can see: web-first assertions, findBy*.
  • Reading a value once and asserting on it (expect(await locator.count()).toBe(1)) — use await expect(locator).toHaveCount(1), which retries.
  • Shared accounts and global resets with fullyParallel: true: workers wipe each other's data. Give each test its own account or records, and run it alone with --repeat-each.
  • Isolate what is not under test: stub third parties and error paths (page.route, MSW), pin the clock (page.clock.install()), locale and timezoneId.
  • Select by role, label or text; a data-testid only where no accessible name exists. Never CSS paths or nth-child.
  • Record a trace on the first retry (trace: "on-first-retry") and read it before touching the test; run new tests with --repeat-each=20 before merging.
  • Retries in CI (retries: 2) hide flakes — keep them, but report flaky tests and treat each one as a bug.

Read and write a small text file

Whole-file reads are right for small files; say the encoding or you get a Buffer.

import { mkdtemp, readFile, rm, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { join } from "node:path";

const dir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "demo-"));
const file = join(dir, "notes.txt");
await writeFile(file, "first line\nsecond line\n", "utf8");
const text = await readFile(file, "utf8");
console.log(text.split("\n").filter(Boolean).length, "lines");
await rm(dir, { recursive: true });
Result
2 lines

Writing atomically

Write a temporary file in the same directory, flush it, then rename over the target: readers see the old file or the new one, never half.

import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { mkdtemp, open, readFile, rename, rm } from "node:fs/promises";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { basename, dirname, join } from "node:path";

async function writeFileAtomic(path: string, data: string): Promise<void> {
  const temp = join(dirname(path), `.${basename(path)}.${randomUUID()}.tmp`);   // same file system, unique per call
  const handle = await open(temp, "wx");     // exclusive: never truncates another writer's file
  try {
    await handle.writeFile(data, "utf8");
    await handle.sync();                     // on the device before the rename publishes it
  } finally {
    await handle.close();
  }
  await rename(temp, path);                  // atomic replace on POSIX file systems
}

const dir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "atomic-"));
const settings = join(dir, "settings.json");
await writeFileAtomic(settings, JSON.stringify({ theme: "dark" }));
await writeFileAtomic(settings, JSON.stringify({ theme: "light" }));
console.log(JSON.parse(await readFile(settings, "utf8")).theme);
await rm(dir, { recursive: true });
Result
light

Streaming a large file line by line

readline over a read stream holds one line at a time, whatever the file size.

import { createReadStream } from "node:fs";
import { mkdtemp, rm, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { join } from "node:path";
import { createInterface } from "node:readline";

const dir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "lines-"));
const log = join(dir, "app.log");
await writeFile(log, Array.from({ length: 10_000 }, (_, i) => `${i % 10 === 0 ? "ERROR" : "INFO"} event ${i}`).join("\n"));

let errors = 0;
const lines = createInterface({ input: createReadStream(log, "utf8"), crlfDelay: Infinity });
for await (const line of lines) {
  if (line.startsWith("ERROR")) errors++;
}
console.log(errors, "errors");
await rm(dir, { recursive: true });
Result
1000 errors

Pipelines and backpressure

pipeline pauses a fast reader for a slow writer, and destroys every stream if one fails.

import { createReadStream, createWriteStream } from "node:fs";
import { mkdtemp, rm, stat, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { join } from "node:path";
import { pipeline } from "node:stream/promises";
import { createGzip } from "node:zlib";

const dir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "gzip-"));
const src = join(dir, "data.csv");
await writeFile(src, "id,value\n".repeat(50_000));
await pipeline(createReadStream(src), createGzip(), createWriteStream(`${src}.gz`));
const [before, after] = await Promise.all([stat(src), stat(`${src}.gz`)]);
console.log(after.size * 100 < before.size ? "compressed over 100x" : "barely compressed");
await rm(dir, { recursive: true });
Result
compressed over 100x

An append-only journal

One JSON object per line (JSON Lines) — appends never rewrite what is already there.

import { appendFile, mkdtemp, readFile, rm } from "node:fs/promises";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { join } from "node:path";

const dir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "journal-"));
const journal = join(dir, "events.jsonl");
for (const event of ["start", "save", "stop"]) {
  await appendFile(journal, `${JSON.stringify({ event })}\n`);
}
const events = (await readFile(journal, "utf8")).trim().split("\n").map((l) => JSON.parse(l).event);
console.log(events);
await rm(dir, { recursive: true });

[ 'start', 'save', 'stop' ]

Where things belong

Node has no sandbox to choose for you — pick the folder from what the data is and how long it must live.

DataWhereSurvivesUse for

per-user app dataLinux $XDG_DATA_HOME (else ~/.local/share), macOS ~/Library/Application Support, Windows %LOCALAPPDATA% (machine-specific, may be large)yesdatabases and state the app owns; build it from os.homedir()

Paths with node:path, files as URLs

Build every path with node:path and every file URL with pathToFileURL — string concatenation breaks on separators, .. and #.

import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from "node:url";

const dataDir = path.join(tmpdir(), "orders-app");      // only computes paths: no file is created

// join normalises separators and ".."; resolve also makes the result absolute.
const report = path.join(dataDir, "exports", "2026", "..", "Q3 report #1.csv");
console.log(path.relative(dataDir, report), "|", path.parse(report).name, "|", path.extname(report));

// A name from a user or a zip entry must stay inside its folder. This check is lexical only:
// if entries can be symlinks, also compare `await realpath(target)` with `await realpath(base)`.
function safeJoin(base: string, untrusted: string): string {
  const target = path.resolve(base, untrusted);
  const rel = path.relative(base, target);
  if (rel === ".." || rel.startsWith(`..${path.sep}`) || path.isAbsolute(rel)) {
    throw new Error(`refusing a path outside ${path.basename(base)}: ${untrusted}`);
  }
  return target;
}
console.log(path.relative(dataDir, safeJoin(dataDir, "invoices/1042.pdf")));
try {
  safeJoin(dataDir, "../../etc/passwd");
} catch (err) {
  console.log((err as Error).message);
}

// "file://" + path would end the path at "#"; pathToFileURL escapes it, and round-trips.
const url = pathToFileURL(report);
console.log(url.href.split("/").at(-1), fileURLToPath(url) === report);

// Next to this module, wherever the process was started from (Node 20.11+).
const schema = fileURLToPath(new URL("./schema.json", import.meta.url));
console.log(path.dirname(schema) === import.meta.dirname);

Real durability: fsync the file and the directory

When "the power went out right after save" must be survivable — a journal, a ledger, a payment record — at a cost of milliseconds per sync, so not for every keystroke.

import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { mkdtemp, open, readdir, readFile, rename, rm } from "node:fs/promises";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { basename, dirname, join } from "node:path";

async function writeFileDurable(path: string, data: string): Promise<void> {
  const dir = dirname(path);
  const temp = join(dir, `.${basename(path)}.${randomUUID()}.tmp`);
  try {
    const file = await open(temp, "wx");
    try {
      await file.writeFile(data, "utf8");
      await file.sync();             // 1. bytes on the device (on macOS, libuv's fsync issues F_FULLFSYNC)
    } finally {
      await file.close();
    }
    await rename(temp, path);        // 2. atomic replace on POSIX; best effort on Windows (MoveFileEx)
  } catch (err) {
    await rm(temp, { force: true }); // never leave a half-written sibling behind
    throw err;
  }
  if (process.platform === "win32") return;   // Windows cannot flush a directory handle
  const folder = await open(dir, "r");
  try {
    await folder.sync();             // 3. the rename is durable only once the directory entry is flushed
  } finally {
    await folder.close();
  }
}

const dir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "ledger-"));
try {
  const ledger = join(dir, "ledger.json");
  await writeFileDurable(ledger, JSON.stringify({ balance: 120 }));
  await writeFileDurable(ledger, JSON.stringify({ balance: 95 }));
  console.log(await readFile(ledger, "utf8"), await readdir(dir));
} finally {
  await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
}
Result
{"balance":95} [ 'ledger.json' ]

Streaming a large write with backpressure

Exporting more rows than fit in memory: batch rows into ~64 KB writes, and wait for drain whenever write() returns false.

import { once } from "node:events";
import { createWriteStream } from "node:fs";
import { mkdtemp, readFile, rm } from "node:fs/promises";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { join } from "node:path";
import { finished } from "node:stream/promises";

function* orderRows(count: number): Generator<string> {
  for (let id = 1; id <= count; id++) {
    yield `${id},customer-${id % 977},${(((id * 37) % 10_000) / 100).toFixed(2)}\n`;
  }
}

async function exportCsv(path: string, rows: Iterable<string>): Promise<void> {
  const out = createWriteStream(path, { highWaterMark: 1 << 16 });
  let batch = "id,customer,total\n";
  for (const row of rows) {
    batch += row;
    if (batch.length < 1 << 16) continue;               // one syscall per ~64 KB, not per row
    if (!out.write(batch)) await once(out, "drain");    // the disk is behind: stop producing
    batch = "";
  }
  out.end(batch);
  await finished(out);                                   // resolves once flushed and closed; rejects on error
}

const dir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "export-"));
try {
  const file = join(dir, "orders.csv");
  await exportCsv(file, orderRows(200_000));
  const lines = (await readFile(file, "utf8")).trimEnd().split("\n");
  console.log(lines.length - 1, "rows;", lines[1], "...", lines.at(-1));
} finally {
  await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
}
// Ignoring write()'s false still "works" — by buffering the whole export in memory.
Result
200000 rows; 1,customer-1,0.37 ... 200000,customer-692,0.00

Algorithm — external merge sort, phase 1: sorted runs

Phase 1 of sorting a file larger than memory: sort chunks that fit and spill each one to a run file, which the k-way merge card then combines.

import { createReadStream } from "node:fs";
import { mkdtemp, readdir, readFile, rm, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { join } from "node:path";
import { createInterface } from "node:readline";

// Memory holds one chunk of lines at a time; each chunk is sorted and spilled to its own run file.
async function makeRuns(input: string, chunkLines: number, dir: string): Promise<string[]> {
  const runs: string[] = [];
  let chunk: string[] = [];
  const spill = async () => {
    const run = join(dir, `run-${runs.length}.txt`);
    await writeFile(run, `${chunk.sort().join("\n")}\n`);
    runs.push(run);
    chunk = [];
  };
  const file = createReadStream(input);
  try {
    for await (const line of createInterface({ input: file, crlfDelay: Infinity })) {
      chunk.push(line);
      if (chunk.length === chunkLines) await spill();
    }
  } finally {
    file.destroy();                                      // closed even if a spill fails (disk full)
  }
  if (chunk.length) await spill();                       // the last, shorter chunk
  return runs;
}

const dir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "sort-"));
try {
  const ids = Array.from({ length: 10_000 }, (_, i) => `ORD-${(i * 7_919) % 10_007}`);   // distinct, shuffled
  await writeFile(join(dir, "orders.txt"), `${ids.join("\n")}\n`);

  const runs = await makeRuns(join(dir, "orders.txt"), 2_500, dir);
  const first = (await readFile(runs[0]!, "utf8")).split("\n").slice(0, 3);
  console.log(runs.length, "runs:", (await readdir(dir)).filter((f) => f.startsWith("run-")).sort(), first);
  // Phase 2 merges the runs into one sorted file: the k-way merge card.
} finally {
  await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
}
Result
4 runs: [ 'run-0.txt', 'run-1.txt', 'run-2.txt', 'run-3.txt' ] [ 'ORD-0', 'ORD-1000', 'ORD-10005' ]

Algorithm — k-way merge of sorted files

Combine files that are each sorted — regional exports, or the runs of an external sort — into one sorted file with one line per file in memory, closing every file even when the write fails.

import { createReadStream, createWriteStream } from "node:fs";
import { mkdtemp, readFile, rm, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { join } from "node:path";
import { createInterface } from "node:readline";
import { pipeline } from "node:stream/promises";

// One line per file in memory. A scan is O(k) per line; a min-heap makes it O(log k) for many files.
async function* mergeSorted(files: string[]): AsyncGenerator<string> {
  const inputs = files.map((f) => createReadStream(f));
  const lines = inputs.map((input) =>
    createInterface({ input, crlfDelay: Infinity })[Symbol.asyncIterator]());
  try {
    const heads: (string | undefined)[] = await Promise.all(lines.map(async (l) => (await l.next()).value));
    for (;;) {
      let min = -1;
      for (const [i, h] of heads.entries()) {
        if (h !== undefined && (min === -1 || h < heads[min]!)) min = i;   // the same order as sort()
      }
      if (min === -1) return;
      yield `${heads[min]}\n`;
      heads[min] = (await lines[min]!.next()).value;
    }
  } finally {
    for (const input of inputs) input.destroy();          // readline's own close leaves the files open
  }
}

const dir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "merge-"));
try {
  const shards = {                                        // each regional export is already sorted
    "eu.txt": "ORD-1002\nORD-1005\n",
    "us.txt": "ORD-1001\nORD-1004\nORD-1006\n",
    "apac.txt": "ORD-1003\n",
  };
  for (const [name, body] of Object.entries(shards)) await writeFile(join(dir, name), body);

  const out = join(dir, "all.txt");
  await pipeline(mergeSorted(Object.keys(shards).map((n) => join(dir, n))), createWriteStream(out));
  console.log((await readFile(out, "utf8")).trimEnd().split("\n").join(" "));
} finally {
  await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
}
Result
ORD-1001 ORD-1002 ORD-1003 ORD-1004 ORD-1005 ORD-1006

Algorithm — an offset index for random access

Jump to line n of a huge log without reading what comes before it: index each line's byte offset once, then read by position.

import { createReadStream } from "node:fs";
import { mkdtemp, open, rm, stat, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { join } from "node:path";

// One streaming pass; the index costs 8 bytes per line, not the line itself.
async function buildIndex(file: string): Promise<number[]> {
  const offsets = [0];
  let position = 0;
  for await (const chunk of createReadStream(file, { highWaterMark: 1 << 16 }) as AsyncIterable<Buffer>) {
    for (let i = chunk.indexOf(10); i !== -1; i = chunk.indexOf(10, i + 1)) offsets.push(position + i + 1);
    position += chunk.length;
  }
  if (offsets.at(-1) === position) offsets.pop();       // a trailing newline starts no line
  return offsets;
}

// Fixed-width records need no index (offset = n × size); a sorted file can be binary-searched by seeking.
async function readLine(file: string, index: readonly number[], n: number): Promise<string> {
  const start = index[n]!;
  const end = index[n + 1] ?? (await stat(file)).size;
  const handle = await open(file, "r");
  try {
    const buffer = Buffer.alloc(end - start);
    const { bytesRead } = await handle.read(buffer, 0, buffer.length, start);   // positional: no seek
    return buffer.subarray(0, bytesRead).toString("utf8").replace(/\r?\n$/, "");
  } finally {
    await handle.close();
  }
}

const dir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "index-"));
try {
  const log = join(dir, "deliveries.log");
  const cities = ["Zürich", "São Paulo", "Kraków", "Lyon"];   // multi-byte: offsets count bytes
  const line = (i: number) => `#${i} delivered to ${cities[i % 4]}\n`;
  await writeFile(log, Array.from({ length: 50_000 }, (_, i) => line(i)).join(""));
  const index = await buildIndex(log);
  console.log(index.length, "lines");
  console.log(await readLine(log, index, 31_415), "|", await readLine(log, index, 49_999));
} finally {
  await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
}
Result

#31415 delivered to Lyon | #49999 delivered to Lyon

Algorithm — tail -n

The last n lines of a log of any size, read backwards in blocks — and the same answers as tail -n for 0, blank lines and CRLF.

import { mkdtemp, open, rm, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { join } from "node:path";

async function lastLines(file: string, count: number): Promise<string[]> {
  if (count <= 0) return [];                            // .slice(-0) would return everything
  const handle = await open(file, "r");
  try {
    let position = (await handle.stat()).size;
    const blocks: Buffer[] = [];
    let newlines = 0;
    // count + 1 newlines guarantee the first wanted line is complete (and a split UTF-8 char is not in it).
    while (position > 0 && newlines <= count) {
      const size = Math.min(1 << 16, position);
      position -= size;
      const block = Buffer.alloc(size);
      await handle.read(block, 0, size, position);
      for (const byte of block) if (byte === 10) newlines++;
      blocks.unshift(block);
    }
    const text = Buffer.concat(blocks).toString("utf8");
    if (text === "") return [];
    // Drop only the final newline: blank lines are lines. CRLF or LF.
    return text.replace(/\r?\n$/, "").split(/\r?\n/).slice(-count);
  } finally {
    await handle.close();
  }
}

const dir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "tail-"));
try {
  const log = join(dir, "access.log");
  await writeFile(log, Array.from({ length: 50_000 }, (_, i) => `GET /orders/${i} 200\r\n`).join(""));
  console.log(await lastLines(log, 2), (await lastLines(log, 0)).length);
  await writeFile(log, "started\n\nstopped\n\n");     // blank lines are lines, as in tail -n
  console.log(await lastLines(log, 2));
} finally {
  await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
}

Algorithm — dedupe and checksum

Two one-pass jobs on files of any size: count the distinct lines, and a SHA-256 for an upload or a cache key.

import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
import { createReadStream } from "node:fs";
import { mkdtemp, rm, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { join } from "node:path";
import { createInterface } from "node:readline";

// A fixed 32-byte digest instead of the line itself — worth it when lines are long.
async function distinctLines(file: string): Promise<number> {
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  for await (const line of createInterface({ input: createReadStream(file), crlfDelay: Infinity })) {
    seen.add(createHash("sha256").update(line).digest("base64"));
  }
  return seen.size;
}

// Feed the hash chunk by chunk; the file is never in memory.
async function sha256(file: string): Promise<string> {
  const hash = createHash("sha256");
  for await (const chunk of createReadStream(file)) hash.update(chunk);
  return hash.digest("hex");
}

const dir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "logs-"));
try {
  const log = join(dir, "requests.log");
  const request = (i: number) => `POST /v1/orders customer=${i % 1_000} items=${"sku-123,".repeat(20)}\n`;
  await writeFile(log, Array.from({ length: 30_000 }, (_, i) => request(i)).join(""));
  console.log(await distinctLines(log), "distinct |", (await sha256(log)).slice(0, 16));
} finally {
  await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
}

1000 distinct | e14de7737d99846c

Enumerating directories

opendir walks lazily and lets you skip a subtree, while readdir with recursive and glob are eager conveniences — and none of them promises an order, so sort.

import { glob, mkdir, mkdtemp, opendir, readdir, rm, stat, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { dirname, join, relative } from "node:path";

// Lazy: one open handle per level of depth, and node_modules is never even opened.
async function totalBytes(dir: string, skip: ReadonlySet<string>): Promise<number> {
  let total = 0;
  for await (const entry of await opendir(dir)) {        // the handle closes when the loop ends
    const full = join(dir, entry.name);
    if (entry.isDirectory() && !skip.has(entry.name)) total += await totalBytes(full, skip);
    else if (entry.isFile()) total += (await stat(full)).size;
  }
  return total;
}

const root = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "project-"));
try {
  const files = { "src/app.ts": 300, "src/data/rates.csv": 50, "reports/q3.csv": 20,
    "node_modules/big/index.js": 10_000, "node_modules/big/fixture.csv": 500 };
  for (const [file, size] of Object.entries(files)) {
    await mkdir(dirname(join(root, file)), { recursive: true });
    await writeFile(join(root, file), "x".repeat(size));
  }
  console.log(await totalBytes(root, new Set(["node_modules"])), "bytes outside node_modules");

  // Eager and recursive: fine for small trees. parentPath (Node 20.12+) is the entry's folder.
  const entries = await readdir(root, { recursive: true, withFileTypes: true });
  const paths = entries.filter((e) => e.isFile()).map((e) => relative(root, join(e.parentPath, e.name)));
  console.log(paths.sort().join(", "));

  // Pattern matching (stable since Node 22.17); exclude stops the walk from descending.
  const csvs: string[] = [];
  for await (const file of glob("**/*.csv", { cwd: root, exclude: (name) => name === "node_modules" })) {
    csvs.push(file);
  }
  console.log(csvs.sort());
} finally {
  await rm(root, { recursive: true, force: true });
}
Result

node_modules/big/fixture.csv, node_modules/big/index.js, reports/q3.csv, src/app.ts, src/data/rates.csv
[ 'reports/q3.csv', 'src/data/rates.csv' ]

Attributes and permissions

Create a secret with mode 0o600 from the first byte, mark a script executable, read size and times with stat.

import { chmod, mkdtemp, rm, stat, utimes, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { join } from "node:path";

const mode = async (file: string) => ((await stat(file)).mode & 0o777).toString(8);
const dir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "perms-"));
try {
  // Private from creation: writing first and chmod-ing after leaves a window where others can read it.
  const credentials = join(dir, "credentials.json");
  await writeFile(credentials, JSON.stringify({ apiKey: "placeholder" }), { mode: 0o600, flag: "wx" });

  // An executable script: chmod is exact (the umask only filters modes at creation).
  const deploy = join(dir, "deploy.sh");
  await writeFile(deploy, "#!/bin/sh\necho deploying\n");
  await chmod(deploy, 0o755);
  console.log(await mode(credentials), await mode(deploy));

  // Size, kind and times. lstat instead reports on a symlink itself rather than its target.
  const releasedAt = new Date("2026-11-16T09:30:00Z");
  await utimes(deploy, releasedAt, releasedAt);
  const info = await stat(deploy);
  console.log(info.size, info.isFile(), info.isDirectory(), info.mtime.toISOString());
} finally {
  await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
}
// Windows honours only the owner-write bit (read-only or not); protect secrets there with ACLs.

25 true false 2026-11-16T09:30:00.000Z

Advisory locking — one writer across processes

Two copies of a CLI or a cron job must not write the same file, so publish the lock with link() — it appears whole or not at all — and report a dead owner instead of reclaiming it, which two waiters would both do (for takeover, use SQLite or a lock library with leases).

import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { link, mkdtemp, readFile, rm, unlink, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { join } from "node:path";

async function tryLock(lockFile: string): Promise<(() => Promise<void>) | null> {   // null: busy
  const draft = `${lockFile}.${randomUUID()}`;
  await writeFile(draft, JSON.stringify({ pid: process.pid }), { flag: "wx" });
  try {
    await link(draft, lockFile);        // publishes it whole and atomically; EEXIST if it is held
    return () => unlink(lockFile);
  } catch (err) {
    if ((err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "EEXIST") return null;
    throw err;                          // EPERM (Linux) or ENOTSUP (macOS): no hard links on FAT, some shares
  } finally {
    await unlink(draft).catch(() => {});   // the lock is held either way; a crash can leave
  }                                        // *.lock.<uuid> drafts behind, and they are safe to delete
}

async function whyBusy(lockFile: string): Promise<string> {   // reports; never reclaims
  try {
    const { pid } = JSON.parse(await readFile(lockFile, "utf8")) as { pid: number };
    process.kill(pid, 0);               // signal 0 only checks that the process exists
    return "held by a running process";
  } catch (err) {
    const code = (err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code;
    if (code === "ESRCH") return "its owner has exited: check, then delete the lock by hand";
    return code === "EPERM" ? "held by another user's process" : "changing hands: retry shortly";
  }
}

const dir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "lock-"));
try {
  const lockFile = join(dir, "sync.lock");
  console.log("first:", (await tryLock(lockFile)) ? "writer" : "busy");   // keeps the lock: never released
  console.log("second:", (await tryLock(lockFile)) ? "writer" : await whyBusy(lockFile));

  const exited = spawnSync(process.execPath, ["--version"]).pid;   // a process that has already ended
  await writeFile(lockFile, JSON.stringify({ pid: exited }));       // the writer crashed holding the lock
  console.log("after a crash:", (await tryLock(lockFile)) ? "writer" : await whyBusy(lockFile));
} finally {
  await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
}
Result
first: writer
second: held by a running process
after a crash: its owner has exited: check, then delete the lock by hand

Files are blocking work: sync APIs stop the event loop

Both columns answer the same, but while readFileSync runs every other request and timer waits, whereas promise APIs run on libuv's threadpool — sync is fine only in startup code and short CLIs.

Blocks every client while it reads
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { mkdtemp, rm, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { createServer } from "node:http";
import { type AddressInfo } from "node:net";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { join } from "node:path";

const dir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "serve-"));
const prices = join(dir, "prices.json");
const server = createServer((_req, res) => {
  const body = readFileSync(prices, "utf8");          // the whole process stops here
  res.writeHead(200, { "content-type": "application/json" }).end(body);
});
try {
  await writeFile(prices, JSON.stringify({ sku: "A-1", cents: 1299 }));
  await new Promise<void>((ready) => server.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", ready));
  const { port } = server.address() as AddressInfo;
  const res = await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${port}/prices`);
  console.log(res.status, await res.text());
} finally {
  server.close();
  await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
}
Waits without blocking
import { mkdtemp, readFile, rm, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { createServer } from "node:http";
import { type AddressInfo } from "node:net";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { join } from "node:path";

const dir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "serve-"));
const prices = join(dir, "prices.json");
// The read runs on libuv's threadpool (4 threads by default, UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE),
// shared with dns.lookup, zlib and crypto — thousands of parallel reads queue there.
const server = createServer(async (_req, res) => {
  const body = await readFile(prices, "utf8");        // other requests run meanwhile
  res.writeHead(200, { "content-type": "application/json" }).end(body);
});
try {
  await writeFile(prices, JSON.stringify({ sku: "A-1", cents: 1299 }));
  await new Promise<void>((ready) => server.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", ready));
  const { port } = server.address() as AddressInfo;
  const res = await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${port}/prices`);
  console.log(res.status, await res.text());
} finally {
  server.close();
  await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
}
Result
200 {"sku":"A-1","cents":1299}

Error handling by errno code

Just try the operation and branch on err.code — checking with existsSync first is a race whose answer is stale.

CodeMeansTypical causeHandle it by
ENOENTno such file or directoryfirst run, a missing config, a missing parent foldera default value, or mkdir(dir, { recursive: true }) first
EEXISTalready existsopen(path, "wx"), link, mkdir without recursivesomeone else created it first: treat it as busy, or as already done
EACCES / EPERMpermission deniedwrong owner or mode; on Windows also a file another process holds openreport the path; on Windows retry a rename briefly
EISDIR / ENOTDIRwrong kind of entryreading a folder, or a file in the middle of a pathvalidate user-supplied paths
ENOTEMPTYdirectory not emptyrmdir, or rename onto a non-empty folderdecide whether its contents may go; only then rm(dir, { recursive: true })
EXDEVcross-device linkrename from os.tmpdir() to another volumeput the temp file next to the target; or copy, then unlink
EMFILE / ENFILEtoo many open filesPromise.all over thousands of opens, leaked handleslimit concurrency; close handles in finally
ENOSPC / EDQUOTno space / over quotadisk full in the middle of a writekeep the old file (atomic write), surface the error
EBUSYresource busyWindows: an antivirus or editor holds the fileretry with backoff
EROFSread-only file systema container's read-only rootwrite to the configured data volume or os.tmpdir()

Testing file code in a temp directory

A fresh mkdtemp folder per test, removed whatever happens — and test the missing-file and corrupt-file paths, not only the happy one.

import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { mkdtemp, readdir, readFile, rename, rm, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { join } from "node:path";
import { afterEach, beforeEach, test } from "node:test";

type Settings = { theme: string };
const defaults: Settings = { theme: "light" };

// Under test: a missing file is a normal first run; anything else is a real error.
async function loadSettings(file: string): Promise<Settings> {
  try {
    return { ...defaults, ...JSON.parse(await readFile(file, "utf8")) };
  } catch (err) {
    if ((err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT") return defaults;
    throw err;
  }
}

async function saveSettings(file: string, settings: Settings): Promise<void> {
  const temp = `${file}.${randomUUID()}.tmp`;           // unique: two saves never share a temp file
  await writeFile(temp, JSON.stringify(settings), { flag: "wx" });
  await rename(temp, file);
}

// One folder per test: no test sees another's files, even when `node --test` runs files in parallel.
let dir = "";
beforeEach(async () => {
  dir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "settings-test-"));
});
afterEach(() => rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }));

test("a missing file means defaults", async () => {
  assert.deepEqual(await loadSettings(join(dir, "settings.json")), defaults);
});

test("a corrupt file is an error, not a silent reset", async () => {
  await writeFile(join(dir, "settings.json"), "{ not json");
  await assert.rejects(loadSettings(join(dir, "settings.json")), SyntaxError);
});

test("saving leaves no temporary file behind", async () => {
  await saveSettings(join(dir, "settings.json"), { theme: "dark" });
  assert.deepEqual(await readdir(dir), ["settings.json"]);
  assert.equal((await loadSettings(join(dir, "settings.json"))).theme, "dark");
});
Result

All three tests pass — ✔ a missing file means defaults, ✔ a corrupt file is an error, not a silent reset, ✔ saving leaves no temporary file behind, then tests 3, pass 3, fail 0 — and the process exits 0 (the timings vary).

  3. Optional type-check: npm i -D typescript @types/node, then npx tsc --noEmit --strict --target esnext --module nodenext main.mts

Rules that prevent data loss

Most file bugs are about the moment between two writes.

  • Replace a file by writing a temporary sibling and rename-ing it; never truncate the original first.
  • await every write and close handles in finally; a crash between writes is the case to design for.
  • readFileSync on a request path blocks every other client of the process.
  • On Windows rename over an open file can fail with EPERM/EBUSY — retry, or keep readers short-lived.
  • fs.watch events are hints, not a log: re-read the file instead of trusting the event payload.

Framework-free state with EventTarget, rendering from state, cancelling superseded requests, persisting preferences.

  • a browser page (the DOM)

Sources: EventTarget — MDN · Using the Fetch API — MDN

A store with EventTarget

One owner of the state, replaced (never mutated) on every update, and a change event to re-render from. EventTarget exists in Node too, so this one runs there.

type State = { items: string[]; filter: string };

class Store extends EventTarget {
  #state: State = { items: [], filter: "" };
  get state(): Readonly<State> {
    return this.#state;
  }
  update(change: Partial<State>) {
    this.#state = { ...this.#state, ...change };   // a new object: `old !== new` detects change
    this.dispatchEvent(new Event("change"));
  }
}

const store = new Store();
store.addEventListener("change", () => {
  const { items, filter } = store.state;
  console.log(items.filter((i) => i.includes(filter)).join(", ") || "(none)");
});
store.update({ items: ["apples", "pears", "plums"] });
store.update({ filter: "um" });
store.update({ filter: "x" });
Result
apples, pears, plums
plums
(none)
Setup
  1. Node.js 22.18 or later (it runs .mts files directly by stripping the types), or any modern browser
  2. Save as main.mts and run node main.mts
  3. Optional type-check: npm i -D typescript @types/node, then npx tsc --noEmit --strict --target esnext --module nodenext main.mts

Ran with Node 24.16.0, TypeScript 5.9.3 on 2026-11-11: the output matched the result shown.

  • browser
  • node
  • typescript >=5.0
  • node >=22.18

Render from state

Rebuild the list from data on every change; textContent, never innerHTML, for anything a user typed.

const list = document.querySelector<HTMLUListElement>("#todos")!;
const input = document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>("#filter")!;
const todos = ["Write tests", "Ship it", "Write docs"];

function render(filter: string) {
  const shown = todos.filter((t) => t.toLowerCase().includes(filter.toLowerCase()));
  list.replaceChildren(...shown.map((t) => Object.assign(document.createElement("li"), { textContent: t })));
}
input.addEventListener("input", () => render(input.value));
render("");
Result

The list shows all three to-dos; typing write leaves Write tests and Write docs.

Setup
  1. A page containing <input id="filter"> and <ul id="todos"></ul>
  2. Compile with tsc (lib including DOM) or a bundler, and load the output with <script type="module">

Compiled with TypeScript 5.9.3 (lib DOM) on 2026-11-11; not run here — running it needs a browser page with the elements named in the setup.

Sources: Element.replaceChildren — MDN

Cancel superseded requests

Each keystroke aborts the previous search, so a slow old response can never overwrite a newer one.

let inFlight: AbortController | undefined;

async function search(query: string): Promise<string[]> {
  inFlight?.abort();                         // supersede the previous request
  const controller = new AbortController();
  inFlight = controller;
  const response = await fetch(`/api/search?q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}`, {
    signal: AbortSignal.any([controller.signal, AbortSignal.timeout(5_000)]),
  });
  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${response.status}`);
  return (await response.json()) as string[];
}

const box = document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>("#search")!;
box.addEventListener("input", async () => {
  try {
    console.log(await search(box.value));
  } catch (e) {
    if (e instanceof DOMException && e.name === "AbortError") return;   // superseded, not a failure
    throw e;
  }
});
Result

Only the response to the latest input is logged; earlier requests show as cancelled in the network panel.

Setup
  1. A page containing <input id="search">, served by an origin with a /api/search?q= endpoint returning a JSON array of strings
  2. Compile with tsc (lib including DOM) or a bundler, and load the output with <script type="module">

Compiled with TypeScript 5.9.3 (lib DOM) on 2026-11-11; not run here — running it needs a browser page served with a /api/search endpoint.

Sources: AbortSignal.any — MDN

Persist preferences safely

Storage can be disabled, full or hold an old shape — read defensively and version the key.

type Prefs = { theme: "light" | "dark" };
const KEY = "prefs:v1";
const DEFAULTS: Prefs = { theme: "light" };

function loadPrefs(): Prefs {
  try {
    const parsed: unknown = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY) ?? "null");
    return typeof parsed === "object" && parsed !== null && "theme" in parsed && (parsed.theme === "light" || parsed.theme === "dark")
      ? { theme: parsed.theme }
      : DEFAULTS;
  } catch {
    return DEFAULTS;                         // private mode, quota, corrupt JSON
  }
}

function savePrefs(prefs: Prefs): void {
  try {
    localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(prefs));
  } catch {
    // keep working without persistence
  }
}

const prefs = loadPrefs();
document.documentElement.dataset.theme = prefs.theme;
savePrefs({ theme: prefs.theme === "light" ? "dark" : "light" });
Result

The page takes the stored theme (light on first load) and the next load starts in the other one.

Setup
  1. A page containing <input id="filter"> and <ul id="todos"></ul>
  2. Compile with tsc (lib including DOM) or a bundler, and load the output with <script type="module">

Rules

What UI frameworks automate, done by hand.

  • One owner per piece of state; everything else derives from it on change.
  • Abort what the user has moved on from — requests, timers, listeners ({ signal } on addEventListener).
  • innerHTML with data: an injection hole. Build nodes, set textContent.
  • React, Vue and Svelte own this layer in real apps; these patterns are what they do underneath.

Coverage against the Swift Catalog

Every Swift topic, and what this catalog has for it — an equivalent, a partial counterpart, or the reason there is none.

How to read the matrix

Nothing here is a translation made to fill a gap.

  • equivalent — a sheet here covers the same concept and shares its concept id, so the language selector lands on it from the Swift sheet.
  • partial — a sheet here covers part of it under its own concept id, so the selector does not land on it: the Here column names it and the reason says what is missing.
  • no counterpart — nothing here; the reason says whether the topic does not exist in this language or is simply not written yet.
